chapters.arabic_text:
في إثبات تلك الأحكام، ويجري فيها القياس.
فما سبيل الخروج عن المطالبة دون إبداء المناسبة فيها؟ [أو ما سبيل إبداء
المناسبة فيها؟، أو] ما وجه الافتقار إلى المناسبة في الآمثلة السابقة، [إن
لم نفتقر إليها في هذه الأمثلة]؟
فالجواب: أن هذه الأمثلة اختلف الأصوليون في تسميتها: فمنهم من عبر عنها:
بأنها في معنى الأصل. وهذا عندنا كلام مجمل. والوجه: تسميتها قياسا، ولكن
ليس من قبيل الأمثلة السابقة. فإن القائس- في مثل هذه الأمثلة- لا يجعل
السبب المؤثر في حكم [مؤثرا في حكم] آخر،  حتى يطالب بإثبات المجانسة بين
الحكمين، بالاستواء في المناسبة. ولكنه يجعل السبب مؤثرا في عين الحكم الذي
ظهر أثره فيه، ولكن في محل آخر غير منصوص عليه إذ [قد] ظهر تأثير اللمس
والمس وخروج الخارج، في إيجاب الوضوء؛ وهو يجعلها مؤثرة في إيجاب الوضوء.
PageV01P129
نعم، لو قال [قائل]: هذه الأسباب إذا نقضت الطهارة، ينبغي أن تنقض الصوم-
لكان هذا وزان الأمثلة السابقة، ولقيل له: لم قلت: إذا ظهر تأثيره في نقض
الطهارة ينبغي أن يظهر في نقض الصوم؟ ويضطر إلى إبداء المجانسة بالاستواء
في المناسبة.
[نعم: نرى] أن يلقب هذا القياس بتنقيح مناط الحكم ومتعلقه. وسنذكر أمثلة
هذا الجنس في موضعه.
وقد سمى فريق من الأصوليين هذا الجنس: دلالة الخطاب. وسماه آخرون: ما في
معنى الأصل. وحاصل ذلك يرجع إلى تنقيح متعلق الحكم ومناطه، بإلغاء ما اقترن
[به] وفاقا غير مقصود باضافة الحكم إليه. فإن قوله: «[من] مس ذكره
فليتوضأ»؛ إضافة الوضوء إلى مس الذكر لا باعتبار أنه ذكره؛ ولكن جرى ذكر
الإضافة إليه وفاقا، لأنه الغالب في المس؛ إذ يبعد أن يمس الإنسان ذكر غيره.
وكذلك قوله عليه السلام: «من أعتق شركا له في عبد» [الحديث].
PageV01P130
فإعتاق البعض سبب السراية [لإعتاق كل العبد]؛ ولكن جرى ذكر العبد وفاقا:
لأنه السابق إلى اللسان في العادة. فهو- بحكم العادة- كناية عن الرقيق.
وكان كقوله عليه السلام: «أيما رجل مات أو أفلس فصاحب المتاع أحق
بمتاعه». والمرأة ملحقة بالرجل، ولكن جرى ذكر الرجل وفاقا: لأنه السابق إلى
اللسان، فهو- بحكم العادة- كناية عن الإنسان في هذا المقام.
وكذلك لو قال لزوجته: أنت طالق يوم يقدم زيد، فقدم ليلا- طلقت عند أكثر
الفقهاء، لأن اليوم في هذا المقام- بحكم العرف- كناية عن الوقت، فإنه
السابق إلى اللسان.
PageV01P131
وكذلك قال رسول الله- صلى الله عليه وسلم- «لا يبلون أحدكم في الماء
الراكد» يتضمن تحريم صب البول من الكوز في الماء؛ لأن المفهوم المنع من
تنجيس الماء بإلقاء النجاسة فيه؛ ولكن الإنسان بطبعه ممتنع من إلقاء
النجاسات في الماء من غير غرض؛ وإنما يتفق منه  البول في الماء؛ فجرى تخصيصه
وفاقا بحكم العادة.
وهذه أمور تعرف من دلالة الخطاب، وسياق الكلام، وقرينه الحال. فنتجاسر
على الإلحاق ونتقصى عن المطالبة في هذا الجنس من الإلحاق، بهذا [24 - أ]
الفن في الكلام.
والجواب الآخر: أن هذا الجنس- أيضا- غير خارج عن فهم نوع من المعنى. فإن
المس نوع هتك: إذ هو مقدمة الإمذاء؛ فإنه يحرك الآلة، ويبعث الشهوة، ويذكر
الوقاع؛ فيخرج المذي: فينتقض الوضوء، لكونه سبب خروج المذي وإن لم يخرج.
وكذلك: لمس النساء سبب الإمذاء، فينتقض الوضوء وإن لم يمذ.
PageV01P132
كما كان النوم سبب خروج الريح، فكان حدثا وإن لم يخرج. وكذلك: التقاء
الخانين سبب خروج المني، فجعل جنابة وإن لم يتحقق.
وخروج النجاسة- على الجملة- يناسب الاشتغال بالتطهير في محل النجاسة، وفي
جميع البدن. ولكن حط استيعاب للعسر، واقتصر على الأعضاء الظاهرة في الغالب.
فهذه المعاني تفهم من هذه الأسباب في التخصيص، وفي التعدية: إما بنفسها،
وإما بكونها قرينة معينة في فهم مناط الحكم من جهة المذكور، ومنبهة على
إلغاء ما لا مدخل له في هذا النوع من التأثير.
فهذا طريق تقرير هذا الفن، وقد سمينا هذه الأجوبة: تنبيها، وهي- على
التحقيق- خيال في مقابلة خيال؛ وهو: سياق نوع من الجدال، وتمهيد طريق إلى
التخييل والاحتيال.
وإنما الكشف الشافي ما نذكره الآن، وهو [أن] قول القائل: إذا ظهر تأثير
العلة في حكم، فلم ينبغي أن يؤثر في جنس آخر من الحكم؟ إن كان محل التعدية
جنسا آخر. وإن كان عين الحكم أو مثله، فكيف تتصور- مع تسليم كونه مؤثرا-
المنازعة في الحكم مع وجود المؤثر فيه؟.
وهذا خيال لا طائل وراءه: فإن العلة إذا ظهر تأثيرها فيحكم، فلا تستعمل
في إثبات حكم آخر- أعني: في إثبات نوع آخر من الحكم- PageV01P133 # بل تستعمل لتعدية ذلك الحكم بعينه إلى محل آخر، على لسان الفقهاء. وهو-
على التحقيق- إثبات مثل ذلك الحكم في محل آخر.
وهو كالأمثلة التي ضرناها في اللمس والمس وخروج الخارج؛ فإنه جمل علة
لانتقاض الوضوء: فلا يستعمل إلا في انتقاض الوضوء؛ ولكن في محل آخر غير  محل
النص: كمس ذكر الغير، ولمس المرأة الرجل، وخروج الدم من غير المخرج
المعتاد. وجميع الأقيسة تجري على هذا المثال: فإن القياس لتعدية حكم
المنصوص بالعلة المتعدية، وتعميمه لعموم العلة. ولو كان يثبت بالعلة جنس
آخر من الحكم: لم يكن هذا تعدية المنصو؛ بل كان ابتداء لحكم على سبيل
الاستئناف. فلعتقد هذا في كل قياس.
أما المثال الذي ضربناه في تقديم الأخ من الأب والأم في الميراث، وقياس
التقديم في ولاية النكاح عليه- فهو من هذا القبيل: لأن الاختصاص بهذه
المزية علة التقديم في الإرث، فيعمم التقديم؛ وهو قضية معقولة، ونعديه إلى
محل آخر وهو: ولاية النكاح. وتكون نسبة ولاية التزويج إلى الإرث، كنسبة
الزبيب إلى التمر في الربا؛ فإن الطعم والكيل حرم الفضل في التمر، فيثبت
تحريم الفضل في الزبيب: للاشتراك في العلة.
وكذا: الصغر علة ولاية المال، وولاية البضع- في حق الابن، فيجعل علة
ولاية البضع في حق الثيب [الصغيرة]، لأنه عقل كونه PageV01P134 # علة الإجبار والولاية [في البضع] في حق الابن، وهو محل الحكم، فيعدى إلى
البضع في [حق] الثيب؛ والبضع ينزل من المال منزلة نوع من المال مع نوع آخر،
ومنزلة الزبيب من التمر في الربا.
فالحكم الثابت في محل الإجماع بعينه، يعدى [24 - ب] ويعمم بالقياس. وكذلك
نطرد هذا الجنس في جميع الأمثلة التي ذكرناها.
وإذا نبهنا على الطريق: لم يخف وجه التقرير في جميع الأمثلة؛ وما خرج من
هذا الجنس فليس من القياس في شيء.
فإن قيل: أليس جعل الشرع القتل علة الحرمان في الميراث، فجعل [بالقياس
علة] بطلان الوصية، وهو حكم آخر. وقد قال تعالى: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق
سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل}، جعل الضعف
والسفه علة قضاء الدين، فجعل علة الإجبار في سائر التصرفات: من البيع
والإجارة، وغيرهما؟
قلنا: هذا داخل الحد الذي ذكرناه. وإنما المفهوم أن الضعف PageV01P135 # بالصغر والسفه سبب نيابة الولي المشفق عنه، فيما تمس حاجته إليه: من قضاء
الدين؛ فسائر ما تمس حاجته  إليه ينزل من محل النص منزلة سائر المكيلات
والمطعومات من المنصوص في الربا. والثابت بالنص في قضاء الدين: [النيابة]
بعلة الصغر في محل الحاجة؛ فعديت النيابة إلى كل ما تتعدى إليه الحاجة.
وأما الوصية، فمن يبغي الإلحاق: يتكلف التلفيق بهذا الطريق، ويثبت أن
استحقاق المال [بمجرد مطلق] الموت نوع خلافه؛ تارة يستفاد بالقرابة، وأخرى
بالزوجية، وطوروا بالوصية؛ فالكل باب واحد؛ فيرجع الافتراق إلى العدد كما
في الربويات، أو يقول: المفهوم من النص معارضته بنقيض قصده فيما تعدى
باستعجاله؛ وفي هذا تشترط الوصية والإرث ويرجع التمييز إلى العدد، وهذا شرط
كل قياس. وما خرج عن هذا القياس، فليس من القياس في شيء.
يبقى خيال السائل: أنه إذا سلم كونه مؤثرا، فكيف يتصور النزاع في المسألة
بعد الإجماع على وجود ما هو المؤثر؟
PageV01P136
قلنا: من سلم الإجماع على كون الوصف مؤثرا، وسلم سلامته عن المعارضة في
محل النزاع- لم يتصور منه النزاع مع ذلك إلا بجحد أصل القياس. وإنما منشأ
النزاع أحد أمرين: إما الاسترابة في كون الوصف مؤثرا بالإجماع والمجاحدة
فيه، أو اعتقاد معارضة في الفرع.
أما مثال الأول: فكمنازعتنا لأبي حنيفة في دعواه أن المؤثر في إطال هبة
المريض حق الغريم؛ فإن من أصحابنا من يعتقد: أنه بطل تصرفه نظرا له في
نفسه، وليس من النظر إبطال إقراره؛ وإنما ننازعهم: لأنا لا نسلم كون هذا
الوصق مؤثؤا بالإجماع.
فطريقه أن يكشف عما يدعيه: من الإجماع؛ وهو إبطال ما ندعيه: من المعنى؛
ليتعين معناه. فإنه حكم لابد من تعليله بما يتضمنه المرض الحادث. والذي
يمكن أن يقدر علة [لا يزيد] على المعنيين؛ في بطلان أحدهما إثبات الآخر.
فيقول: إبطال تصرف العاقل نظرا له، لا عهد به. وإبطال تصرفه لحق الغير [عهد
في الشرع في مواضع بالإجماع؛ فإحالة الحكم في هذا المقام إلى ما] عهد في
الشرع اعتباره في إبطال التصرفات أولى؛ لأنه معنى عرف بالإجماع تأثيره في
جنس هذا الحكم.
فيرجع مثار النزاع إلى أنا لا نعترف بالإجماع أولا، فلو اعترفنا PageV01P137 # أولا  بالإجماع: لما نازعناه رفي الإقرار إلا بتقدير [25 - أ] دليل في
الإقرار يعارض ما ذكروه، وهو قياس الإقرار على النكاح وسائر التصرفات،
لرابطة الحاجة؛ ويتبين به أن حق الغريم لا يمنعه إلا عما يستغني عنه في هذا
المقام. بخلاف حق الغريم في الرهن والتركة وغيره.
وأما الجنس الآخر من المنازعة- بعد تسليم التأثير- فينشأ من تقدير
المعارضة: كما ذكرناه على أحد التقديرين في مسألة غرماء المرض والصحة، وكما
نعتقد في مسألة الثيب الصغيرة، ويعتقد أبو حنيفة في مسألة غرم السارق.
فأما مسألة الصغيرة، فنسلم أن الصغر علة الولاية في حق الابن وفي حق
ولاية المال؛ نسلم وجود الصغر في [عين] محل النزاع؛ PageV01P138 # ولكن نقول: عارض الصغر الثيابة، وهي علة لإسقاط الولاية بنصب الشارع
إياها علة، بقوله: «الثيب أحق بنفسها من وليها».
ويسلم الخصم وجود علة الضمان [في السارق] ولكن يقول: عرضه وجوب القطع،
ومن ضرورته إسقاط الضمان بتقدير انتقال العصمة إلى [اليد] كما قرروه في تلك
المسألة.
ولو استعمل سائل هذا الاعتراض على طريق المطالبة والممانعة، وقال: لا
نسلم أن تلف المال تحت اليد العادية سبب الضمان لمجرده، بل هو مع سقوط
القطع هو السبب؛ والصغر مع انتفاء الثيابة هو العلة- فهذا كلام فاسد يضاهي
كلام من يقول: العلة ما ذكرته مع PageV01P139 # السلامة عن المعارضة [فإذا ذكر وجه السلامة عن المعارضة] فهو مردود عليه؛
والمطالبة متوجهة عليه بإبداء المعارضة، إذا ليس هذا جاريا مجرى أجزاء
العلة، بل له منصب الاستقلال.
فإن قيل: فبماذا تنقطع المطالبة إذا قال السائل: سلمت تأثير العلة في ذلك
المحل، فما دليل تأثيره في محل النزاع؟
قلنا: هذه المطالبة ساقطة بمجرد تسليم التأثي، وكان كقول القائل: سلمت أن
الكيل هو المؤثر في تحريم [ربا] الفضل في البر، وسلمت وجود الكيل في الجص؛
ولكن لم قلت: إذا أثر ثم، ينبغي أن يؤثر ها هنا؟ وهذا تشوف إلى حسم باب
القياس؛ وليس يحتاج المعلل إلأى إظهار وجه المناسبة بعدما سلم له كون الوصف
مؤثرا في الحكم في موضع ما: لأن معنى  كونه مؤثرا [هو]: أن الحكم حصل به ومن
أثره، وأن الشارع نصبه علة موجبة، وقد عرف ذلك بالإجماع، فصار كما لو عرف
ذلك بالنص والإيماء.
وقد بينا أنه يستغنى فيه عن إبداء المناسبة، وإن كان يبعد انفكاكه عن
مناسبة ما. فقل ما يوجد- من تصرفات الشرع- ما يجري على مذاق التحكم الجامد
المحض؛ ولكن: لو وجد وجب اعتباره في غير PageV01P140 # محل النص، بحكم الدليل الذي دل على أصل القياس، وكان هذا كما لو قال: لا
تبيعوا التمر بالتمر لأنه حلو؛ فيعتر الزبيب به بجامع الحلاوة، بعد أن عرف
الشرع كونه علة وإن لم تعرف مناسبته ووجه اقتضاء تحريمه من طريق المصالح.
وإذا قال: لا تبيعوا البر بالبر لأنه أيض؛ قيس عليه الأرز وإن لم تعرف
مناسبته. ولم نلتفت إلى قول القائل: أن البياض علة في البر لا في غيره،
والحلاوة علة في التمر لا في غيره.
والسبب في ذلك كله- وهو طريق الرد على منكري القياس-: قضاء العقول باتباع
الأسباب، والأعراض عن المحال. فلا فرق في [25 - ب] عقل حملة الشريعة- بين
أن يقول الشارع: اقتلوا ما عزا لأنه زان؛ وبين أن يقول: اقتلوه لأنه طويل-
في أنا نطرد إيجاب القتل في حق جميع الزناة وجميل الطوال، وان انتفت
المناسبة؛ لأن المناسبة طريق يعرف بها كون الوصف منصوبا من جهة الشرع علما
على الحكم وعلة له؛ وهي دون النص والإجماع، فإذا ظهر بالنص أو الإجماع:
أغنىعلى إظهار المناسبة.
ورجع حاصل هذا المسلك إلى أن الوصف إنما يصير علة: إذا علم أن الشارع
جعله علة؛ وإنما يعرف جعل الشارع إياه علة: بنصه،
PageV01P141
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes a recurrent cause, an occasioning factor, or a defect that necessitates a repeated effect; it implies a nexus between an efficient cause and its consequent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, ʿilla is the divinely-instituted attribute (waṣf) that serves as the sign (amārah) and motive (bāʿith) for a ruling, known either by naṣṣ, ijmāʿ, or munāsabah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, ʿilla is a cause that "recurs" (taʿallala) to produce its effect; metaphorically, it is the legal ratio that justifies the extension (taʿdiyah) of a ḥukm to new cases.
- Root: ق-ي-س (q-y-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To measure, compare, or estimate by analogy; the act of equating one thing with another on the basis of a shared attribute.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyās is the juristic method of extending a ruling from an original case (aṣl) to a branch case (farʿ) due to the commonality of the effective cause (ʿilla).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, measuring length or quantity; metaphorically, the intellectual operation of transferring a ḥukm by identifying a shared ratio.
- Root: ن-ق-ض (n-q-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To break, annul, or invalidate; to undo a prior state of validity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, naqḍ refers to the nullification of ritual purity (ṭahārah) or a contract, indicating the removal of a prior legal status.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, the unraveling of a woven fabric; metaphorically, the abrogation of a legal effect by a countervailing cause.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-Ḥukm bi al-ʿIllah (Attribution of a ruling to its cause) — When a predicate is attached to a subject via a conditional or causal particle (e.g., "man massa... fa-l-yatawaḍḍaʾ"), the ruling is understood to be contingent upon the stated cause, allowing for its extension to analogous instances where the cause exists.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding the establishment of those rulings and the operation of qiyās (analogy) therein — what is the way to escape the demand [for justification] without demonstrating the suitability (munāsabah) in them? Or what is the way to demonstrate the suitability in them? Or what is the face of the need for suitability in the previous examples, if we do not need it in these examples?

The answer: These examples are those over which the uṣūliyyūn (legal theorists) have differed in their nomenclature. Some of them have described them as being "in the meaning of the original" (fī maʿnā al-aṣl). This, in our view, is an ambiguous statement. The correct view is to call them qiyās, but they are not of the same kind as the previous examples. For the one who performs qiyās (al-qāʾis) in such examples does not make the effective cause (al-sabab al-muʾaththir) operative in another ruling, such that he would be required to prove the homogeneity (mujānasah) between the two rulings through their equality in suitability. Rather, he makes the cause operative in the very same ruling whose effect has appeared in it, but in another locus (maḥall) not explicitly stated [in the text]. For the effect of touching (al-lams), sexual contact (al-mass), and the emission of something (khurūj al-khārij) has appeared in the obligation of wuḍūʾ (ablution); and he makes them operative in the obligation of wuḍūʾ.

Yes, if someone were to say: "These causes, since they nullify purity (ṭahārah), ought to nullify the fast (ṣawm)" — this would be of the same weight as the previous examples, and it would be said to him: "Why do you say: 'Since their effect has appeared in nullifying purity, it ought to appear in nullifying the fast'?" And he would be compelled to demonstrate the homogeneity through equality in suitability.

Rather, we see that this kind of qiyās should be labeled "the refinement of the locus of the ruling and its attachment" (tanqīḥ manāṭ al-ḥukm wa-mutaʿallaqih). We shall mention examples of this kind in its proper place.

A group of uṣūliyyūn have called this kind "the indication of the address" (dalālat al-khiṭāb). Others have called it "that which is in the meaning of the original" (mā fī maʿnā al-aṣl). The upshot of all this reverts to the refinement of the attachment of the ruling and its locus, by canceling (ilghāʾ) what is conjoined with it incidentally (wifāqan) and not intended by the attachment of the ruling to it. For His saying — peace be upon him — «من مس ذكره فليتوضأ» ("Whoever touches his penis, let him perform ablution") — the attachment of wuḍūʾ to the touching of the penis is not because it is his penis; rather, the mention of the attachment to it occurred incidentally, because it is the predominant case in touching; for it is unlikely that a man would touch another's penis.

Likewise, his saying — peace be upon him — «من أعتق شركا له في عبد» ("Whoever frees his share in a slave") [the ḥadīth]. The freeing of a part is the cause of the extension of freedom (sarāyah) to the freeing of the entire slave; but the mention of the slave occurred incidentally, because it is what comes first to the tongue in custom. Thus, by the rule of custom, it is a metonymy (kināyah) for any slave (raqīq).

And it is like his saying — peace be upon him — «أيما رجل مات أو أفلس فصاحب المتاع أحق بمتاعه» ("Any man who dies or becomes bankrupt, the owner of the goods has the greater right to his goods"). The woman is annexed to the man, but the mention of the man occurred incidentally, because he is what comes first to the tongue; thus, by the rule of custom, he is a metonymy for the human being (insān) in this context.

Similarly, if a man said to his wife: "You are divorced on the day Zayd arrives," and he arrived at night — she is divorced according to the majority of jurists, because "day" in this context, by the rule of custom (ʿurf), is a metonymy for "time" (waqt), since it is what comes first to the tongue.

Likewise, the Messenger of Allah — peace be upon him — said: «لا يبلون أحدكم في الماء الراكد» ("Let none of you urinate in still water") — this entails the prohibition of pouring urine from a jug into the water; because the understood meaning (mafhūm) is the prevention of polluting the water by casting impurity into it. But a person, by his nature, refrains from casting impurities into water without a purpose; rather, what occurs from him is urination in the water. Thus, its specification occurred incidentally, by the rule of custom.

These are matters known from the indication of the address (dalālat al-khiṭāb), the context of speech (siyāq al-kalām), and the circumstantial evidence (qarīnat al-ḥāl). So we dare to make the annexation (ilḥāq) and we escape the demand [for justification] in this kind of annexation, by this art of discourse.

The other answer: This kind, too, is not outside the understanding of a type of meaning (maʿnā). For touching (al-mass) is a type of violation (hatk): since it is a prelude to the emission of madhy (pre-ejaculatory fluid); for it stirs the organ, arouses desire, and recalls intercourse; thus madhy is emitted, and wuḍūʾ is nullified, because it is a cause of the emission of madhy even if it does not emit. Likewise, touching women is a cause of the emission of madhy, so wuḍūʾ is nullified even if no madhy is emitted.

Just as sleep is a cause of the emission of wind (rīḥ), so it is an event (ḥadath) even if no wind is emitted. Likewise, the meeting of the two circumcised parts (iltiqāʾ al-khātanayn) is a cause of the emission of semen (manī), so it is made a major impurity (janābah) even if it is not verified.

And the emission of impurity (khurūj al-najāsah) — in general — is suitable (munāsib) to the occupation with purification (taṭhīr) at the locus of impurity, and over the entire body. But the encompassing of the entire body was dropped due to hardship (ʿusr), and it was restricted to the apparent limbs in the predominant case.

These meanings are understood from these causes in specification (takhṣīṣ) and in extension (taʿdiyah): either by themselves, or by being a corroborating indicator (qarīnah muʿayyinah) in understanding the locus of the ruling (manāṭ al-ḥukm) from the direction of the mentioned [cause], and a pointer to the cancellation of what has no entry into this type of effect.

This is the way of establishing this art. We have called these answers "al-tanbīh" (the pointer), and they are — in truth — a figment (khayāl) in response to a figment; that is, a course of a type of disputation (jadal), and a paving of the way to figuration (takhyīl) and evasion (iḥtiyāl).

But the revealing disclosure (al-kashf al-shāfī) is what we now mention, namely: The saying of the speaker: "If the effect of the cause has appeared in a ruling, why ought it to effect another genus of ruling?" — if the locus of extension is another genus. But if it is the very same ruling or its like, then how can one conceive — while conceding its being effective — of disputing the ruling with the existence of what is effective in it?

This is a figment with nothing behind it: For when the cause's effect has appeared in a ruling, it is not used to establish another ruling — that is, to establish another type of ruling — but rather it is used to extend that very ruling to another locus, in the language of the jurists. And it is — in truth — the establishment of the like of that ruling in another locus.

This is like the examples we gave in touching (al-lams), sexual contact (al-mass), and the emission of something (khurūj al-khārij); for it is made a cause for the nullification of wuḍūʾ: so it is not used except in the nullification of wuḍūʾ, but in another locus other than the locus of the text: such as touching another's penis, a woman touching a man, and the emission of blood from other than the customary outlet. And all qiyās proceeds on this example: For qiyās is for the extension of the ruling of the text by the transgressive cause (al-ʿillah al-mutaʿaddiyah), and its generalization by the generality of the cause. And if another genus of ruling were established by the cause, this would not be an extension of the text; rather, it would be an initiation of a ruling by way of a fresh start (istiʾnāf). So let this be believed in every qiyās.

As for the example we gave in the advancement of the paternal brother (al-akh min al-ab wa-al-umm) in inheritance, and the qiyās of advancement in the guardianship of marriage (wilāyat al-nikāḥ) upon it — this is of that kind: For the specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) with this merit is the cause of advancement in inheritance, so it is generalized in advancement; and it is a rational matter (qaḍiyyah maʿqūlah), and we extend it to another locus, namely: the guardianship of marriage. And the relation of the guardianship of marriage to inheritance is like the relation of raisins (zabīb) to dates (tamr) in ribā (usury); for the taste (ṭaʿm) and the measure (kayl) prohibited the excess (faḍl) in dates, so the prohibition of excess is established in raisins: due to the sharing in the cause.

Likewise, minority (ṣighar) is a cause of guardianship over wealth (wilāyat al-māl) and guardianship over the pudendum (wilāyat al-buḍʿ) — in the case of the son — so it is made a cause of guardianship over the pudendum in the case of the mature virgin (al-thayyib al-ṣaghīrah), because he understands its being a cause of compulsion (ijbār) and guardianship over the pudendum in the case of the son, which is the locus of the ruling, so it is extended to the pudendum in the case of the mature virgin; and the pudendum descends from wealth in the station of one type of wealth with another type, and in the station of raisins from dates in ribā.

So the ruling established in the locus of consensus (maḥall al-ijmāʿ) — in its very self — is extended and generalized by qiyās. Likewise, we run this kind through all the examples we have mentioned.

And when we have pointed to the way, the face of establishment in all examples is not hidden; and whatever falls outside this kind is not of qiyās in any way.

If it is said: "Does not the Lawgiver make killing (qatl) a cause of deprivation (ḥirmān) in inheritance, and then make it, by qiyās, a cause of the invalidity of bequest (waṣiyyah), which is another ruling? And He — exalted — has said: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل} ("If the one upon whom the right is due is a fool or weak or cannot dictate, then let his guardian dictate with justice") — He made weakness (ḍaʿf) and foolishness (safah) a cause of the settlement of debt (qaḍāʾ al-dayn), and then made it a cause of compulsion in all other transactions: from sale (bayʿ), hire (ijārah), and others?"

We say: This falls within the limit we have mentioned. For the understood meaning is that weakness — by minority and foolishness — is a cause of the deputyship (niyābah) of the compassionate guardian on his behalf, in what his need requires: from the settlement of debt; so all that his need requires descends from the locus of the text in the station of the other measurable and edible items (al-makīlāt wa-al-maṭʿūmāt) from the texted [items] in ribā. And what is established by the text in the settlement of debt is: deputyship, by the cause of minority in the locus of need; so deputyship is extended to everything to which need extends.

As for the bequest (waṣiyyah), whoever seeks the annexation must undertake the stitching (talfīq) by this way, and establish that the entitlement to wealth — by mere absolute death — is a type of its like; sometimes it is obtained by kinship (qarābah), sometimes by marriage (zawjiyyah), and sometimes by bequest; so all are one door (bāb wāḥid); thus the differentiation reverts to the number (al-ʿadad) as in the ribawiyyāt (usurious items). Or he says: The understood meaning from the text is its opposition to the contrary of its intent (naqīḍ qaṣdih) in what exceeds by its hastening (istiʿjāl); and in this, the bequest and inheritance are conditioned, and the distinction reverts to the number, and this is the condition of every qiyās. And whatever falls outside this qiyās is not of qiyās in any way.

There remains the figment of the questioner: That if he concedes its being effective, how can the dispute in the matter be conceived after the consensus on the existence of what is effective?

We say: Whoever concedes the consensus on the attribute's being effective, and concedes its safety from opposition (muʿāraḍah) in the locus of dispute — his dispute with that is not conceivable except by the denial of the very principle of qiyās. Rather, the source of the dispute is one of two matters: either doubt (istirābah) in the attribute's being effective by consensus and the denial (mujāḥadah) of it, or the belief in an opposition in the branch (farʿ).

As for the example of the first: It is like our dispute with Abū Ḥanīfah in his claim that the effective [cause] in the invalidation of the sick person's gift (hibat al-marīḍ) is the right of the creditor (ḥaqq al-gharīm). For among our companions (aṣḥāb) there are those who believe: that his transaction is invalidated out of consideration for himself (naẓaran lahu fī nafsih), and it is not from consideration to invalidate his acknowledgment (iqrār). And we only dispute them: because we do not concede this attribute's being effective by consensus.

So his way is to uncover what he claims: of consensus; and it is the invalidation of what we claim: of the meaning; so that his meaning is determined. For it is a ruling that must be caused by what the emergent illness (al-maraḍ al-ḥādith) entails. And what can be estimated as a cause — no more than the two meanings — in the invalidation of one of them is the establishment of the other. So he says: The invalidation of a sane person's transaction out of consideration for him — there is no precedent for it. And the invalidation of his transaction for the right of another — has precedent in the Law in places by consensus; so the referral of the ruling in this context to what is known in the Law as being considered in the invalidation of transactions is more appropriate (awlā); because it is a meaning known by consensus to have effect in this genus of ruling.

So the source of the dispute reverts to our not acknowledging the consensus first. For if we acknowledged the consensus first, we would not dispute him in the acknowledgment (iqrār) except by estimating a proof in the acknowledgment that opposes what they mentioned — namely, the qiyās of the acknowledgment upon marriage (nikāḥ) and all other transactions, due to the bond of need (rābiṭat al-ḥājah); and by it, it becomes clear that the right of the creditor does not prevent him except from what he is independent of in this context. Unlike the right of the creditor in the pledge (rahn), the estate (tarikah), and others.

As for the other genus of dispute — after the concession of effectiveness — it arises from the estimation of opposition: as we mentioned on one of the two estimations in the matter of the creditors of illness and health (ghuramāʾ al-maraḍ wa-al-ṣiḥḥah), and as we believe in the matter of the mature virgin (al-thayyib al-ṣaghīrah), and as Abū Ḥanīfah believes in the matter of the thief's guarantee (ghurm al-sāriq).

As for the matter of the minor [virgin], we concede that minority is a cause of guardianship in the case of the son and in the case of guardianship over wealth; we concede the existence of minority in the very locus of dispute; but we say: The minority is opposed by the state of being a mature virgin (thayyibah), which is a cause for the dropping of guardianship, by the Lawgiver's installation of it as a cause, by His saying — peace be upon him: «الثيب أحق بنفسها من وليها» ("The mature virgin has more right to herself than her guardian").

And the opponent concedes the existence of the cause of guarantee in the thief, but he says: The obligation of amputation (wujūb al-qaṭʿ) opposes it, and from its necessity is the dropping of the guarantee, by the estimation of the transfer of inviolability (ʿiṣmah) to the hand, as they have established in that matter.

And if the questioner were to use this objection by way of demand and resistance (muṭālabah wa-mumānaʿah), and say: "We do not concede that the destruction of wealth under the transgressing hand is a cause of guarantee by its mere self; rather, it is with the dropping of amputation that it is the cause; and minority with the absence of the state of being a mature virgin is the cause" — this is corrupt speech (kalām fāsid) resembling the speech of one who says: "The cause is what I mentioned, with safety from opposition." For if he mentions the face of safety from opposition, it is rejected against him; and the demand is directed upon him to demonstrate the opposition, since this does not run in the course of the parts of the cause, but rather has the station of independence (istiqlāl).

If it is said: "By what is the demand cut off when the questioner says: 'I concede the effect of the cause in that locus, so what is the proof of its effect in the locus of dispute?'"

We say: This demand falls by the mere concession of effectiveness. It is like the saying of one who says: "I concede that measure (kayl) is the effective [cause] in the prohibition of excess in wheat (burr), and I concede the existence of measure in gypsum (jiṣṣ); but why do you say: 'If it effected there, it ought to effect here?'" This is a yearning to seal the door of qiyās. And the one who gives the cause (al-muʿallil) does not need to show the face of suitability after the concession to him of the attribute's being effective in the ruling in some locus: because the meaning of its being effective is: that the ruling is obtained by it and from its effect, and that the Lawgiver installed it as an obligating cause (ʿillah mūjibah), and that is known by consensus, so it becomes as if it were known by text (naṣṣ) and indication (īmāʾ).

And we have explained that one is independent of showing suitability in it, even if it is unlikely to be free of some suitability. For rarely is found — from the transactions of the Law — what runs on the taste of pure arbitrary command (taḥakkum jāmid muḥḍ). But: if it were found, it would be obligatory to consider it in other than the locus of the text, by the rule of the proof that indicated the principle of qiyās. And this is like if He said: "Do not sell dates for dates because it is sweet (ḥulw)"; then raisins would be considered by it through the commonality of sweetness, after the Law's being known to make it a cause, even if its suitability and the face of its requiring prohibition are not known from the way of interests (maṣāliḥ).

And if He said: "Do not sell wheat for wheat because it is white (abyaḍ)"; rice (aruzz) would be measured upon it, even if its suitability is not known. And we do not heed the saying of one who says: "Whiteness is a cause in wheat, not in other than it; and sweetness is a cause in dates, not in other than it."

And the reason for all this — and it is the way of refuting the deniers of qiyās — is: the judgment of intellects (qaḍāʾ al-ʿuqūl) to follow causes, and to turn away from the impossible (muḥāl). For there is no difference — in the intellect of the bearers of the Law — between the Lawgiver's saying: "Kill whoever commits adultery (zanā) because he is an adulterer (zān)," and His saying: "Kill him because he is tall (ṭawīl)" — in that we extend the obligation of killing to all adulterers and all tall people, even if suitability is absent; because suitability is a way by which the attribute's being installed by the Law as a sign (ʿalam) of the ruling and a cause for it is known; and it is below the text and consensus. So when it appears by text or consensus, it suffices over showing suitability.

And the upshot of this path reverts to: The attribute only becomes a cause when it is known that the Lawgiver made it a cause; and the Lawgiver's making it a cause is only known by His text, or by consensus, or by indication (īmāʾ), or by suitability (munāsabah) — and the latter is the weakest of these paths. So when the effectiveness is known by text or consensus, the demand for suitability is dropped, and the extension (taʿdiyah) becomes obligatory by the very principle of qiyās, which is the consensus of the Companions and the continuous practice of the Law.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "relation, affinity, connection" — a bond between two things that renders them coherent or fitting together.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, munāsabah denotes a descriptive attribute whose suitability to the ruling is rationally discernible, indicating divine wisdom (ḥikmah) in legislation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to genealogical or relational kinship; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any conceptual congruence between cause and effect in legal reasoning.
- Root: خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning is "to imagine, to fancy, to form a mental impression" — often carrying a sense of subjective estimation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Takhyīl (imaginative suggestion) in kalām refers to a psychological inclination of the heart toward a meaning, distinct from demonstrative proof.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Distinguishes the literal sense of "imagining" from the technical legal sense where ikhālah is used pejoratively by opponents to dismiss suitability as mere subjective fancy.
- Root: أ-ث-ر (a-th-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "trace, mark, effect" — that which remains as a consequence of an agent's action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, al-muʾaththir is the attribute whose causal efficacy (taʾthīr) is established by textual evidence or consensus, not by mere rational suitability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes physical imprinting; metaphorical usage in legal theory denotes proven causal efficacy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīr (Ellipsis Restoration) — When terms like "al-munāsabah" are defined, the underlying syntactic structure must be restored (e.g., "al-waṣf al-munāsib" = the suitable attribute) to clarify the referent and avoid ambiguity in argumentation.
chapters.translation:
I say: The fourth path is the inference that an attribute is a legal cause (ʿillah) by virtue of its suitability (munāsabah) to the ruling — either through an indication of the text in its admonition and allusion (tanbīh wa īmāʾ), as previously discussed, or through consensus (ijmāʿ) of the ummah. For consensus in definition is like the text itself. Thus this path is annexed to the preceding paths, and one becomes independent of suitability therein, just as in the case of the explicitly stated (manṣūṣ) and the textually indicated (munabbah ʿalayh).

The fourth path concerns inferring that an attribute is a cause by virtue of suitability between it and the ruling. This is a matter upon which the uṣūliyyūn have differed.

What Abū Zayd [al-Dabūsī] mentioned is that suitability is not sufficient to establish that an attribute is a cause; rather, one must demonstrate efficacy (taʾthīr) — through the text or consensus, as previously stated. He thus restricted himself to the preceding paths and was not satisfied with anything less. He argued for this by saying: The essence of ikhālah (imaginative suggestion) reduces to a psychological occurrence, an acceptance by the heart, and a tranquility of the soul toward it. This is an internal matter that cannot be established against an opponent. For if one says, "This has prevailed in my conjecture (ghalaba ʿalā ẓannī)," the opponent may reply, "It has not prevailed in my conjecture." Thus appealing to the heart is only permissible in the absence of evidentiary proofs, or when proofs conflict and their paths are obstructed, due to the necessity compelling it. Moreover, it is restricted to the mujtahid's own judgment and can never be erected as a proof against an opponent.

What he mentioned is indeed conceded — but the intended meaning of the suitable imaginative attribute (al-maʿnā al-mukhayyil al-munāsib) is not what he supposed and imagined. Rather, by "suitability" we mean a meaning that is rationally intelligible and manifest to the intellect, which can be readily established against an opponent through the path of rational inquiry — such that the opponent, after its demonstration through its proper method, is attributed, in his denial, to rejection and obstinacy.

Thus, the source of the difficulty is the clarification of the definition of suitability (ḥadd al-munāsabah); and ikhālah is merely an expression for it. The jurists have variously employed the terms: al-muʾaththir (the efficacious), al-munāsib (the suitable), al-mukhayyil (the imaginative), al-mulāʾim (the compatible), al-muʾadhdhin bi-l-ḥukm (the indicator of the ruling), and al-mushʿir bihi (the suggester of it). Yet the discernment and distinction among these aspects has remained obscure to the multitude of scholars and the virtuous — except those whom God wills — and the path to grasping their realities, with their definitions and properties, has proven difficult for them.

Attached to the trailing ends of these genera are the analogy of resemblance (qiyās al-shabah) and mere dismissal (al-ṭard) — which constitute the great diving place and the immense deep. Rare indeed upon the face of the earth is one who knows the meaning of the valid resemblance (al-shabah al-muʿtabar), who excels in distinguishing it from the imaginative (al-mukhayyil) and the dismissive (al-ṭard), and who applies it upon a course that does not blend with either of the two arts.

And we — with God's aid and His gracious success — shall elaborate these genera, and therein heal the thirst (nashfī al-ghalīl), and be concise in our discourse on the analogy of resemblance. We now proceed to explain what we have resolved upon: the types of analogy of meaning (qiyās al-maʿnā).

We say: The sum total of these expressions yields three types.

### ||| The Efficacious (al-Muʾaththir), the Suitable (al-Munāsib), and the Compatible (al-Mulāʾim)

As for al-mushʿir (the suggester), al-muʾadhdhin (the indicator), and al-mukhayyil (the imaginative) — these are, in effect, repeated expressions for the suitable (al-munāsib).

As for al-muʾaththir (the efficacious) — it is what we have mentioned: that which the text or consensus has indicated to be the cause of the ruling in the locus of the text, or in a locus other than the text's. This is what we have chosen to label "al-muʾaththir," so that the genus may be distinguished from the genus — otherwise, the designation of "al-munāsib" would suffice.

### ||| The Suitable (al-Munāsib), and Its Examples

يستد التمثيل، وينقطع عن المؤثر، فإن  المستدل بالمناسبه يدعى الإستغناء عن
النص وإيمانه ودلالة الإجماع على كونه مؤثرا؛ ويزعم: أن المناسبه كافية في
التعريف، على ما سنذكر وجه حصول المعرفه بها.
وكذلك إذا قلنا: إن الجماعة قتلوا بالواحد، كيلا يتخذ الظلمة PageV01P146 # الاستعانه ذريعة إلى قتل الأعداء-كان ذلك تعليلا بمخيل مناسب ظهر وجه
استدعائه للحكم، واقتضائه له في العقل. ولم يدل دليل على تأثيره: لا من جهة
النص؛ ولا من جهة الإجماع. بخلاف التعليل بالصغر فإنه- مع المناسبه
المعقولة - ظهر تأثيره في الولاية المالية، وولاية التزويج - في حق الأبن،
بالإتفاق.
وكذلك إذا قلنا: حط قضاء الصلوات عن الحائض، لما فيه: من الحرج والمشقة
والكلفة مع تكرر الصلاه في اليوم والليله؛ بخلاف قضاء الصوم -كان] هذا
[الكلام مناسبا] 26 - ب [مخيلا، متميزا عن تعليله: بأن الصوم يقضى لأنه لا
تجب فية الطهاره مثلا، بخلاف الصلاه. فإن هذا الفرق لايناسب، ولا ينسى عن
الحكم في قضيه العقل بحال.
فهذا بيان المناسب. وليس يتميز عن المؤثر بذاته، وإنما يتميز عن المؤثر
بأن ليس من جهة النص والإجماع دلالة على كونه علة، بل لا دلالة عليه سوى
مناسبته. وما دل الإجماع على كونه عله] وسببا]، قد يناسب: كالصفر يناسب
الولاية، ومزيد PageV01P147 # الاختصاص في القرابة يناسب الترجيح والتقديم، الى غير ذلك مما تقدم: من
الأمثله. وقد لا يناسب: كخروج النطفة الطاهره، جعل سببا للغسل ولا يناسبه،
وكذلك مس الذكر: يبعد تخيل المناسبة فيه.
هذا وجه تمييز المناسب عن المؤثر والطرد.
أما تمييزه عن الملائم، فوجهه: أن المناسب ينقسم إلى ما يلائم معاني
الشرع، ويجانس تصرفاته فى ملاحظة المعاني. والى ما يكون غريبا: لا يلفى له جنس.
فالذي ذهب اليه الجماهير: أن المناسب لا يكون علة الا بشرط الملائمه] كما
سنذكره. ومنهم من اكتفى بمجرد المناسبة ولم يشترط الملائمة [، فكل مناسب
عهد جنسه في تصرفات الشرع: فهو ملائم؛ وما لم يعهد جنسه: فهو المناسب
الغريب الذى لا نظير له في تصرفات الشرع.
وهذا] الأن [مزله قدم؛ فقد يشتبه على الناظر الفرق بين الملائم والمؤثر،
فيقول: المؤثر هو: الذي عهد في الشرع معتبرا كما في الصغر؛ والملائم أيضا
كذلك. فما الفرق بين من شرط التأثير، وبين من شرط الملاءمه مع المناسبه؟
فنقول: الفرق بينهما: أن المؤثر هو: الذى ظهر تأثير، عينه في عين PageV01P148 # الحكم المتنازع فيه - بالإجماع أو النص، في محل النزاع، أو غير محل
النزاع. كقول الحنفي: إن الثيب الصغيرة تزوج لصغرها؛ ويبين أن عين الصغر
ظهر تأثير بالإجماع في الولاية في حق الأبن، وفي ولاية المال. فقد ظهر
تأثير عين هذا المعنى فى عين هذا الحكم، في محل آخر غير محل النزاع؛ فعدى
ذلك الحكم بعينه، وهو: الولاية بتلك العلة بعينها، وهي: الصغر - الى محل
النزاع، وهو: الثيب الصغيرة. وأما الملائم، فتعنى به: أنه عهد جنسه مؤثرا
فى جنس ذلك الحكم، وإن لم يعهد عنه مؤثرا فى عين ذلك الحكم - فى محل آخر.
مثاله: أن سقوط قضاء الصلاه إذا علل بالحرج والكلفه، يعلم أنه من جنس معاني
الشرع وملائم له، إذ ظهر - على الجمله - إسقاط] الشرع [جملة من التكاليف
بأنواع] من [الكلفة: كما في السفر والمرض وغيره؛ ولم يظهر تأثيره عين
المعنى فى عين الحكم، وإنما وزان المؤثر من] مثل [هذا الأصل: أن يأمر النبى
عليه السلام PageV01P149 # -مثلا- عائشة رضى الله عنها بقضاء الصوم الفائت في أيام الحيض، وبترك
القضاء فى الصلوات. فيقاس عليها سائر النساء. أو يحكم به في الحرة، فيقاس
عليها الرقيقة. فينقدح أن يقال: ظهر تأثير الحيض فى إسقاط الصلاة في حق
الحرة، فيعدى عين هذا الحكم لعين هذه العلة، الى الرقيقة.
وكذلك: إذا عللنا إنقطاع الولاية عن الثيب بالممارسة الحاصلة لها، وما
تستفيده المرأه: من الاختبار والتمييز والإهتداء الى المقاصد؛ وعديناه الى
الثيب الصغيرة- كان هذا مناسبا ولكنه غريب. إذ يقال: ليس هذا من جنس تصرفات
الشرع فى إثبات الولاية وقطعها، فنقول: هو من جنسه؛ إذ قال عز وجل:
"وابتلوا] 27 - أ [اليتامى حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح، فإن آنستم منهم رشدا
فأدفعوا اليهم أمواله".
فجعل ممارسه اليتيم في المال سببا، فيصير  ملائما. وهذه المناسبة مع
الملاءمة في نهاية الضعف، وليس من غرضنا عين هذه PageV01P150 # المسئلة؛ وإنما المقصود التمثيل لتعرف الجنس.
وكذلك إذا قلنا: قيد الشرع بيع الأشياء الأبعة فى الربا بثلاث شرائط،
فكان ذلك معللا بالطعم المنبئ عن الحرمة والعزة، فإن ما يعز ويحترم يضيق
طريق تحصيله، وما يستهان به يتسع الأمر فيه، ويتساهل في أمره؛ فلا يضيق
طريقه؛ لأن المضنون به عقلا وشرعا: ماظهرت الحاجة اليه، وعظمت حرمته بسببه،
والتقييد بالشرائط سد لبعض المسالك؛ وسد بعض الطرق إلى شيء ضنه به.
فهذا نوع من الكلام: فيه ضرب مناسبة، ولكنه غريب يزعم] الخصم [أنه لا
يلائم تصرفات الشرع، فنقول] لا [بل قيد الشرع إستحلال البضع بشروط: كالعوض
والولى والشهادة؛ وميزه عن الأموال. فكان ذلك إظهارا لشرف البضع، وتخصيصا
له بميزه الإعتناء، وكشفا عن خطره وحرمته، وإشارة إلى ان المال مبتذل
بالإضافة اليه، وأنه مصون مضنون به بالإضافه الى المال. فقد التحق بما عهد
جنسه في الشرع، فصار ملائما لتصرفاته.
PageV01P151
وطريق المعترض: أن يبين أن تقييد النكاح] بهذه الشروط [لم يكن بهذا
الطريق، بل كان لحاجة البضع في الصون الى هذه الشروط؛ ولا حاجة في صون
الأطعمه الى هذه الشروط، فيعترض بهذا الجنس، ويجاب عنه بطريقه. وغرضنا
التمثيل.
وكذلك إذا قلنا: القليل الذي لا يسكر- من الأنبذة - محرم قياسا على قليل
الخمر؛ وعللنا تحريم قليل الخمر: بأنه داع الى الكثير؛ وأن الطباع تختلف،
والقدر الذي يسكر كل شخص في كل حال لا ينضبط؛ فيحسب الباب بحكم المصلحة-كان
هذا كلاما مناسبا: يستوى فيه النبيذ والخمر، وتظهر ملاءمته لتصرفات الشرع:
بتحريم الشارع الخلوة بالأجنبية والنظر إليها، لأنه داع الى الزنا؛ وما
يجرى مجراه: من تعميم الشرع] التحريم [على مقدمات المحظورات ودواعها؛ فيكون
ملائما، ولا يكون مؤثرا التأثير الذي غيناه فيما سبق؛ إذ لم يظهر تأثير عين
انبعاث داعية الشرب، فى تحريم الشرب. ولا ظهر في مسئلة الربا تأثير عين
الطعم وحرمته في اشتراط المماثلة والتقابض PageV01P152 # والحلول؛ بل ظهر اعتبار جنس الحرمة، في جنس التقييد بالشروط.
فأن قيل: فما مثال المناسب [الغريب] الذي لا يلائم؟
قلنا: قل ما يتفق في المسائل أمثلته، فأن المعاني إذا ظهرت مناسبتها؛ فلا
تنفك عن التفات الشرع إلى جنسها في غالب الأمر؛ والذي يظهر لنا الآن من
أمثلتها أربعة:
المثال الأول: ما ذكرناه: من تعليل سقوط الإجبار عن الثيب بالممارسة.
فهذا وأن عددناه في قسم الملائم، فهو- عندنا -من المناسب الغريب الذي لا
نظير له.
وأما ابتلاء اليتيم في التصرف، فليس من هذا القبيل، وإنما مثاله: وطء
الابن زوجته؛ وذلك لا يوجب قطع الإجبار عنه: إذا كان صغيرا. أو وزانه من
الأموال: ما إذا تناول جنسا من الطعام وذاقه واستطابه أو استكرهه. وكل ذلك
ساقط الأثر في قطع الإجبار، وإسقاط الولاية. وابتلاء اليتيم: لتعرف هدايته
إلى المصالح، وانفكاكه عن داعية السفه والتبذير وغباوة الإسراف، والتصاون
عن الغبن والخداع؛ حتى إذا عرف ذلك بامتحانه بالبيع والشراء، رد المال إليه
بعد [27 - ب] جريان البلوغ: الذي هو السبب الظاهر في قطع الولاية. فوزانه:
أن تمتحن المرأة بانتقاء زوج من الأزواج للنكاح، وتراقب أحوالها في
اقتراحات مصالح النكاح وما تقترح عليها؛ فننقاد [إلى] الإجابة إلى PageV01P153 # ما تقتضيه المصلحة، ونستعصيى فيما ينافي الغبطة. ومثل ذلك لا عهد به في
النكاح؛ وإلمام الزوج بها ليس من هذا الجنس بحال؛ وإنما وزانه: تناول
الطعام وذوقه، ولبس الثوب، وركوب الدابة. فيبقى هذا نوعا غريبا من الكلام،
[وهو- مع كونه غريبا -] ضعيف في نفسه. وكذلك تتفق المعاني الغريبة؛ فأن ما
يظهر ويقوى لا ينعدم التفات الشرع إلى جنسه، في غالب الأمر.
المثال الثاني: تعليل الربا في المطعومات بعلة الطعم؛ فهو- أيضا -من
المعاني الغريبة التي لا تلائم معاني الشرع. وما ذكرناه- من إظهار الملائمة
بأمر البضع -ضعيف؛ لأن الخصم لا يسلم اشتراط الولي. نعم: قيد بالشهادة إما
صونا له من الفوات بالجحود، أو تمييزا [له] عن السفاح الذي هو فاحشة. وليس
في حسم طريق بيع البر بالبر متفاضلا، أو نسيئة، أو دون التقابض في المجلس -
ما يصونه عن فوات هو متعرض له، أو  يميزه [عن فاحشة] هو بصدد الانتباه بها؛
فلا مجانسة بينهما.
فيبقى ذلك معنى- أن سلم مناسبته -غريبا لا نظير له في الشرع.
والاعتماد في مسئلة الثيب الصغيرة، وإثبات الثيابة علة - على الإضافة
اللفظية، المستفادة من قوله- عليه السلام -: "الثيب أحق بنفسها من وليها".
وفي مسئلة الربا، وإثبات الطعم علة - على قوله- عليه السلام -: "لا تبيعوا PageV01P154 # الطعام بالطعام"، على ما قررناه في كتاب "مآخذ الخلاف"، وكتاب "تحصين
المآخذ" [وقد نبهنا على هذا المسلك الضعيف وطريق تقريره، في هذه الكتب].
المثال الثالث: تعليل بعض العلماء، حرمان القاتل عن الميراث، بمعارضته
بنقيض قصده: في استعجال الحق قبل أوانه.
وهذا أن لم يستعمل في معرض العقاب على عدوانه، يكون فنا غريبا من المعنى:
لا يلفى له نظير.
وإذا قيل: القتل جناية، والحرمان عقوبة؛ فكان منوطا به لكونه جناية، وقطع
عنه الصبي والمجنون - كان ذلك من قبيل التعليل بالمعنى الملائم؛ فأن تأثير
الجنايات في العقوبات والتغليظات، معهود من دأب الشرع.
PageV01P155
ولو ثبت معنى المعارضة بنقيض القصد للاستعجال، لكان تعليل [بعض] أصحابنا
في تحريم الخل الحاصل من التخليل، بمعارضته بنقيض قصده في استعجاله - من
جنس الملائم؛ إذ يصير معهود النظير في القتل، ولكن هذا المعنى- في القتل
-غير ثابت ولا مستقيم على السبر والبحث ولا يسلم عن النقض. وغرضنا ضرب
الأمثلة، لا أعيان هذه المسائل.
المثال الرابع للمناسب الغريب: تخصيص الوضوء في ترتيبه: بتقديم الوجه على
اليدين، وذكر ممسوح بين مغسولين؛ حتى قال الشافعي رحمه الله؛ هذا تنبيه على
كون الترتيب على هذا الوجه مقصودا؛ إذ لو لم يكن مقصودا: لم يكن هذا
الترتيب. وتخصيصه بالذكر- مع إيقاع ممسوح بين مغسولين -أولى من جريانه على
ترتيب الخلق: من البداية بالرأس، والانحدار إلى الوجه، والختم بالرجل. إلى
غير ذلك: من وجوه الترتيب.
PageV01P156
فيمنع الشافعي عن هذا الاستدلال، بأن يقال: سبب هذا الترتيب: تقديم الوجه
[28 - أ] لأنه أهم الأعضاء بتحصيل النظافة فيه؛ وتأخير الرجل: لأنه أحرى
الأعضاء بالبعد من النظافة، لمخالطة التراب في نقل الأقدام، ومماسة الخف
إلى غير ذلك؛ فتبقى اليد  والرأس، فكان تقديم اليد أولى: إذ هو آلة التناول
ويقع مكشوفا غالبا؛ والرأس في الغالب مستور بكور العمامة؛ ولذلك خفت وظيفته
وهو: المسح.
فهذا فن من الكلام مناسب، يتميز عن قول القائل: قدم الوجه لأنه على شكل
الاستدارة مثلا؛ إلى غير ذلك: من صفات خلقية تنبو عن الحكم.
إلا أن مثل هذه المعاني- وإن كانت مناسبة -فغير موثوق بها؛ إذ لم يثبت من
[جهة] الشرع ملاحظة جنسها، ويتسع التقدير في أمثالها، ولا يضيق طريقها على
أي وجه كان، فأنه لو ذكر الترتيب على عكس المعهود: لأمكن أن يعكس هذا
المعنى، ولكان يقال: الوضوء للصلاة، والصلاة تقع بعده؛ فأخره غسل الوجه:
لأنه أهم الأعضاء بالنظافة، ليكون العهد به- عند الاشتغال بالصلاة -أقرب؛
ولو ابتدأ بالرأس، ثم بالوجه، ثم باليد، ثم بالرجل: لأمكن أن يقال: سببه PageV01P157 # ترتيب الخلقة؛ ولو قدم اليد لأمكن أن يقال: سببه تنظيف الآلة أولا حتى
ينظف بها غيرها.
وأمثال هذه الخيالات يتسع طريقها، ولا يوثق بها.
نعم: هي صالحة في هذا المقام لدفع الاستدلال بالآية؛ فإن الآية ليس فيها
صيغة تدل على وجوب الترتيب؛ وإنما يستند المستدل فيها إلى تخصيص البعض
بالتقديم والتأخير، ويقول: إذا لم يكن له سبب، فسببه وجوب التقديم. فيقال:
هذا إمكان تعلقت به، وهذه الإمكانات تعارضه؛ فتطرق إليه الاحتمال.
فهذا ما يعن من أمثلة المناسب الغريب، وقد يتطرق نظر إلى بعض هذه الأمثلة
في إلحاقها بأجناسها. وغرضنا حاصل من تعريف الأجناس، ولا غرض في أعيان
الأمثلة.
فتحصل أن المعاني المناسبة تنقسم: إلى [مؤثرة، وهي: التي ظهر اعتبار
عينها] في عين الحكم المنظور فيه، وإلى ملائمة ليست مؤثرة، وهي: التي ظهر
اعتبار جنسها في جنس ذلك الحكم، وإلى غريبة: لم يظهر في [في الشرع] اعتبار
عينها، ولا اعتبار جنسها، وهي- مع ذلك -تناسب نوعا من المناسبة: تتميز به
عن الطرد الذي ينبو عن الحكم نبوة: لا يتقاضاه، ولا يتعلق به. فهذا بيان
تمييز الأجناس.
فأن قال قائل: ما ذكرتموه بيان انقسام المناسب - بالإضافة إلى ما يدل
PageV01P158
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Relation, affinity, suitability; a connection by which one thing is drawn toward another in proportion or correspondence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The intellectual congruence between a legal attribute and a ruling such that the attribute "calls for" (yastadʿī) the ruling in view of underlying purpose (maṣlaḥah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here as a technical term of uṣūl al-fiqh — not mere rhetorical congruity, but a real, mind-apprehensible suitability (munāsabah ʿaqliyyah) distinct from mere formal analogy (ṭard).
- Root: أ-ث-ر (a-th-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Trace, mark, effect; that which remains from something and indicates it.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, the proven efficacy (taʾthīr) of an attribute in producing a ruling — established by text (naṣṣ) or consensus (ijmāʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense: the attribute leaves its effect in the ruling. Metaphorical extension: the Lawgiver's designation of the attribute as the cause.
- Root: ل-أ-م (l-a-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be fitting, suitable, harmonious; to agree with something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Compatibility with the established patterns (jins) of the Lawgiver's rulings — that the meaning belongs to a genus already recognized in Sharīʿah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: harmony between parts. Technical: the attribute's genus has been shown effective in the genus of the ruling, even if not in the very same instance.
- Root: غ-ر-ب (gh-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be remote, strange, unfamiliar; that which departs from the known.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A suitable meaning whose genus has no precedent in the Lawgiver's rulings — hence weak and unreliable.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical: a stranger among the recognized categories; its suitability is admitted but its genus is unacknowledged.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-ʿāmil (Supplying the Governing Element) — In conditional and contrastive constructions (e.g., "if it were not for X, then Y"), the apodosis is governed by an implied operator; likewise, in distinguishing definitions (tamyīz al-aqsām), the predicate is understood through the governing term (al-mumayyiz) that separates each category by its defining property.
chapters.translation:
I say: The suitable (al-munāsib) is that which is effective (muʾaththir), and you may call the effective one "suitable" and "compatible" (mulāʾim) — loosely. For whatever is made a cause (ʿillah) for a ruling is made a cause only because the Lawgiver made it a cause, not because of its suitability per se. However, suitability may serve as an indicator (taʿrīf) and a pointer (tanbīh) to the Lawgiver's having made it a cause — according to some scholars. And once the Lawgiver's making it a cause is known, its efficacy (taʾthīr) is known; for there is no meaning of "efficacy" except the occurrence of the ruling from its effect and by its cause.

But since the meanings have been divided into three categories, we wished to single out each category — according to the terminology of the jurists — with a distinct, well-known expression. The purpose is only to define the aspect of distinction and division. Then, once you have understood this, let these expressions be taken as known signposts (aʿlām) for them. For expressions follow meanings and are leveled upon them; as for leveling meanings upon expressions — that is among the causes of confusion and the bringers of error. So we say: These ranks are clarified by giving examples.

As for the effective (al-muʾaththir), we have already mentioned its example.

As for the suitable (al-munāsib), its example is: the prohibition of wine (al-khamr), for its rationale appears in its being an intoxicant (muskir) that removes the intellect, so that nabīdh (date-wine) is measured against it. But in the Book, there occurs an allusion to this very meaning; so from this aspect it joins the effective — since the efficacy of this attribute has appeared by the text, where He alerted to its effecting enmity and hatred. However:

PageV01P145

Had the Qurʾān not alluded to this, and had it confined itself to mentioning the prohibition in its bare form — then its rationale by intoxication and removal of the intellect would be a rationale by a suitable meaning. And the meaning of its suitability is: this meaning's calling for this ruling from the aspect of benefit (maṣlaḥah), and its demanding it. For the intellect is the mainstay (mālāk) of the affairs of religion and this world. Its preservation is intended, and its loss is corruption. So it was prohibited for what is in it: of leading to corruption.

And this is clear, intelligible speech that can be established against the opponent. Where is this compared to the saying of Abū Zayd: that it reverts to the heart's acceptance and the soul's tranquility? And we do not doubt the distinction of this from the saying of one who says: it was prohibited for its foul, overpowering odor, or for its redness — for redness has no suitability to prohibition, nor does it call for it, nor does it demand it rationally. But this (intoxication) demands prohibition for what we have mentioned; so it is distinguished from mere formal analogy (ṭard) by the rational suitability between the meaning and the ruling.

And it is distinguished from the effective by saying: it has never been known in the Law, in another place — neither by text nor by consensus — that intoxication is effective in prohibition, such that the rationale by it would be a rationale by a meaning whose efficacy is known. And let us suppose the absence of the text's informing of the rationale by this cause, so that the analogy is blocked and it is cut off from the effective. For the one who argues by suitability claims independence from the text and from consensus indicating its being effective; and he claims that suitability suffices for the indication, as we shall mention the manner of obtaining knowledge through it.

Likewise, if we say: the group is killed for the one (whom they killed together), lest the oppressors take assistance as a pretext (dharīʿah) for killing enemies — that would be a rationale by a suitable, imaginative (mukhayyil) meaning whose aspect of calling for the ruling and demanding it has appeared in the intellect. And no evidence indicates its efficacy — neither from the text nor from consensus. Unlike the rationale by minority (al-ṣighar), for — along with its rational suitability — its efficacy has appeared in financial guardianship (al-wilāyah al-māliyyah) and guardianship of marriage — regarding the son — by agreement.

Likewise, if we say: the making-up (qaḍāʾ) of prayers is dropped for the menstruating woman, due to what is in it of hardship (ḥaraj), difficulty (mashaqqah), and burden (kulfah) with the repetition of prayer in the day and night — unlike the making-up of fasting — then this speech is suitable and imaginative, distinguished from its rationale by saying: fasting is made up because purity is not required in it, for example, unlike prayer. For this difference has no suitability, nor does it call for the ruling in the judgment of the intellect at all.

This is the exposition of the suitable. And it is not distinguished from the effective by its essence; rather, it is distinguished from the effective by the fact that there is no indication from the text or consensus of its being a cause — rather, there is no indication of it except its suitability. And what consensus indicates as being a cause and a reason may be suitable: like minority being suitable for guardianship, and the increase of specific closeness in kinship being suitable for preference (tarjīḥ) and advancement — and other examples that have preceded. And it may not be suitable: like the emission of pure semen being made a cause for the major ablution (ghusl) — and it has no suitability to it; likewise, touching the penis — the imagination of suitability in it is remote.

This is the aspect of distinguishing the suitable from the effective and from mere formal analogy.

As for distinguishing it from the compatible (al-mulāʾim), its aspect is: the suitable divides into what is compatible with the meanings of the Law and homogeneous with its acts in observing meanings — and into what is strange (gharīb): for which no genus is found. What the majority (al-jamāhīr) have held is: the suitable is not a cause except with the condition of compatibility, as we shall mention. And among them is one who sufficed with mere suitability and did not require compatibility. So every suitable meaning whose genus has been known in the acts of the Law is compatible; and what has not had its genus known is the strange suitable that has no parallel in the acts of the Law.

And here is a slippery slope (mazallah); for the observer may be confused about the difference between the compatible and the effective, and say: The effective is that which has been known in the Law as considered, as in minority; and the compatible is likewise. So what is the difference between one who stipulates efficacy and one who stipulates compatibility along with suitability?

We say: The difference between them is: the effective is that whose very essence (ʿaynuhu) has appeared effective in the very essence of the disputed ruling — by consensus or text, in the locus of dispute or outside it. Like the Ḥanafī's saying: the adult virgin (al-thayyib al-ṣaghīrah) is married for her minority; and he shows that the very essence of minority has appeared effective by consensus in guardianship regarding the son, and in guardianship of wealth. So the efficacy of the very essence of this meaning in the very essence of this ruling has appeared in another locus outside the locus of dispute; so that ruling itself — namely, guardianship — is transferred by that very cause — namely, minority — to the locus of dispute, namely, the adult minor. As for the compatible, we mean by it: that its genus has been known as effective in the genus of that ruling, even if its very essence has not been known as effective in the very essence of that ruling — in another locus.

Its example: when the dropping of the making-up of prayer is rationalized by hardship and burden, it is known that it is of the genus of the Law's meanings and compatible with it — since it has appeared, in general, that the Law drops a number of obligations by various kinds of burden: as in travel, illness, and others. But the efficacy of the very essence of the meaning in the very essence of the ruling has not appeared. Rather, the measure of the effective from such an origin is: that the Prophet — peace be upon him — PageV01P149 — for example, commanded ʿĀʾishah — may God be pleased with her — to make up the fasting missed during the days of menstruation, and to abandon the making-up of prayers. Then other women would be measured against her. Or He ruled it regarding the free woman, then the slave woman would be measured against her. Then it would flash forth to say: the efficacy of menstruation in dropping prayer has appeared regarding the free woman, so the very essence of this ruling is transferred by the very essence of this cause to the slave woman.

Likewise: if we rationalize the cessation of guardianship over the adult woman (al-thayyib) by the experience (al-mumārasah) she has obtained, and what the woman gains of testing, discernment, and guidance to objectives; and we transfer it to the adult minor — this would be suitable but strange. For it would be said: this is not of the genus of the Law's acts in establishing and cutting guardianship. We say: it is of its genus; for He — Mighty and Majestic — said: {«وَابْتَلُوا الْيَتَامَىٰ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَ فَإِنْ آنَسْتُم مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًا فَادْفَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ»} ("And test the orphans until they reach the age of marriage; then if you perceive in them sound judgment, deliver to them their wealth"). So He made the orphan's experience in wealth a cause; thus it becomes compatible. And this suitability with compatibility is at the utmost weakness, and it is not our purpose to examine this very issue; rather, the intent is the example, to know the genus.

Likewise, if we say: the Law restricted the sale of the four things in ribā (usury) by three conditions; and that was rationalized by the nutritive quality (ṭuʿm) indicating honor and inviolability (ḥurmah). For what is honored and respected has its path of acquisition narrowed, while what is held in contempt has its matter widened and is treated leniently; so its path is not narrowed — because what is guarded (al-maḍnūn bihi) rationally and legally is that whose need has appeared and whose inviolability has been magnified by it; and restriction by conditions is a blocking of some paths; and blocking some roads to something guarded by it.

This is a type of speech: in it is a kind of suitability, but it is strange; the opponent claims it does not comport with the Law's acts. We say: rather, the Law restricted the seeking of lawful sexual union (istiḥlāl al-buḍʿ) by conditions: like the dowry (ʿiwaḍ), the guardian (walī), and witnesses (shahādah); and distinguished it from wealth. So that was a showing of the honor of the pudendum, a singling out of it with the distinction of care, a disclosure of its danger and inviolability, and an indication that wealth is common in comparison to it, and that it (the pudendum) is preserved and guarded in comparison to wealth. So it has joined what has its genus known in the Law, and thus became compatible with its acts.

PageV01P151

And the way of the objector is: to show that the restriction of marriage by these conditions was not by this path, but rather was for the need of the pudendum for preservation to these conditions; and there is no need in the preservation of foods for these conditions. So he objects by this genus, and it is answered by its method. And our purpose is the example.

Likewise, if we say: the small amount that does not intoxicate — of nabīdh — is prohibited by analogy to the small amount of wine; and we rationalize the prohibition of the small amount of wine: that it is a caller (dāʿin) to the large amount; and that temperaments differ, and the amount that intoxicates each person in each state cannot be fixed; so the door is closed by the judgment of benefit — this would be suitable speech: in which nabīdh and wine are equal, and its compatibility with the Law's acts appears: by the Lawgiver's prohibiting seclusion with a foreign woman and looking at her, because it is a caller to fornication; and what runs in its course: of the Law's generalizing prohibition over the preliminaries of prohibited things and their callers. So it would be compatible, but not effective with the efficacy we defined earlier; for the efficacy of the very essence of the arousal of the drinking motive in prohibiting drinking has not appeared. Nor has the efficacy of the very essence of nutritive quality and its honor appeared in the ribā issue in stipulating equality and hand-to-hand exchange and immediacy; rather, the consideration of the genus of honor has appeared in the genus of restriction by conditions.

If it is said: What is the example of the strange suitable that is not compatible?

We say: Its examples rarely occur in the issues; for when meanings show their suitability, they are not free from the Law's attention to their genus in most cases. And what appears to us now of their examples are four:

The first example: what we mentioned: of rationalizing the dropping of compulsion (ijbār) over the adult woman by experience. For this — even if we counted it in the category of the compatible — is, in our view, of the strange suitable that has no parallel.

As for the testing of the orphan in disposition, that is not of this kind; rather, its parallel is: the son's intercourse with his wife; for that does not necessitate cutting compulsion over him: if he is a minor. Or its measure from wealth: when one partakes of a genus of food and tastes it and finds it good or finds it repugnant. And all of that is of no effect in cutting compulsion and dropping guardianship. And the testing of the orphan: to know his guidance to benefits, his separation from the motive of folly and waste and the stupidity of extravagance, and his preservation from being cheated and deceived; so that when that is known by testing him through buying and selling, the wealth is returned to him after the occurrence of puberty: which is the apparent cause in cutting guardianship. So its parallel is: that the woman be tested by selecting a husband from among husbands for marriage, and her states be observed in her proposals of the benefits of marriage and what is proposed upon her; so we yield to answering what benefit requires, and we resist what contradicts well-being (ghibṭah). And the like of that has no precedent in marriage; and the husband's touching her is not of this genus at all; rather, its parallel is: partaking of food and tasting it, wearing the garment, and riding the mount. So this remains a strange type of speech, and — while being strange — it is weak in itself. And likewise do strange meanings occur; for what appears and is strong is not devoid of the Law's attention to its genus, in most cases.

The second example: the rationalization of ribā in foodstuffs by the cause of nutritive quality; it too is of the strange meanings that do not comport with the Law's meanings. And what we mentioned — of showing compatibility by the matter of the pudendum — is weak; because the opponent does not concede the stipulation of the guardian. Yes: it was restricted by witnessing — either to preserve it from being lost by denial, or to distinguish it from illicit fornication (sifāḥ), which is an obscenity. And there is not in blocking the path of selling wheat for wheat in excess, or on credit, or without hand-to-hand exchange in the session — what preserves it from a loss it is exposed to, or distinguishes it from an obscenity it is on the verge of committing; so there is no homogeneity between them.

So that meaning remains — even if its suitability is conceded — strange, with no parallel in the Law.

And the reliance in the issue of the adult minor, and establishing thaybūbah (having been married) as a cause — is on the verbal addition (al-iḍāfah al-lafẓiyyah) derived from his saying — peace be upon him —: "The adult woman (al-thayyib) has more right to herself than her guardian." And in the ribā issue, and establishing nutritive quality as a cause — on his saying — peace be upon him —: "Do not sell food for food," as we have established in the book "Maʾākhidh al-Khilāf" and the book "Taḥṣīn al-Maʾākhidh" — and we have alerted to this weak path and the method of establishing it in these books.

The third example: the rationalization of some scholars of depriving the killer of inheritance, by his opposing the contrary of his intent (muʿāraḍatuhu bi-naqīḍ qaṣdihi): in hastening the right before its time.

And this — if it is not used in the context of punishment for his transgression — is a strange genre of meaning: for which no parallel is found.

And if it is said: killing is an offense (jināyah), and deprivation is a punishment; so it was attached to it for being an offense, and the minor and the insane are cut off from it — then that is of the kind of rationalization by the compatible meaning; for the efficacy of offenses in punishments and aggravations is well-known from the custom of the Law.

PageV01P155

And were the meaning of opposing the contrary of intent for hastening established, then the rationalization of some of our companions of the prohibition of vinegar produced by acetification (takhallul), by its opposing the contrary of his intent in hastening it — would be of the genus of the compatible; for it would become a known parallel in killing. But this meaning — in killing — is not established, nor is it sound upon examination (sabr) and investigation, nor is it safe from refutation (naqḍ). And our purpose is to strike examples, not the very issues themselves.

The fourth example of the strange suitable: the specification of ablution (wuḍūʾ) in its order: by advancing the face over the hands, and mentioning something wiped (mamsūḥ) between two washed things; until al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said: this is an alert that the order in this manner is intended; for were it not intended, this order would not be. And its specification by mention — with the occurrence of something wiped between two washed things — is more appropriate than its proceeding upon the order of creation: beginning with the head, descending to the face, and ending with the feet. And other such aspects of order.

PageV01P156

So al-Shāfiʿī is prevented from this inference, by saying: the cause of this order: the advancement of the face because it is the most important of the limbs in attaining cleanliness in it; and the delay of the feet because they are the most deserving of the limbs for distance from cleanliness, due to their mixing with dust in moving the feet, and the touching of the khuff (leather sock), and so on; so the hand and the head remain, and the advancement of the hand is more appropriate: for it is the instrument of grasping and is generally exposed; and the head is generally covered by the folds of the turban; and therefore its duty was lightened, namely: the wiping.

So this is a genre of speech that is suitable, distinguished from the saying of one who says: the face was advanced because it is round in shape, for example; and other such created attributes that recoil from the ruling.

Except that such meanings — even if suitable — are not relied upon; for the Law's observation of their genus has not been established, and estimation (taqdīr) expands in their likes, and their path is not narrowed in any manner. For were the order mentioned in reverse of the known: it would be possible to reverse this meaning, and it would be said: ablution is for prayer, and prayer occurs after it; so the washing of the face was delayed: because it is the most important of the limbs for cleanliness, so that the covenant with it — upon engaging in prayer — would be nearer. And were He to begin with the head, then the face, then the hand, then the foot: it would be possible to say: its cause is the order of creation. And were the hand advanced, it would be possible to say: its cause is cleaning the instrument first, so that other things are cleaned with it.

And the likes of these fancies (khayālāt) have a wide path, and are not relied upon.

Yes: they are useful in this context for repelling the inference by the verse; for the verse contains no formula indicating the obligation of order; rather, the inferrer relies in it on the specification of some parts by advancement and delay, and says: if it had no cause, then its cause is the obligation of advancement. So it is said: this is a possibility you have clung to, and these possibilities oppose it; so probability (iḥtimāl) enters upon it.

This is what occurs of the examples of the strange suitable. And a consideration may enter upon some of these examples in attaching them to their genera. And our purpose is attained by defining the genera, and there is no purpose in the very examples.

So it is established that the suitable meanings divide: into effective — which are those whose very essence has appeared considered in the very essence of the ruling under consideration; and into compatible that are not effective — which are those whose genus has appeared considered in the genus of that ruling; and into strange — for which neither their very essence nor their genus has appeared considered in the Law — and which, nonetheless, have a kind of suitability: by which they are distinguished from mere formal analogy (ṭard) that recoils from the ruling with a recoiling: it neither demands it nor attaches to it. This is the exposition of distinguishing the genera.

If someone says: What you have mentioned is an exposition of the division of the suitable — in addition to what indicates

### ||| CHECK تقسيم المناسب إلى ملائم وغريب وإمثلة كل حد المناسب وحقيقته

على اعتباره من تأثير، أو ملائمة، أو فقد التأثير والملائمة. فما حد
المناسب وحقيقته [وإلى ماذا يرجع حاصله] وما المعيار الذي يعرف به كون
المعنى مناسبا: إذا وقع فيه الشك للناظر، أو التنازع للمناظر؟
قلنا: المعاني المناسبة: ما تشير إلى وجوه المصالح وأماراتها. وفي إطلاق
لفظ المصلحة [أيضا] نوع إجمال؛ والمصلحة ترجع إلى جلب منفعة أو دفع مضرة.
والعبارة الحاوية لها: أن المناسبة ترجع على رعاية أمر مقصود.
أما المقصود، فينقسم: إلى ديني، وإلى دنيوي. وكل واحد ينقسم: إلى تحصيل،
وإبقاء. وقد يعبر عن التحصيل بجلب المنفعة. وقد يعبر عن الإبقاء: بدفع
المضرة. يعني: [أن] ما قصد بقاؤه: فانقطاعه مضرة، وإبقاءه دفع للمضرة.
فرعاية المقاصد عبارة حاوية للإبقاء ودفع القواطع، وللتحصيل على سبيل
الابتداء. وجميع أنواع المناسبات ترجع إلى رعاية المقاصد. وما انفك عن
رعاية أمر مقصود، فليس مناسبا. وما أشار إلى رعاية أمر مقصود، فهو:
المناسب.
PageV01P159
ثم الشيء ينبغي أن يكون مقصودا للشارع، حتى تكون رعايته مناسبة في أقيسة
الشرع. فقد علم - على القطع [28 - ب] أن حفظ النفس والعقل والبضع والمال،
مقصود في الشرع.
فجعل القتل سببا لإيجاب القصاص، لمعنى معقول مناسب، وهو: حفظ النفوس
والأرواح المقصود بقاؤها في الشرع، وعرف كونها مقصودة على القطع.
وحرم الشرع شرب الخمر: لأنه يزيل العقل؛ وبقاء العقل مقصود للشرع، لأنه
آلة الفهم وحامل الأمانة، ومحل الخطاب والتكليف.
والبضع مقصود الحفظ، لأن في التزاحم عليه اختلاط الأنساب، وتلطيخ الفراش،
وانقطاع التعهد عن الأولاد: لاستبهام الآباء: وفيه التوثب على الفروج
بالتشهي [والتغلب] وهي مجلبة الفساد والتقاتل.
والأموال مقصودة بالحفظ على ملاكها؛ عرف ذلك بالمنع من التعدي على حق
الغير، وإيجاب الضمان، ومعاقبة السارق بالقطع.
PageV01P160
