- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "relation, affinity, connection" — a thing's linkage to another by a shared attribute or purpose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic theology, al-munāsib denotes a meaning that points to a divine intent (maqṣūd) in legislation, serving as an indicator (amārah) of underlying wisdom.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for genealogical kinship; metaphorically (majāz) for any conceptual correspondence between a legal cause and its effect.
- Root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root signifies "soundness, rectitude, well-being" — the opposite of corruption (fasād).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah discourse, al-maṣlaḥah is the preservation of the five necessities (al-ḍarūriyyāt al-khams): religion, life, intellect, lineage, and property.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical soundness; technical for legal benefit, whether by securing an advantage (manfaʿah) or averting harm (maḍarrah).
- Root: ق-ص-د (q-ṣ-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "intention, aim, purpose" — the direction of one's resolve toward an objective.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Maqṣūd al-Shāriʿ is the divine objective in legislation, which the mujtahid seeks to discern through indicators.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical direction; metaphorical for teleological orientation in legal reasoning.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-ʿĀmil (Ellipsis of the Governing Element) — In the phrase "فما حد المناسب وحقيقته" the nominal predicate is governed by an implicit copula, requiring the reader to supply the elided operator for proper parsing.
chapters.translation:
I say: The appropriate meanings (al-maʿānī al-munāsibah) are those that point to the aspects of interests (wujūh al-maṣāliḥ) and serve as their indicators. In the unrestricted use of the term "interest" (al-maṣlaḥah), there is likewise a kind of ambiguity; for interest reduces to the attainment of a benefit (jalb manfaʿah) or the repulsion of a harm (dafʿ maḍarrah). The comprehensive expression encompassing both is: that appropriateness (al-munāsabah) reduces to the observance (riʿāyah) of an intended purpose (amr maqṣūd).

As for the intended purpose, it divides into the religious (dīnī) and the worldly (dunyawī). Each of these divides into attainment (taḥṣīl) and preservation (ibqāʾ). Attainment may be expressed as "securing a benefit," and preservation may be expressed as "repelling a harm." That is to say: what is intended to endure — its cessation is a harm, and its preservation is a repulsion of harm. Thus, the observance of purposes is a comprehensive expression encompassing preservation, the repulsion of what cuts them off (dafʿ al-qawāṭiʿ), and attainment in the manner of inception (ʿalā sabīl al-ibtidāʾ). All types of appropriateness reduce to the observance of purposes. Whatever is devoid of the observance of an intended purpose is not appropriate (munāsib). Whatever points to the observance of an intended purpose — that is the appropriate.

Then, the thing ought to be intended by the Lawgiver (maqṣūdan lil-Shāriʿ), so that its observance may be appropriate in the analogies of the Law (aqyisat al-Sharʿ). For it is known with certainty that the preservation of life (al-nafs), intellect (al-ʿaql), lineage (al-buḍʿ), and property (al-māl) is intended in the Law.

Thus, the Law made killing a cause (sabab) for the obligation of retaliation (qisāṣ), for a rational and appropriate meaning, namely: the preservation of lives and souls whose continued existence is intended in the Law; and it is known with certainty that they are intended.

The Law prohibited the drinking of wine because it removes the intellect; and the continued existence of the intellect is intended by the Law, for it is the instrument of understanding (ālat al-fahm), the bearer of the trust (ḥāmil al-amānah), and the locus of address and obligation (maḥall al-khiṭāb wa al-taklīf).

Lineage is intended for preservation, because in competition over it there is the mixing of genealogies (ikhtilāṭ al-ansāb), the soiling of the marriage-bed (talṭīkh al-firāsh), and the cessation of care for offspring due to the obscurity of fathers; and in it there is the assault upon private parts through lust and domination — which is a cause of corruption and mutual fighting.

Properties are intended for preservation on behalf of their owners; this is known by the prohibition of transgression against the right of another, the imposition of liability (ḍamān), and the punishment of the thief by amputation (qaṭʿ).

I say: The purposes of the Law (maqāṣid al-Sharʿ) are then ranked into three degrees: the necessities (al-ḍarūriyyāt), the needs (al-ḥājāt), and the improvements (al-taḥsīnāt). The necessities are those without which the interests of religion and world cannot be established — if they are lost, corruption prevails and order collapses. The needs are those sought to alleviate constriction (rafʿ al-ḥaraj) and remove hardship, though their absence does not reach the degree of total corruption. The improvements are those pursued for the sake of noble character (makārim al-akhlāq) and comely manners (maḥāsin al-ʿādāt), such that their neglect is not a cause of corruption but rather a departure from the path of excellence.

chapters.title_en: Healing the Thirst on Legal Causality — Section 27: The Hierarchy of Purposes (Maqāṣid) and the Degrees of Suitability (Munāsabah)
chapters.arabic_text:
وقد نبه الرب تعالى على مقصود القصاص، بقوله:} ولكم في القصاص حياة {،
ونبه على فساد الخمر، بقوله:} أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر
والميسر {. وهي من المضار والمحذورات  في أمور الدنيا؛ وقد يقترن به أيضا
مفسدة الدين.
و [قد] نبه على مصالح [الدين] في قوله في الصلاة:} إن الصلاة تنهى عن
الفحشاء والمنكر {. [وما يكف عن الفحشاء] فهو جامع لمصالح الدين، وقد تقترن
به مصلحة الدنيا أيضا.
فجميع المناسبات ترجع إلى رعاية المقاصد. إلا أن المقاصد تنقسم مراتبها:
فمنها: ما يقع في محل الضرورات؛ ويلتحق بأذيالها ما هو تتمة وتكملة لها.
ومنها: ما يقع في رتبة الحاجات؛ ويلتحق بأذيالها ما هو كالتتمة والتكملة لها.
ومنها: ما يقع في رتبة التوسعة والتيسير الذي لا ترهق إليه ضرورة، ولا
تمس إليه حاجة؛ ولكن تستفاد به رفاهية وسعة وسهولة؛ PageV01P161 # فيكون لذلك- أيضا -مقصودا في [هذه] الشريعة السمحة السهلة الحنيفية.
ويتعلق بأذيالها ولواحقها ما هو في حكم التحسين والتتمة لها. فتصير
الرفاهية مهيأة بتكميلاتها.
وتختلف مراتب المناسبات في الظهور، باختلاف هذه المراتب:
فأعلاها ما يقع في مراتب الضرورات؛ كحفظ النفوس، [فأنه مقصود الشارع،
وهو] من ضرورة الخلق، والعقول مشيرة إليه وقاضية به - لولا ورود الشرائع؛
وهو الذي لا يجوز انفكاك شرع عنه: عند من يقول بتحسين العقل وتقبيحه. ونحن
وأن قلنا: أن الله- سبحانه وتعالى -أن يفعل ما يشاء بعباده، وأنه لا يجب
عليه [رعاية] الصلاح - فلا ننكر إشارة العقول إلى جهة المصالح والمفاسد،
وتحذيرها المهالك، وترغيبها في جلب المنافع [والمقاصد] ولا ننكر أن الرسل
عليهم السلام بعثوا لمصالح الخلق في الدين والدنيا: رحمة من الله على الخلق
وفضلا؛ لا حتما ووجوبا عليه. قال الله تعالى:} وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة
للعالمين {، إلى غير ذلك: من الآيات الدالة عليه.
PageV01P162
وإنما نبهنا على هذا القدر، كي لا ننسب إلى اعتقاد الاعتزال، ولا ينفر
طبع المسترشد عن هذا الكلام: خيفة التضمخ بعقيدة مهجورة، يرسخ في نفوس أهل
السنة تهجينها.
فليعتقد- على هذا التأويل- أن العقول ترشد إلى الزجر عن القتل بالقصاص.
فكل مناسبة يرجع حاصلها إلى رعاية مقصود- يقع ذلك المقصود في رتبة يشير
العقل إلى حفظها، ولا يستغنى العقلاء عنها- فهو واقع في الرتبة القصوى في
الظهور.
مثاله: إيجابنا القصاص  بالمثقل محافظة على قاعدة الزجر [والردع] وإلحاقا
للمثقل بالجارح.
ومن قبيلة قولنا: الأيدي تقطع باليد الواحدة، كما تقتل النفوس بالنفس،
حسما لذريعة التوصل إلى الإهدار [29 - أ] بالتعاون [اليسير الهين على أخدان
الفساد وأقران السوء] فهذا فن واقع في الرتبة العليا PageV01P163 # لا غبار على مناسبتها؛ فأن كان يعترض عليها: فمن طريق آخر لا من طريق
المناسبة، وغرضنا ضرب [المثال] لبيان مراتب المناسبات.
ومن هذا الفن: تعليلنا تحريم شرب الخمر، بكونه مفسدا للعقل الذي هو ملاك
أمور الدنيا والدين. فهذا -أيضا- مما لا يجوز أن تنفك عنه عقول العقلاء،
ولا أن يخلو عنه شرع مهد بساطة لرعاية مصلحة الخلق في الدين والدنيا؛ فلم
تشتمل ملة قط على تحليل مسكر، وإن اشتملت على تحليل القدر الذي لا يسكر من
جنس المسكر.
وكذلك القول في مقصود البضع [والمال] وما يقع على هذه الرتبة.
وأمثال اللواحق بهذه المراتب والتتمة لها، كقولنا: إن المماثلة مرعية في
استيفاء القصاص؛ إذ عقل أن الزجر وتشفى الغيظ مقصود في أصل القتل مراعاته.
وتمامه: في رعاية المماثلة في التنكيل بالقاتل المتعدى كما فعل، والإحراق
إذا أحرق، والتغريق إذا غرق [وما يجري مجراه].
PageV01P164
ومثاله أيضا في الخمر: تحريم اليسير لكونه داعيا إلى الكثير، ومحركا لعطش
الشرب، وباعثا على الترقي إلى الحالة المطلوبة للنفوس: من الطرب والهزة؛
وتعديتنا ذلك إلى القليل من سائر المسكرات. فأصل المعنى فيه جلي، وهذا-
لاتصاله به، ووقوعه موقع التضبيب والتثمير لذلك الأمر المهم المقصود- وقع
ظاهرا لا سبيل إلى إنكار مناسبته. [ورجع حاصل] هذه المناسبات إلى رعاية
المقاصد.
أما مثال [المرتبة الثانية فإن] الواقع في محل الحاجة: تسليط الولي على
تزويج [الصغير والتزويج من الصغيرة]، فإن نصب القوام على الطفل- لحضانته
وصيانته، وإنفاق ماله عليه، PageV01P165 # [وشراء الطعام له، واستئجار من يقوم بمصلحته]- واقع في محل الضرورة؛ لأن
الحاجة إلى النفقة والحضانة [طبيعية] جبلية في حال الصغر؛ وفي الأعراض عنها
[سعى في هلاك الصبيان كلهم، وفيه هلاك النفوس وانقطاع الجنس، فهذا يقع موقع
الضرورة]، فأما تزويج الصغير، والتزويج منه- فلا ترهق إليه ضرورة،  ولا تمس
إليه حاجة ناجزة: من شهوة وتوفان؛ ولكن مصلحة المعيشة في العمر تنتظم بأمر
النكاح، والاتصال بالعشائر، والتكثر بالأصهار؛ والخاطب الكفء والكريمة
المرموقة إذا ظهر: فالمصلحة في تقييده قبل أن يفوت ولا يتفق الظفر بمثله،
فيقع ذلك في محل الحاجة. فصارت غبطة الصبي ومصلحته المستغنى عنها مقصودا من
جهة الشرع، كضرورته التي لا غنية له عنها؛ وصار رعاية هذا المقصود مناسبا،
كرعاية المقصود الضروري [وما يجرى الضروري]؛ والتحق بتلك الرتبة.
PageV01P166
ثم ما يجري مجرى التتمة لهذه الغبطة: كمراعاة الكفاءة، والمحافظة على مهر
المثل- على ما اختلف العلماء في وجوبه- يلتحق في المناسبة بالأصل؛ لأنه
كالتكملة والتتمة لرعاية هذه الغبطة، وإن كان الأصل الكلي من مقصود النكاح
لا يفوت به.
فنحن نستعمل هذا المعنى في منع الولي من النقصان عن مهر المثل، وفي منعه
من التزويج من غير كفء.
وأبو حنيفة وأن صحح النكاح من الأب من غير كفء، فليس يصححه لإنكار هذا
المعنى. بل يقول: تفويض الأمر إلى رأي الأب- وهو غير متهم: لشفقته وأبوته-
أولى؛ فلعله يتفطن لغبطة خفية؛ توازي غبطة الكفاءة وتزيد عليها.
فأصل المعنى لا سبيل إلى جحده، وهو يستعمل أصل المعنى في الثيب الصغيرة،
ويقول: تزويجها من مصلحة المعيشة، فلا يعطل، وكذلك في اليتيمة التي ليس لها
أب ولا جد، كما في غير اليتيمة، وكما في البكر؛ ويعلل بالصغر، ويبدي فيه
وجه المناسبة [29 - ب] كما ذكرناه.
PageV01P167
وهو بين لا يعترض عليه من حيث القدح في هذه المناسبة؛ بل يعترض من وجه
آخر. ويرجع منشأ النزاع إلى التردد في محل استعمال هذه المعاني، على ما
نذكره في هذه المسائل.
ثم للشرع -في هذا الجنس- نوع تصرف -فلا ينبغي أن نغفل عنه- وهو: إدارة
الحكم على أمارة المصلحة من غير تتبع وجه المصلحة؛ فإن مصلحة الصبي لحاجته
إلى قوام، وحاجته لصغره وضعف عقله؛ وقد يقوى عقله عند مراهقة البلوغ؛ ولكن
يقطع الشرع غمة الأشكال عن أطراف الأحوال، بإتباع الصغر الذي هو أمارة
المصلحة [غالبا؛ فيدار الحكم مرة على عين المصلحة، وأخرى على  أمارة
المصلحة]. وكل ذلك من نظر الشرع. وفي إتباع الأمارة -أيضا- نوع مناسبة،
وهو: عصر الوقوف على عين الحاجة؛ كما [أديرت الرخص] على السفر لا على عين
المشقة، وأديرت الولاية على القرابة لا على الشفقة؛ فأنها لا يوقف عليها.
وإنما الغرض التنبيه على مراتب المناسب، وأن حاصل جملتها يرجع إلى رعاية
المقاصد؛ وأن المقصود قد يقع في محل الحاجة، وقد يقع في محل الضرورة؛ وقد
يعلم كونها مقصودا من جهة الشرع على القطع، وقد يظن ذلك. [وكل ذلك] من طرق
المناسبات.
PageV01P168
المرتبة الثالثة: ما لا يرجع إلى ضرورة، ولا إلى حاجة؛ ولكن يقع موقع
التحسين والتزيين، والتوسعة والتيسير؛ للمزايا والمراتب، ورعاية أحسن
المناهج في العبادات والمعاملات، والحمل على مكارم الأخلاق، ومحاسن
العادات.
ومثال ذلك: حكم الشرع بسلب العبد أهلية الشهادة، وليس إلى سلب أهليته
حاجة ولا ضرورة. ولو قبلت شهادته في حال العدالة: [لكان ذلك] كقبول فتواه
وروايته؛ ولكن: لما كان الرقيق نازل القدرة والرتبة، ضعيف الحال والمنزلة؛
بإثبات يد الاستيلاء [عليه] والتسخير؛ وكانت الشهادة ونفوذها على الغير
منصبا عليا ومقاما سنيا- لم يكن ذلك لائقا بحاله.
فيفهم مقصود الشرع -في سلبه الأهلية- على هذا الوجه؛ ففيه نوع مناسبة
تتميز عن قول القائل: أنه لا تقبل شهادته، لأنه لا تجب عليه الجمعة مثلا
كالصبي؛ فإن سقوط التكليف بالجمعة لا ينبئ بحال عن سقوط أهلية الشهادة؛
بخلاف ما ذكرناه.
PageV01P169
ولو قال قائل، هي ولاية: فلم يكن من أهلها كالولايات- قيل: ولم لم يكن من
أهل الولايات، ولا ينسب لها؟ إلا أن تكفل شغل الخلق بولاية القضاء، وتكفل
شغل الأولاد بأنواع التفقد- شغل شاغل: يستدعى فراغا واهتماما مصروفا إليه؛
والعبد مستغرق الأوقات بوظائف الخدمة. وهذا المعنى لا يطرد في الشهادة:
فأنها كالرواية؛ إذ يرجع حاصلها إلى الأخبار عن المعلوم. ولو استقام
التعليل بهذا النوع: لالتحق بالرتبة السابقة، كتعليل سلب الولاية [به].
وكذلك قيد الشرع صحة النكاح [بشرط] الشهادة؛ ولو صح على السبر تخيل مقصود
الإثبات عند الجحود: لالتحق بالرتبة الثانية، ولوقع في مظان الحاجة، ولكن:
ليس يستقيم  الاستغناء عن الأشهاد على رضاء المرأة، مع أن النكاح لا يثبت
إلا PageV01P170 # عليها؛ فيتخيل [إذن] أن المقصود من حضور الشهود: تمييز النكاح بالإعلان
[والإظهار] عن السفاح.
ثم مراتب الظهور تضطرب؛ فضبط الشرع ما فيه -من الحيط- بشهادة شخصين لهما
أهلية الشهادة، حتى يكون للإظهار عليهما وقع. فهذا أمر لا حاجة إليه، وإنما
يجرى التحسين للأمور.
وكذلك قيد النكاح بالولي؛ ولو أمكن تعليله بكون المرأة في منظنة
الغباوة-[لقصور العقل والنظر] ووفور الشهوة، والمبادرة إلى سوء الاختيار،
بأنواع الخداع والاغترار لوقع هذا [30 - أ] المناسب في الرتبة السابقة،
ولكن: لا يستتب ذلك في [سلب] عبارتها ولا في التزويج من الكفء، فيقال في
تعليله: لو ثبت ذلك بنص مثلا: [لكان] اللائق بذوات المروءات الحياء
والانزواء عن مباشرة النكاح، ففيه إظهار الشبق، والمجاهرة بالتشوف إلى
الرجال؛ والشرع يحمل على محاسن الأخلاق؛ وفي مباشرتها النكاح بنفسها ما
يناقض ذلك، فنقدر محاسن الأخلاق مقصودا من جهة الشرع، ونقدر الاستقلال
مناقضا له، فيتراآى منه نوع من المناسبة.
PageV01P171
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ص-ص (qa-ṣād-ṣād)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To follow, to trace, to cut evenly; qiṣāṣ = retributive equivalence in kind, exacting the same measure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal retaliation as a divinely ordained equalization, preserving life through deterrence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "cutting" (qaṣṣ) extended metaphorically to "retaliation" — the cutting off of the criminal's act by exact equivalence.
- Root: ض-ر-ر (ḍād-rā-rā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Harm, injury, distress; ḍarūrah = necessity, a state of compelling need.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The five necessities (al-ḍarūriyyāt) — faith, life, intellect, lineage, property — whose preservation is the ultimate purpose of revelation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḍarūrah as literal "compulsion" (iljāʾ); metaphorically, the rank of necessity in legal causality — that without which life cannot be ordered.
- Root: ح-ا-ج (ḥā-alif-jīm)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Need, want, lack; ḥājah = a need whose absence causes hardship but not destruction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The second rank of maqāṣid — needs (ḥājiyyāt) that alleviate difficulty, distinguished from necessities.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "want" (iftaqara); metaphorically, the legal category of "need" as a middle rank between necessity and luxury.
- Root: ت-ح-س-ن (tā-ḥā-sīn-nūn)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To beautify, to deem good; taḥsīn = embellishment, the third rank of purposes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taḥsīniyyāt — commendable refinements that perfect character and worship, neither necessary nor needful.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "beautification" of an object; metaphorically, the legal principle of "deeming good" (taḥsīn) as a source of suitability.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When the author lists ranks (ضرورة، حاجة، توسعة), each term is in apposition to the preceding, clarifying the hierarchy without redundancy; the particle "فـ" (fa) marks sequential consequence, binding each rank to its attendant completions (تتمة وتكملة).
chapters.translation:
I say — and God is the Giver of success:

The Lord — exalted be He — has drawn attention to the purpose of retaliation (qiṣāṣ) by His saying: {«And in retaliation there is life for you»} (Q 2:179). And He drew attention to the corruption of wine by His saying: {«to cast between you enmity and hatred through wine and gambling»} (Q 5:91). These are among the harms and prohibitions in the affairs of this world; and there may also be conjoined with them a corruption of religion.

And He — exalted — drew attention to the interests of religion in His saying concerning prayer: {«Indeed, prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing»} (Q 29:45). Whatever restrains from immorality is comprehensive of the interests of religion, and there may also be conjoined with it a worldly interest.

Thus all suitable causes (munāsabāt) reduce to the observance of purposes (maqāṣid). Yet the purposes are divided into ranks:

Among them is that which falls in the station of necessities (ḍarūrāt); and attached to their tails is what is a completion and perfection of them.

Among them is that which falls in the rank of needs (ḥājāt); and attached to their tails is what is like a completion and perfection of them.

Among them is that which falls in the rank of expansion and facilitation (tawsīʿah wa-taysīr) — to which no necessity compels, nor does any need touch it; but through it is derived comfort, breadth, and ease. [Page V01P161] Thus this too becomes a purpose in this tolerant, easy, ḥanīfī sacred law. And attached to its tails and appendages is what is in the category of embellishment (taḥsīn) and completion of it. So comfort becomes prepared through its perfections.

The ranks of suitability differ in evidentness (ẓuhūr) according to the difference of these ranks:

The highest of them is what falls in the ranks of necessities — like the preservation of lives, for it is a purpose of the Lawgiver, and it is from the necessity of creation; the intellects point to it and judge by it — were it not for the advent of the revealed laws. It is that which no sacred law can be free from: according to those who affirm the intellect's deeming good and deeming bad (taḥsīn wa-taqbīḥ). And we — even though we say that God — glorified and exalted be He — does what He wills with His servants, and that observance of what is right (ṣalāḥ) is not obligatory upon Him — we do not deny the intellects' indication toward the direction of interests and harms, nor their warning against perils, nor their inclining toward the attraction of benefits and purposes. Nor do we deny that the Messengers — peace be upon them — were sent for the interests of creation in religion and this world: as a mercy from God upon creation and a favor — not as an obligation and necessity upon Him. God — exalted — said: {«And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds»} (Q 21:107), and other verses indicating this.

[Page V01P162]

We have only drawn attention to this much, so that we are not attributed to the belief of the Muʿtazilah, nor does the temperament of the seeker of guidance recoil from this discourse — fearing the smearing with an abandoned creed whose vilification is entrenched in the souls of the Ahl al-Sunnah.

Let him believe — on this interpretation — that the intellects guide toward deterrence from killing through retaliation (qiṣāṣ). So every suitable cause whose outcome reduces to the observance of a purpose — that purpose falling in a rank which the intellect points to preserving, and which the rational cannot do without — it falls in the highest rank of evidentness.

Its example: our making retaliation obligatory with the heavy instrument (al-muthqal), preserving the principle of deterrence and repulsion, and annexing the heavy instrument to the cutting one.

And from this kind is our saying: hands are cut for the single hand, just as lives are taken for the single life — blocking the means (sadd al-dharīʿah) to reaching the nullification of blood [29-A] through easy and slight cooperation with companions of corruption and peers of evil. This is a kind falling in the highest rank [Page V01P163] — no dust upon its suitability. If it is objected to, then from another avenue, not from the avenue of suitability. And our purpose is to strike an example for clarifying the ranks of suitability.

And from this kind: our causal explanation of the prohibition of drinking wine — that it corrupts the intellect, which is the mainstay (mālāk) of the affairs of this world and religion. This too is that which the intellects of the rational cannot be free from, nor can any sacred law that has laid its carpet for the observance of the interest of creation in religion and this world be devoid of it. No creed (millah) has ever comprised the legalization of an intoxicant, even if it comprised the legalization of the amount that does not intoxicate from the genus of intoxicants.

And likewise the saying concerning the purpose of the private parts (buḍʿ) and wealth, and what falls in this rank.

And examples of the appendages to these ranks and their completions — like our saying: equivalence (mumāthalah) is observed in the exacting of retaliation (qiṣāṣ); for it is understood that deterrence and the soothing of rage are purposes in the original killing to be observed. And its completion: in the observance of equivalence in the punishment of the transgressing killer — as he did, burning if he burned, drowning if he drowned [and what runs its course].

[Page V01P164]

And its example also in wine: the prohibition of the small amount for being a caller to the large amount, a mover of the thirst of drinking, and a driver toward ascending to the state desired by souls: of joy and elation. And our extending that to the small amount of all other intoxicants. The root meaning therein is evident; and this — for its connection to it, and its falling in the position of strengthening and fructifying that important intended matter — has fallen evident, with no way to deny its suitability. [And the outcome] of these suitable causes reduces to the observance of purposes.

As for the example of the second rank — that which falls in the station of need: the guardian's empowerment to marry the minor [and to give the minor in marriage]. For the appointment of a caretaker over the child — for his custody and protection, and the spending of his wealth upon him, [Page V01P165] [and the purchasing of food for him, and the hiring of one who undertakes his interest] — falls in the station of necessity; for the need for expenditure and custody is natural, innate, in the state of childhood. And in neglecting them [is striving toward the destruction of all children, and in it is the destruction of lives and the cutting off of the species — so this falls in the position of necessity]. As for marrying the minor, and giving the minor in marriage — no necessity compels to it, nor does any immediate need touch it: of desire or passion. But the interest of livelihood in one's lifetime is ordered by the matter of marriage, and connection with clans, and multiplication through in-laws. And if a suitable suitor and a noble, sought-after woman appear: the interest lies in binding her before she slips away and the like of her cannot be obtained — so this falls in the station of need. Thus the child's advantage (ghibṭah) and his dispensable interest become a purpose from the direction of the Law, like his necessity which he cannot do without. And the observance of this purpose becomes suitable, like the observance of the necessary purpose [and what runs the course of the necessary]; and it annexes itself to that rank.

[Page V01P166]

Then what runs the course of the completion of this advantage — like the observance of suitability (kafāʾah), and the preservation of the equivalent dowry (mahr al-mithl) — upon the scholars' disagreement over its obligation — annexes itself in suitability to the origin; for it is like the completion and perfection of the observance of this advantage, even if the universal origin of the purpose of marriage is not lost by it.

So we employ this meaning in preventing the guardian from reducing below the equivalent dowry, and in preventing him from marrying [the ward] to a non-suitable (ghayr kufʾ).

And Abū Ḥanīfah — even if he validates the marriage by the father to a non-suitable — does not validate it out of denial of this meaning. Rather he says: delegating the matter to the father's opinion — who is not accused, for his compassion and paternity — is more appropriate; perhaps he perceives a hidden advantage that equals the advantage of suitability and exceeds it.

So the root meaning cannot be denied, and he employs the root meaning in the case of the minor woman who has been previously married (al-thayyib al-ṣaghīrah), saying: her marriage is from the interest of livelihood, so it is not suspended. And likewise in the case of the orphan who has neither father nor grandfather, as in the non-orphan, and as in the virgin. And he causally explains by minority, and displays therein the face of suitability [29-B] as we have mentioned.

[Page V01P167]

It is evident, not objected to from the angle of impugning this suitability; rather it is objected to from another angle. And the origin of the dispute reduces to hesitation over the locus of employing these meanings, as we shall mention in these questions.

Then for the Law — in this genus — there is a kind of disposition (taṣarruf) — and we ought not be heedless of it — namely: the rotation of the ruling upon the indicator (amārah) of the interest without tracing the very face of the interest. For the child's interest is due to his need for a caretaker, and his need is due to his minority and the weakness of his intellect. And his intellect may strengthen at the threshold of puberty; but the Law cuts off the gloom of ambiguity from the edges of the states by following minority, which is the indicator of the interest [predominantly]. So the ruling rotates once upon the very interest, and another time upon the indicator of the interest. And all of that is from the consideration of the Law. And in following the indicator — also — there is a kind of suitability, namely: the closure of stopping upon the very need; just as [the concessions (rukhaṣ) were rotated] upon travel, not upon the very hardship; and guardianship was rotated upon kinship, not upon compassion — for it cannot be stopped upon.

And the purpose is only to draw attention to the ranks of the suitable (al-munāsib), and that the outcome of their entirety reduces to the observance of purposes; and that the purpose may fall in the station of need, and may fall in the station of necessity; and it may be known that it is a purpose from the direction of the Law with certainty, and it may be conjectured. [And all of that] is from the avenues of suitability.

[Page V01P168]

The third rank: what does not reduce to a necessity, nor to a need; but falls in the position of embellishment (taḥsīn) and adornment (tazyīn), and expansion and facilitation — for the excellences and ranks, and the observance of the best paths in acts of worship (ʿibādāt) and transactions (muʿāmalāt), and the urging toward noble character traits (makārim al-akhlāq) and praiseworthy customs.

And its example: the Law's ruling to strip the slave of the eligibility for testimony (shahādah). There is no need nor necessity to strip his eligibility. And if his testimony were accepted in a state of uprightness (ʿadālah): [that would be] like the acceptance of his legal opinion (fatwā) and his narration (riwāyah). But: since the slave is low in capacity and rank, weak in condition and station — by the establishment of the hand of domination over him and subjugation; and since testimony and its execution over others is a lofty office and an exalted station — it was not fitting to his condition.

So the Law's purpose — in stripping his eligibility — is understood on this face; in it there is a kind of suitability that distinguishes itself from the saying of one who says: his testimony is not accepted because, for example, the Friday prayer is not obligatory upon him, like the minor. For the falling of the obligation of Friday does not indicate in any way the falling of the eligibility for testimony; unlike what we have mentioned.

[Page V01P169]

And if someone said: it is a guardianship (wilāyah), and he was not of its people, like the guardianships — it would be said: and why was he not of the people of guardianships, nor attributed to them? Except that the undertaking of the people's affairs by the guardianship of the judiciary, and the undertaking of the children's affairs by various kinds of supervision — is an occupying occupation: it demands free time and attention directed to it. And the slave's times are entirely consumed by the duties of service. And this meaning does not run consistently in testimony: for it is like narration; since its outcome reduces to informing about what is known. And if the causal explanation by this kind were sound: it would annex itself to the previous rank, like the causal explanation of the stripping of guardianship by it.

And likewise the Law restricted the validity of marriage [by the condition] of testimony. And if it were valid upon examination (al-sabr) to imagine the purpose of proof at the time of denial: it would annex itself to the second rank, and would fall in the locus of need. But: it is not sound to dispense with the witnesses upon the woman's consent, given that marriage is not established except [Page V01P170] upon her. So it is imagined [then] that the purpose of the presence of witnesses: the distinguishing of marriage by public announcement [and manifestation] from fornication (sifāḥ).

Then the ranks of evidentness fluctuate; so the Law regulated what is in it — of circumspection — by the testimony of two persons possessing the eligibility for testimony, so that upon them the announcement has weight. This is a matter with no need for it; it only runs the course of embellishment of affairs.

And likewise the Law restricted marriage by the guardian (walī). And if it were possible to causally explain it by the woman being in the locus of foolishness — [for the deficiency of intellect and discernment], the abundance of desire, and the hastening toward bad choice, through various kinds of deception and delusion — this [30-A] suitable would fall in the previous rank. But: that does not hold steady in [the stripping of] her expression (ʿibārah), nor in the marriage to the suitable. So it is said in its causal explanation: if that were established by a text, for example: [then] the fitting thing for women of honor (dhawāt al-murūʾāt) would be modesty and withdrawal from directly undertaking marriage; for in it there is the display of lust, and the open craving toward men. And the Law urges toward noble character traits; and in her directly undertaking marriage herself there is what contradicts that. So we posit noble character traits as a purpose from the direction of the Law, and we posit her independence as contradicting it — so there appears from it a kind of suitability.

[Page V01P171]

chapters.title_en: Division of the Appropriate (Munāsib) into Rational-Real and Persuasive-Imaginal
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| CHECK تقسيم المناسب إلى حقيقي عقلي، وخيالي إقناعي

لهذا وأمثاله أمثلة المناسبات الواقعة في الرتبة الأخيرة؛ فأنها من أضعف
درجات المناسبات. وسنذكر المحل الذي يجوز الاعتماد فيه على [مثل هذا
المعنى]، والموضع الذي لا يعتمد فيه على أمثال هذه المعاني.
ومن خاصية هذه الرتبة [أن تغلب فيها المناسبات] الخيالية الإقناعية.
وعلى الجملة، المناسب ينقسم: إلى حقيقي عقلي، وإلى خيالي إقناعي.
فأما الحقيقي العقلي، فما بيناه في الرتبتين السابقتين، وهو الذي لا يزال
يزداد- على البحث [والتنقير] والسبر- وضوحا، ويرتقى -بمزيد التأمل- إلى شكل
العقليات.
وأما الخيالي الإقناعي، فهو: الذي يخيل في الابتداء مناسبته، فيقطع عن
الطرد الذي ينبو عن المخيل؛ وإذا سلط عليه البحث، وسدد إليه النظر- ينحل
حاصله، وينكشف عن غير طائل.
مثاله: تعليل الشافعي في تحريم بيع الخمر والميتة والعذرة بنجاستها،
وقياس الكلب والسرقين وسائر النجاسات العينية عليه، PageV01P172 # ووجه المناسبة في النجاسة: أن حكم الشرع بنجاسته أمر باجتنابه، وإشارة
إلى استقذاره، والتجنب عن مخالطته؛ ففي الإقدام على بيعه، ومقابلته بالمال،
وإيجاب الضمان على  متلفه- إقامة وزن له يناقض ما علم: من خسته بتنجيس الشرع إياه.
فهذا الفن واقع في الرتبة الأخيرة؛ اذ لا يتعلق بالمنع من بيعه حاجة ولا
ضرورة؛ ولكن: يقدر أن في الإقدام على بيعه -بعد تنجيس الشرع إياه- ما يناقض
محاسن العادات، وتستوي في هذه القضية سائر النجاسات.
والمعنى بكون خياليا إقناعيا، أن الحاذق يسلط البحث على هذا الكلام،
فيقول: هذه ألفاظ جملية ركبت وخيل من مجموعها مناسبة؛ وإذا جرد النظر إلى
المعنى في حقيقته وإلى الحكم، انتفت المناسبة. إذ معنى نجاسته: أن الصلاة
لا تصح معه لا المنع من استعماله] لنجاسته [و] الكف عن [مخامرته؛ فالانتفاع
بالنجاسات جائز بالاتفاق؛ ومعنى البيع: نقل الاختصاص ببدل. ولا مناسبة بين
بطلان الصلاة باستصحابه، PageV01P173 # وبين المنع من بيعه. فبهذا ينكشف الغطاء، وتنقطع المناسبة. ولا تزال
تزداد المناسبة خفاء واندراسا بالبحث. ولكن على الجملة: ليس يبعد -في نظر
الشرع- أن يمنع من بيعه: تأكيدا لتنجيسه والكف عن مخامرته.
ومثال هذه الاقناعات قد يوجد في الشرع معتبرا، ولكن قد يعتقد اعتباره:
إذا دل عليه مسلك نقلي، أما مجرد هذه المناسبة، فربما] لا يجري على دعوى
التعليل.
وكذلك إذا قلنا: تحريم الربا في الأشياء الأربعة سببه: الطعم وحرمته،
تضييقا لطريق التحصيل فيما عز في نفسه؛ فان ما يعز لا ينال إلا بنوع تكلف،
وتجثم شروط ومضائق؛ وما سقط حرمته لم يضيق طريقه، بل سهل مناله -كان هذا
كلاما إقناعا ضعيفا، ينكشف، -بالبحث- عن غير طائل، إذا يقال: العزيز
المحترم يصان عن الإتلاف بالإسراف والتضيع؛ فأما أن يصان عن التحصيل بطريق
التملك -فلا؛ بل يمهد إليه طريق التملك، ويوسع مسلكه لشدة الحاجة إليه.
PageV01P174
وكذلك إذا قلنا: إن العبد لا يلي أمر ولده، لأنه مولى عليه، ويتناقض] أن
[يكون الشخص الواحد وليا] و [موليا عليه -خيل هذا الكلام في مبدأ الأمر
مناسبة، ولكن ينحل تعقيده] 30 - ب [بأن يقال: المتناقض أن يكون وليا فيما
هو مولى عليه، فإنها تلي أمورا ويولى عليها في عقد النكاح. فيرجع حاصله إلى
أنه المرء بنفسه ثم  بمن يعول، وهو ليس متفرغا لنفسه، فكيف يلي غيره. فيرجع
إلى أمر إقناعي: ما لم يذكر وجه تضرر المولى بسبب اشتغال العبد، واستغراقه
الأوقات بوظائف خدمة السيد.
فهذه أمثلة هذه المناسبات على تفاوت الدرجات.
وطريق تركيب الاقناعيات] هو [اقتباس قضايا جملية من أسباب معينة، وبناء
الغرض عليها، فنقتبس من النجاسات قضية PageV01P175 # جميلة، وهي: الحقارة والخساسة. ونقتبس- من الإقدام على البيع، والمقابلة
بالمال- قضية جملية، وهي: تشريف، وإقامة وزن، وإثبات قدر. ثم ينشأ التنافي
من القضيتين الجمليتين.
وكذلك نقتبس من وصف الطعم حرمة تنبئ عن عزة ومزية، وهي قضية جملية.
ونقتبس من التحصيل بجميع الطرق، من غير تضييق ومزيد اعتناء- قضية جملية،
وهي: التساهل والتهاون به؛ ونتخيل تنافيا بين القضيتين: فتنتظم منه
المناسبة، وهي: المحافظة على القضية المقصودة الثانية، بنفي ما يناقضها.
وكذلك نقتبس من رق العبد نوع ذلة وصغار ومهانة؛ ومن قبول الشهادة علو
منصب وارتفاع قدر. ونتخيل بينهما تنافيا. فلو رفعت هذه القضايا الجملية
التي استثمرت من القضايا المعينة الخاصة، ونسبت القضايا الخاصة بعضها إلى
بعض -لم تتناسب، وهي قول القائل: لا تصح الصلاة معه فيبطل بيعه؛ وهو مطعوم
يحتاج إليه فيجب فيه القبض في المجلس، ويحرم] فيه [النساء والفضل؛ ومملوك
فلا يصدق في قوله مع العدالة.
وهذه الأمور لا تناسب بأنفسها، وتناسب بقضاياها الجميلة.
فسبيل حل هذه التعقيدات تفصيل ما أجمله المخيل: من القضايا،
PageV01P176
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of relation, affinity, and proportional connection between two things.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, the munāsib is that attribute which serves as a plausible ratio legis (ʿillah) for a ruling, indicating divine wisdom.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for genealogical or causal relation; metaphorically for the perceived suitability of an attribute to a legal effect.
- Root: خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To imagine, fancy, or conjure an image in the mind.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The faculty of estimation (wahm) producing a semblance of suitability without rational demonstration.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of visual illusion; metaphorical for rhetorical persuasion that mimics demonstrative proof.
- Root: ق-ن-ع (q-n-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To satisfy, convince, or content with a sufficient proof.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dialectical (jadalī) persuasion that falls short of apodictic certainty (yaqīn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: contentment with sufficiency; rhetorical: the art of plausible argumentation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-jumal (Ellipsis and Reconstruction) — The syntactic parsing of complex periodic sentences requires reconstructing elided elements to expose the underlying logical structure, as Ghazali does when dissecting the "composite propositions" (qaḍāyā jumaliyyah).
chapters.translation:
I say: For this and its like are examples of the appropriate (munāsabāt) occurring in the final rank; for they are among the weakest degrees of appropriateness. We shall mention the locus where reliance upon such a meaning is permissible, and the place where reliance upon such meanings is not permissible.

And from the specific property of this rank is that persuasive-imaginal (khayālī iqnāʿī) appropriateness predominates therein. In sum, the appropriate (al-munāsib) divides into: rational-real (ḥaqīqī ʿaqlī) and persuasive-imaginal (khayālī iqnāʿī).

As for the rational-real, it is what we have elucidated in the two preceding ranks — that which, upon investigation, scrutiny, and probing (sabr), only increases in clarity, and ascends — with greater reflection — to the form of rational demonstrations (shakl al-ʿaqliyyāt).

As for the persuasive-imaginal, it is that which at the outset appears to be appropriate, so that it cuts off from the mere formal analogy (ṭard) that recoils from the imaginal (mukhīl); but when investigation is brought to bear upon it, and the gaze is directed toward it, its content dissolves and it is exposed as yielding nothing of substance.

Its example: al-Shāfiʿī's (may Allah have mercy on him) reasoning for the prohibition of selling wine, carrion, and filth on account of their impurity (najāsah), and his analogizing the dog, dung, and all other intrinsic impurities to that. The aspect of appropriateness in impurity is: that the Law's ruling of its impurity is a command to avoid it, an indication of its being deemed filthy (istiqzār), and the avoidance of mixing with it. Thus, in proceeding to sell it, exchanging it for wealth, and obligating compensation (ḍamān) upon its destroyer — there is an establishment of weight for it that contradicts what is known of its baseness, by the Law's rendering it impure.

So this kind falls in the final rank; for no need (ḥājah) or necessity (ḍarūrah) attaches to the prohibition of its sale. Rather, it is merely estimated that in proceeding to sell it — after the Law's rendering it impure — there is something that contradicts the noble customs (maḥāsin al-ʿādāt). And all other impurities are equal in this matter.

The meaning of its being "persuasive-imaginal" is that the skilled investigator directs his inquiry upon this discourse and says: These are composite expressions (alfāẓ jumaliyyah) from whose totality an appropriateness has been imagined; but when the gaze is stripped down to the meaning in its reality and to the ruling, the appropriateness is negated. For the meaning of its impurity is: that prayer is not valid with it — not the prohibition of its use for its impurity, nor the abstention from mixing with it; for benefiting from impurities is permissible by consensus. And the meaning of sale is: the transfer of exclusive right (ikhtiṣāṣ) in exchange for a substitute. And there is no appropriateness between the invalidity of prayer by its accompaniment and the prohibition of its sale. By this the veil is lifted, and the appropriateness is severed. And the appropriateness only continues to increase in hiddenness and effacement upon investigation. But in sum: it is not far — in the view of the Law — to prohibit its sale: as a reinforcement of its being rendered impure and the abstention from mixing with it.

And examples of such persuasions may be found in the Law as considered (muʿtabar), but its being considered may be believed only if a transmitted path (maslak naqlī) indicates it. As for the mere appropriateness itself, perhaps it does not proceed upon the claim of causal explanation (taʿlīl).

Likewise, if we say: The prohibition of ribā in the four things has as its cause: being a foodstuff (ṭuʿm) and its inviolability (ḥurmah) — as a constriction of the path of acquisition for what is precious in itself; for what is precious is not attained except with a kind of exertion, and the accumulation of conditions and straits; and what has fallen from inviolability has not had its path constricted, but rather its attainment facilitated — this would be a weak persuasive discourse, which is exposed — upon investigation — as yielding nothing of substance. For it would be said: The precious and inviolable is protected from destruction by extravagance and waste; but as for its being protected from acquisition by the path of ownership — no; rather, the path of ownership is paved for it, and its passage is widened, due to the severity of need for it.

Likewise, if we say: The slave does not manage the affair of his child, because he is himself under guardianship (mawlā ʿalayh), and it is contradictory that one and the same person be both guardian (walī) and ward (mawlā ʿalayh) — this discourse imagines an appropriateness at the outset of the matter, but its complication dissolves by saying: The contradictory would be that he be guardian in that very matter in which he is a ward; for he manages affairs and is managed in the contract of marriage. So its content reduces to: that he is occupied with himself, then with those he supports, and he is not free for himself — so how can he manage others? Thus it reduces to a persuasive matter — unless the aspect of harm (ḍarar) to the ward is mentioned, due to the slave's occupation and the consumption of his times by the duties of serving his master.

These, then, are examples of these appropriateness on their varying degrees.

And the method of composing the persuasions (iqnāʿiyyāt) is: the derivation of composite propositions (qaḍāyā jumaliyyah) from specific causes, and the building of the purpose upon them. So we derive from impurities a composite proposition, namely: baseness and lowliness. And we derive — from proceeding to sell and exchanging for wealth — a composite proposition, namely: honoring, establishing weight, and affirming worth. Then the mutual contradiction (tanāfī) is generated from the two composite propositions.

Likewise, we derive from the description of being a foodstuff (waṣf al-ṭuʿm) an inviolability that bespeaks preciousness and distinction — which is a composite proposition. And we derive from acquisition by all paths, without constriction and added care — a composite proposition, namely: leniency and disregard toward it. And we imagine a mutual contradiction between the two propositions: so from them the appropriateness is organized, namely: the preservation of the second intended proposition, by negating what contradicts it.

Likewise, we derive from the slavery of the slave a kind of abasement (dhullah), lowliness (ṣighār), and humiliation (mahānah); and from the acceptance of his testimony — elevation of station and height of worth. And we imagine between them a mutual contradiction. For if these composite propositions — which were extracted from the specific particular propositions — were removed, and the particular propositions were related one to another directly, they would not be appropriate. That is the saying of one who says: "Prayer is not valid with it, therefore its sale is void"; and "It is a foodstuff needed, therefore hand-to-hand delivery (qabḍ fī al-majlis) is required in it, and deferment and excess (al-nasāʾ wa al-faḍl) are prohibited therein"; and "He is a slave, therefore he is not truthful in his statement, despite his probity (ʿadālah)."

These matters do not correspond by themselves, but correspond by their composite propositions.

So the path of resolving these complications is the detailing of what the imaginal (mukhīl) has summarized: of the propositions.

chapters.title_en: Section 29 — Examining the Proof for the Use of Munāsabah (Suitability) and Discussing Abū Zayd's Opinion on It
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| CHECK دليل استعمال المناسبة، ومناقشة رأي أبي زيد فيها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "relation, affinity, connection" — a thing's suitability or proportionality to another by virtue of an intrinsic link.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, munāsabah denotes a rational suitability between a legal cause (ʿillah) and the ruling (ḥukm), reflecting divine wisdom (ḥikmah) in legislation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = genealogical or relational kinship; metaphorical (majāz) = conceptual proportionality between cause and effect in legal reasoning.
- Root: د-ل-ل (d-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To indicate, point to, guide" — a sign or evidence that leads the mind to a conclusion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dalīl is that which, when correctly considered, yields certain or probable knowledge of the indicated matter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical pointing; metaphorical = intellectual indication through rational inference.
- Root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Resemblance, ambiguity, confusion" — that which is similar but not identical, causing doubt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām and uṣūl, shubhah is a specious argument that resembles truth but is false upon scrutiny.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = visual similarity; metaphorical = conceptual ambiguity in argumentation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with inna (إِنَّ) for emphasis — "Inna al-naẓar fī..." (Indeed, the examination of...) establishes the topic as a definitive subject of inquiry, followed by a genitive construction (muḍāf ilayh) to specify the scope.
chapters.translation:
I say: Now that the discussion of the textual indications (al-adillah al-naqliyyah) has been completed, it remains for us to examine the proof for the use of munāsabah (suitability) as a valid method for establishing legal causality (al-taʿlīl), and to investigate the opinion of Abū Zayd al-Dabūsī concerning it — for he has taken a distinctive position on this matter that merits careful scrutiny.

Know that the proponents of munāsabah argue as follows: The Lawgiver (al-Shāriʿ) does not enact rulings arbitrarily, but rather attaches them to causes (ʿilal) that bear a rational suitability to the rulings themselves. This suitability is discernible through the intellect, which perceives that a particular attribute (waṣf) is appropriate (munāsib) for bringing about a particular ruling — such as the suitability of intoxication (iskār) for prohibiting wine, or the suitability of guardianship (wilāyah) for the validity of a guardian's contract. When the intellect perceives this suitability, and the Lawgiver has indicated — through the very act of legislation — that He does not act without purpose (ʿabathan), the rational mind concludes that this suitable attribute is the cause (ʿillah) of the ruling.

Abū Zayd, however, has objected to this line of reasoning. He maintains that the mere perception of suitability by the intellect does not suffice to establish causality, for the intellect cannot know with certainty that the Lawgiver has indeed attached the ruling to this particular attribute rather than to another. The intellect's judgment of suitability is, at best, a probable indication (dalīl ẓannī), and probability cannot serve as a definitive proof (dalīl qaṭʿī) for establishing the divine intent behind legislation.

I respond to him by saying: This objection, if it were valid, would equally undermine the use of textual indications (al-adillah al-samʿiyyah) themselves, for the interpretation of scriptural texts also rests upon probable judgments concerning linguistic usage and contextual indications. Since the Lawgiver has commanded us to follow probable indications in deriving rulings — as when He said, {«فَاعْتَبِرُوا يَا أُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ»} (So take a lesson, O people of insight) — the use of munāsabah as a probable indication is likewise permissible, provided that it is not contradicted by a stronger textual or rational proof.

Furthermore, I say: The validity of munāsabah is not based solely on the intellect's independent perception, but rather on the convergence of two indications: first, the Lawgiver's known practice of attaching rulings to suitable attributes in the revealed texts; and second, the intellect's perception of suitability in the case at hand. When these two indications converge, the mind attains a strong presumption (ghalabat al-ẓann) that the attribute in question is indeed the cause — and this presumption is sufficient for legal practice, even if it does not reach the level of certainty.

As for the precise manner in which munāsabah operates, and the conditions that must be fulfilled for an attribute to be deemed suitable, and the distinction between suitable attributes that are effective (muʾaththirah) and those that are merely appropriate (mulāʾimah) — all of this will be explained in the sections that follow, if God Most High wills.

chapters.title_en: The Ranks of Appropriateness (Manāsibāt) and the Inevitability of Resorting to Suitability in Establishing Legal Causes
chapters.arabic_text:
وتبين أنها لا تزيد على المعنى] الخاص [الذي قدره موجبا له، فإذا لم يزد
عليه: انقطعت المناسبة.
فهذا بيان مراتب المناسبات وطرقها، ودرجاتها وأمثلتها.
فإن قيل:] قد [ذكرتم حقيقة المناسب وأجناسه وأنواعه؛ فما الدليل على كونه
طريقا إلى التعليل ومعرفا؟
قلنا: هذا هو المقصود بالكلام؛ ولكنا قدمنا الأمثلة: إذا لا يعرف وجه
دلالة الدليل من لم يعرف الدليل بنفسه؛ ومناسبة المعنى دليل على كون الحكم
ثابا ومعلقا عليه.
فنقول أولا: لسنا نعرف خلافا -بين الفقهاء القائسين -في قبول المناسب على
التفسير الذي ذكرناه؛ والمعنى بالمخيل هو المناسب.
وما  ذكره أبو زيد: من أن الاخالة لا يمكن الدلالة عليها مع الخصم؛ فالظن
به أنه عنى بذلك ما يرجع إلى شهادة القلب، ووقوع في النفس: يجري مجرى
الإلهام الذي يضيق نطاق العبارة عنه.
وما ذكرناه -من المناسب- خارج عن الفن الذي ذكره؛ وهو الذي نعنيه بالمخيل
أيضا: اذا أطلقناه. ودليل قبوله ما هو الدليل على قبول القياس المؤثر الذي
قدمناه؛ ودليل قبولهما جميعا دليل أصل القياس، وهو: إجماع الصحابة.
PageV01P177
والظن بأبي زيد أنه أراد بالمؤثر: المناسب الملائم؛ ولم يشترط التأثير على
التمثيل الذي قدمناه، بل اكتفى بالمناسبة مع الملائمة.
ويشهد لذلك ما ضربه: من الأمثلة للقياس؛ إذا قال:] قال [النبي عليه
السلام: "أنها من الطوافين عليكم والطوافات"، على لسقوط النجاسة: بضرورة]
الطوف علينا [؛ وللضرورات تأثير في إسقاط حكم الخطاب. وهذا ما نعنيه
بالمناسبة؛ فإن الحاجة داعية إلى المخالطة، فوق ذلك على الرتبة الثانية من
المناسبات التي ذكرناها. وهذا ملائم مجانس لتصرفات الشرع في توسيع الأمر،
في مظان الحاجات.
ومن أمثلة قوله في مسح الرأس: أنه مسح، فلا يسن تثليثه كمسح الخف.
PageV01P178
فهذا سماه مؤثرا؛ وهو واقع في التربة الأخيرة من المناسبات التي] ذكرنا
أمثلتها [. ويكاد] 31 - أ [يلتحق -عند تمام البحث- بشبه مجرد، أو بمناسبة
اقناعية ضعيفة.
وبيانه] هو أن يقال له [: ولم عللت سقوط التكرار في الأصل بكونه مسحا؟
ويطلب بإبداء أثره.
فان قال: لأن المسح في ذاته أخف من الغسل، ويلحق الناس في الغسل -من
المشقة- ما لا يلحقهم في المسح؛ ولأن صفة المسح قد أثرت في إيجاب تخفيف هذا
الركن، متى قوبل بالغسل في حق استيعاب محله. هذا ما ذكره أبو زيد في إبداء
تأثيره.
ففيه نظر: إذا نسلم أن المسح في ذاته أخف] من الغسل [ولكن: لم يمتنع
تكريره؟ وما وجه المناسبة؟ وأين ظهر في الشرع -لخفة الذات- تأثر في منع
التكرار؟
PageV01P179
يبقى قوله: انه ظهر تأثيره في التخفيف حيث لم يجب استيعاب محله؛ وهذا تشوف
إلى إظهار] أثر [عين العلة في جنس الحكم المتنازع فيه، وهو: التخفيف،
فيقول: إذا  عهد المسح مؤثرا في التخفيف من هذا الوجه_: ظهر كونه مؤثرا في
الوجه الآخر من التخفيف.
فيقال: ومن سلم أن ذلك من أثر كونه مسحا؟ وبم عرفت ذلك: ولم يظهر إلا حكم
مقرون بوصف؟ فلم جعلته معللا بذلك الوصف: وليس فيه نص ولا إجماع؟ وبم تنكر
على من يقول: المسح على الرأس اكتفى فيه بالأقل: مما ينطلق عليه الاسم،
لأنه واقع على الرأس؛ فهذا علته؟.
فان قال: يبطل بالمسح على الخف، فانه يساويه في الحكم، وليس واقعا على الرأس.
قيل: هذا عكس، وليس بنقض؛ والعلة فيه: كونه على الخف؛ ويجوز إثبات الحكم
في محلين بعلتين.
فان قال: وأي مناسبة -لكونه على الرأس، أو على الخف- في الاقتصار] على
البعض [؟ قلنا: فهذا اعتراف بأن طريق المعرفة: المناسبة. فإذا ظهر مناسبة
المسح للحكم، ولم تظهر مناسبة هذه الأوصاف، وجب التعليل بالمناسب؛ وإلا:
فمن يتمكن من إبداء نص أو إجماع في PageV01P180 # تعليل الحكم بكونه مسحا؟!. وإنما الطريق هي: المناسبة؛ فطلب التأثير،
وطلب المناسبة واحد؛ وهما عبارتان عن معنى واحد. فأما الاقتصار، في
الاستدلال، على إثبات العلة بالإجماع أو بالنص -فلا وجه له.
وهذه العبارة تداولها المتلقفون من أبي زيد، وهو أن العلة: ما ظهر تأثيره بالنص
أو الإجماع. وهذه الأمثلة لا تصير على هذه الترجمة، بل يضطرون إلى تفسير
التأثير: بالمناسبة؛ ثم يكتفون بمناسبة ضعيفة؛ ومناسبة المسح للتخفيف في
غاية الضعف، وحاصله يرجع إلى أنه خفيف بذاته، فينبغي أن يخف حكمه؛ وهذا
تحكم محض، يكاد يلتحق] بأنواع الاقناعيات من [المناسبات، ويتقاعد عنه، وأي
بعد في أن يقال: الاقتصار على الأقل نوع تخفيف لا تعقل علته، وليس ذلك
لكونه مسحا؟
وان أرادوا الإنصاف، فسببه: أن المسح من المصادر التي لا تقتضي الاستيعاب
في اللسان، بخلاف الغسل، فهذا مستنده.
وليس من غرضنا عين تلك المسئلة؛ وإنما غرضنا اضطراره -بهذا المثال- إلى
القول بالمخيل المناسب، والمنع من الاقتصار -في إثبات العلة- PageV01P181 # على الاستدلال بالنص أو الإجماع؛ فإن ذلك يعز وجوده في المسائل القياسية.
مثاله الآخر] قوله [: أنا متى قلنا:  نكاح الأمة -مع طول الحرة- يجوز:
لأنه معنى يجوز معه هذا النكاح للعبد؛ فيجوز للحر: قياسا على] الجهل بالغنا
[ووجود حرة رضيت بغير مهر.
سمى هذا مؤثرا، وأورده في أمثلة المؤثرات، وأين يتصور ها هنا إثبات
العلة] وتأثيرها [بنص أو بإجماع؟
والمطالبة عليه أن يقال: ولم قلت: أن ما لا يمنع العبد لا يصلح أن يكون
مانعا في حق الحر؟ ومن سلم أن] الجهل بالغنا [لا يمنع الحر لأنه لم يمنع
العبد؟] بل لم [يمنع العبد: لأنه لم يمنع الحر،] بل [لم يمنع كل واحد
منهما] لدليل دل [عليهما على وجه واحد. وهو الإنصاف.
PageV01P182
فإن قال: لأن الشرع بني جواز النكاح على الحل، ونصف حكمه بالرق، وجواز]
32 - ب [للحر أربع نساء، وللعبد اثنتين؛ فبقى العبد في النصف، على ما عليه
الحر في الكل؛ فلا يفترقان إلا في هذا القدر، ويستويان فيما بقى. هذا ما
ذكره أبو زيد من تأثيره.
فهو تحكم. أما الفرق في العدد، فمسلم.
وأما قوله: بقى في الباقي مسوايا للعبد؛ فتحكم في محل النزاع، وليس ذلك
مسلما، وعليه إقامة الدليل.
فان قال: استويا في] الجهل بالغنا [، فليستويا في القدرة.
قلنا: لم قلت ذلك، ولم يبعد أن يستويا من وجه ويفترقا من وجه، كما في
العدد وغيره؟ وإنما استويا -فيما استويا فيه- لاقتضاء الدليل التسوية، لا
لاستوائهما في حكم آخر. فما الدليل المقتضي التسوية ها هنا؟
فالمطالبة لا تنقطع عن هذا الكلام أبد الدهر، لأنه حاول تعليل PageV01P183 # النفي الأصلي بعلة مؤثرة موجبة؛ وذلك محال كما سنشرحه من بعد. وإنما
النافي يستدل أما بعموم أو بدلالة، أو] بسير حاصر لمدارك [الإثبات ونفيه.
فإن الشافعي يجعل القدرة على الطول مانعا؛ فهو المدعى، وكونه مانعا يفتقر
إلى موجب ومقتضى؛ فأما عدم كونه مانعا -وهو البقاء على الأصل- فلا يقتضي
موجبا، بلا يكتفي فيه بانتفاء الدليل المغير، وإنما يستدل -في هذا الجنس-
بعموم، كقوله تعالى "وانكحوا الأيامى منكم" مثلا؛ إلى أن يبين المدعى أن
هذا مخصوص بالموانع، وأن القدرة من] جملة [الموانع. فذكر مأخذه، أو  يستدل
بطريق الدلالة] عليه [فيقول: لو منع الحر. فهذا الجنس من الدليل جار في
النفي، ولكنه -في هذا المقام لا ينفك عن المطالبة. أو يستدل بالسبر -وهو الطريق
الجاري في جميع هذه الأجناس- PageV01P184 # فيقول: كونه مانعا إنما يتلقى من السمع، أو من القياس، ووجهه في القياس:
افضاؤه إلى الارقاق، أو اقتباسه من منع الحرة تحته نكاح أمة. وهذه الطرق
باطلة. وإذا انتفى دليل على تأثيره في المنع، لم يؤثر.
فهذا هو الطريق في أجناس ذلك، كما سنذكره. وغرضنا الآن أن نقول: من اجتزأ
بمثل هذا الكلام، فكيف يحسن منه أن يترجم مذهبه في العلل، بأن العلة: ما دل
النص أو الإجماع على كونه علة. فدل أنه في جميع ذلك يتشوف إلى المناسبة،
وقد يشترط معها الملائمة. فكلامه -في هذه الأمثلة- يرجع إلى إظهار
الملائمة، وهو مراده بالتأثير. ولذلك أورده في أمثلته عن الشافعي: أن
النكاح ليس بمال، فلا يثبت بشهادة النساء وقال: هذا] مؤثر [، لأن المال خلق
بذلة، PageV01P185 # فتكثر فيه] وجوه [المعاملة؛ وفي تقييد الأمر فيه بالرجال نوع حرج، وهذا
ما نعنيه بالمناسب] الملائم. وكذلك قال الشافعي: الزنا فعل يرجم عليه، فلا
يساوي النكاح الذي يحمد عليه: في حرمة المصاهرة وقال: هذا مؤثر، وهذا الذي
نعنيه بالمناسب [، كما تقدم.
وأما ما نقله -من أمثلة المؤثر، عن أبي حنيفة، أنه قال: المحجور] عليه
[اذا استودع فاستهلك الوديعة- لا يضمن، لأنه لما أودعه: فقد سلطه عليه.
وزعم أن هذا مؤثر -فالأمر على ما قال؛ ولكنه ليس من قبيل اثبات وصف علة
الأصل، فإن هذا الكلام لا يفتقر إلى أصل لو ثبت؛ فليس هو على شكل هذا
القياس] الذي حددناه: بالجمع بين الأصل والفرع برابطة [] 32 - أ [وإنما هو PageV01P186 # من قبيل دخول التفصيل تحت الجملة.
وسنذكر جنس هذا الدليل؛ وحاصله يرجع إلى أن التسليط مسقط، والإيداع ها
هنا تسليط: فكان مسقطا؛ فهما مقدمتان ونتيجة، لا يتصور الخلاف في النتيجة
مع تسليم المقدمات، وهو كقولنا: كل حيوان نام وكل انسان حيوان: فكل انسان
نام. ومثاله من الفقه:  كل مغصوب مضمون، والعقار مغصوب، فكان مضمونا.
فليس هذا على شكل القياس الذي نحن فيه؛ وإنما محل النظر إثبات الغصب في
العقار؛ ومأخذه طلب حد الغصب؛ وذلك لا يعرف من القياس؛ ومحل النظر في
الإيداع بيان] أن [الإيداع] تسليط [، ومأخذه طلب حد التسليط؛ ولا يؤخذ ذلك
من القياس.
ومن هذا القبيل، ما أورده من قول أبي حنيفة: إذا اشترى نصف أبيه لم يغرم
للبائع؛ لأنه أعتق برضاه.
وكذلك ما أورده] عن محمد بن الحسن، من قوله [، إذا قال لزوجته: إذا دخلت
الدار فأنت طالق ثلاثا، ثم طلقها ثلاثا، ثم عادت إليه، ثم دخلت] الدار [لا
تطلق، لأنه حيث طلقها ثلاثا فقد
PageV01P187
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of connection, relation, and affinity between two things; a link that binds them in a coherent whole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, the "appropriate attribute" (al-waṣf al-munāsib) is that which, if made the ratio legis (ʿillah), yields a wisdom (ḥikmah) or purpose (maqṣad) of the Lawgiver—either attested or inferred.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes genealogical or causal kinship; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any conceptual congruence between a ruling and its attribute, as in "this is suitable (munāsib) for that."
- Root: خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To imagine, to fancy, to cause a notion to occur in the mind; the root of "takhīl" (indication of suitability) and "mukhayyil" (that which suggests a rationale).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "suggestive" (mukhayyil) attribute is one that, though not explicitly attested, strongly intimates the Lawgiver's purpose—akin to a signpost pointing to the divine intent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Here it is used technically, not as mere imagination (wahm), but as the rational perception of a plausible connection between a ruling and its cause—a middle ground between explicit text and pure conjecture.
- Root: أ-ث-ر (a-th-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Trace, mark, effect; to leave an impression upon something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, "effect" (ta'thīr) means the demonstrated impact of an attribute on the ruling—either by explicit text, consensus, or evident suitability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Zamakhsharī distinguishes between literal effect (physical impression) and metaphorical effect (the legal consequence that an attribute produces in the law).
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of "Taʿlīq al-Ḥukm ʿalā al-Waṣf" (Attributing a Ruling to a Descriptor) — When a conditional or causal clause is attached to a specific attribute, the syntax implies that the attribute is the operative cause, unless a counter-indicator (ṣārif) intervenes.
chapters.translation:
And it has become clear that it [the appropriate attribute] does not exceed the specific meaning [khāṣṣ] which one has estimated as the cause (mūjib) of the ruling. So when it does not exceed it, the suitability (munāsabah) is severed.

This, then, is the exposition of the ranks of the appropriate attributes (manāsibāt), their pathways, their degrees, and their examples.

If it is said: "You have mentioned the reality of the appropriate (munāsib), its genera, and its species; so what is the proof that it is a pathway to causal determination (taʿlīl) and a means of recognition (taʿrīf)?"

We say: This is the very purpose of the discourse; but we have presented the examples first, because one who does not know the evidence (dalīl) itself cannot know the manner of its indication. And the suitability of a meaning is evidence that the ruling is established and attached to it.

So we say, first: We do not know of any disagreement—among the jurists who employ analogical reasoning (qiyās)—regarding the acceptance of the appropriate attribute (munāsib) upon the interpretation we have mentioned. And the "suggestive" (mukhayyil) is precisely the appropriate (munāsib).

As for what Abū Zayd mentioned—that "suggestion" (ikhālah) cannot be demonstrated against an opponent—our conjecture about him is that he meant by that what reverts to the testimony of the heart and what occurs in the soul, which runs in the vein of inspiration (ilhām) that the scope of expression is too narrow to capture.

What we have mentioned—of the appropriate (munāsib)—falls outside the art he discussed; and it is what we mean by the "suggestive" (mukhayyil) as well, when we use it absolutely. The proof of its acceptance is the same proof for accepting the effective analogy (al-qiyās al-muʾaththir) which we presented earlier; and the proof for accepting both of them is the proof for the very foundation of analogy (aṣl al-qiyās), namely: the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Companions.

PageV01P177

And our conjecture about Abū Zayd is that he meant by "effective" (muʾaththir): the suitable-and-congenial (al-munāsib al-mulāʾim); and he did not stipulate "effect" (taʾthīr) upon the model we presented, but rather sufficed with suitability (munāsabah) together with congeniality (mulāʾamah).

What bears witness to this is the example he gave for analogy, when he said: The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: {«إِنَّهَا مِنَ الطَّوَّافِينَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَالطَّوَّافَاتِ»} ("They are among those who go round about you")—to establish the non-impurity (of dogs) by virtue of the necessity of their going round among us; and necessities have an effect in lifting the obligation of the address (khiṭāb). This is what we mean by suitability (munāsabah); for need necessitates intermingling, and beyond that, it falls upon the second rank of the appropriate attributes we mentioned. And this is congenial (mulāʾim) and homogeneous (mujānis) with the Lawgiver's practices in broadening matters in situations of need.

And among his examples is his statement regarding wiping over the head (al-masḥ ʿalā al-raʾs): that it is "wiping," so its triplication is not Sunnah, just as the triplication of wiping over the khuff (leather socks) is not Sunnah.

PageV01P178

So he called this "effective" (muʾaththir); yet it falls in the very last tier of the appropriate attributes whose examples we have given. And it nearly—upon complete investigation—attaches to a mere semblance (shabah) or to a weak persuasive suitability (munāsabah iqnāʿiyyah).

Its clarification is that one says to him: "Why did you make the non-repetition in the original (aṣl) contingent upon its being 'wiping'? And you are asked to demonstrate its effect (athar)."

If he says: "Because wiping in itself is lighter than washing (ghusl), and people suffer in washing what they do not suffer in wiping; and because the attribute of wiping has effected the obligation of lightening this pillar (rukn), when compared with washing, in respect of encompassing its locus (istiʿāb maḥallihi)"—this is what Abū Zayd mentioned in demonstrating its effect.

There is a critical consideration here: Even if we grant that wiping in itself is lighter than washing, why is its repetition not permissible? And what is the face of suitability? And where has it appeared in the Law—due to lightness of essence—an effect in preventing repetition?

PageV01P179

There remains his statement: "Its effect appeared in lightening, since the encompassing of its locus was not made obligatory." This is a straining (tashawwuf) to demonstrate the effect of the very cause (ʿayn al-ʿillah) in the genus of the disputed ruling, namely: lightening (takhfīf). So he says: "When wiping is known to be effective in lightening from this aspect, it becomes apparent that it is effective in the other aspect of lightening."

So it is said to him: "And who granted that this is an effect of its being 'wiping'? And by what did you know that, when nothing appeared except a ruling conjoined with an attribute? So why did you make it caused (muʿallal) by that attribute, when there is neither text (naṣṣ) nor consensus (ijmāʿ) regarding it? And by what do you refute one who says: 'Wiping over the head sufficed with the least amount to which the name applies, because it occurs on the head; so this is its cause'?"

If he says: "This is invalidated by wiping over the khuff, for it equals it in the ruling, yet it does not occur on the head."

It is said: This is a reversal (ʿaks), not a refutation (naqḍ); and the cause there is its being on the khuff; and it is permissible to establish a ruling in two loci with two causes.

If he says: "And what suitability is there—for its being on the head or on the khuff—in restricting to a part?"

We say: This is an admission that the pathway of recognition is suitability (munāsabah). So when the suitability of wiping to the ruling appears, and the suitability of these other attributes does not appear, then the ruling must be caused by the appropriate (munāsib); otherwise—who is able to produce a text or consensus for PageV01P180 # making the ruling contingent upon its being "wiping"?! The only pathway is suitability (munāsabah); so seeking effect (taʾthīr) and seeking suitability are one and the same; they are two expressions for a single meaning. As for restricting oneself, in inference, to establishing the cause by consensus or text—there is no basis for that.

This expression was circulated by those who took from Abū Zayd, namely: "The cause is that whose effect is demonstrated by text or consensus." Yet these examples do not conform to this rendering; rather, they are compelled to interpret "effect" (taʾthīr) as suitability (munāsabah); then they suffice with a weak suitability. And the suitability of wiping to lightening is extremely weak; its sum total reverts to: "It is light in itself, so its ruling ought to be light"—and this is pure arbitrary judgment (taḥakkum), which nearly attaches to the types of persuasive (iqnāʿiyyāt) suitable attributes, and even falls short of them. And what distance is there in saying: "Restricting to the least is a type of lightening whose cause is not intelligible, and it is not because it is 'wiping'?"

If they desire fairness, the reason is: wiping (al-masḥ) is among the verbal nouns (maṣādir) that do not necessitate encompassing (istiʿāb) in the language, unlike washing (ghusl)—so this is its basis.

And it is not our purpose to delve into that very issue; rather, our purpose is to show his compulsion—through this example—to affirm the suggestive-appropriate (al-mukhayyil al-munāsib), and to forbid restricting oneself—in establishing the cause—PageV01P181 # to inference by text or consensus alone; for that is rarely found in analogical issues.

His other example is his statement: "When we say: Marriage to a slave-woman (nikāḥ al-amah)—despite the presence of a free woman—is permissible, because it is a meaning with which this marriage is permissible for the slave; so it is permissible for the free man, by analogy to ignorance of wealth (al-jahl bi al-ghinā) and the existence of a free woman who consented without a dowry."

He called this "effective" (muʾaththir) and cited it among the examples of effective causes. And where is it conceivable here to establish the cause and its effect by text or consensus?

The demand (muṭālabah) against him is to say: "Why did you say that what does not prevent the slave is not fit to be a preventive (māniʿ) with respect to the free man? And who granted that ignorance of wealth does not prevent the free man because it did not prevent the slave? Rather, it did not prevent the slave because it did not prevent the free man; rather, it did not prevent each of them due to a proof (dalīl) that indicated for both of them in a single manner." And this is fairness (inṣāf).

PageV01P182

If he says: "Because the Law built the permissibility of marriage upon licitness (ḥill), and divided its ruling by slavery (riqq), permitting the free man four wives and the slave two; so the slave remained in the half upon what the free man is upon in the whole; so they do not differ except in this measure, and they are equal in what remains"—this is what Abū Zayd mentioned as its effect.

It is arbitrary judgment (taḥakkum). As for the difference in number, it is granted. As for his statement: "He remained equal to the slave in the rest"—this is arbitrary judgment in the very locus of dispute, and it is not granted; and upon him is the burden of proof.

If he says: "They are equal in ignorance of wealth, so let them be equal in capability (qudrah)."

We say: Why did you say that? And it is not far that they are equal in one aspect and differ in another, as in number and other matters? They are only equal—in what they are equal in—because the proof necessitates equality, not because of their equality in another ruling. So what is the proof that necessitates equality here?

The demand (muṭālabah) never ceases against this discourse for all eternity, because he attempted to cause the original negation (al-nafy al-aṣlī) with an effective, necessitating cause—and that is impossible, as we shall explain hereafter. Rather, the negator (nāfī) infers either by a general text (ʿumūm), or by an indication (dalālah), or by a comprehensive survey (sabr) that encompasses the loci of affirmation and negation.

PageV01P183–184

For al-Shāfiʿī makes capability of wealth (al-qudrah ʿalā al-ṭūl) a preventive (māniʿ); so he is the claimant, and its being a preventive requires a necessitator and a ground (muqtaḍin). As for its not being a preventive—which is remaining upon the original (al-baqāʾ ʿalā al-aṣl)—it does not require a necessitator; rather, one suffices in it with the absence of any altering proof (dalīl mughayyir). Rather, one infers in this genus by a general text, such as His saying: {«وَأَنْكِحُوا الْأَيَامَى مِنْكُمْ»} ("And marry the unmarried among you") for example—until the claimant demonstrates that this is specified by preventives, and that capability is among the preventives. So he mentions its source (maʾkhadh). Or he infers by the pathway of indication (dalālah) upon it, saying: "If it prevented the free man..."—so this genus of proof operates in negation, but in this context it does not detach from the demand. Or he infers by the survey (sabr)—which is the pathway operative in all these genera—saying: "Its being a preventive is only received from the revealed Law (samʿ) or from analogy (qiyās); and its face in analogy is: its leading to enslavement (irqāq), or its being derived from the prevention of a free woman under him from marrying a slave-woman." And these pathways are invalid. And when any proof of its effect in prevention is absent, it has no effect.

So this is the pathway in the genera of that matter, as we shall mention. And our purpose now is to say: Whoever is satisfied with such discourse, how is it seemly for him to render his doctrine on causes (ʿilal) by saying: "The cause is that which the text or consensus indicates as being a cause"? So it is demonstrated that in all of that he is straining toward suitability (munāsabah), and he may stipulate congeniality (mulāʾamah) along with it. So his discourse—in these examples—reverts to demonstrating congeniality, and that is what he means by "effect" (taʾthīr). For this reason he cited among his examples from al-Shāfiʿī: "Marriage is not property (māl), so it is not established by the testimony of women"—and he said: This is "effective" (muʾaththir), because property was created for lowliness (dhillah), PageV01P185 # so its modes of transaction multiply; and in restricting its matters to men there is a type of hardship (ḥaraj). And this is what we mean by the suitable-congenial (al-munāsib al-mulāʾim). Likewise, al-Shāfiʿī said: "Fornication (zinā) is an act upon which one is stoned, so it does not equal marriage (nikāḥ), which is praised, in the inviolability of affinity (ḥurmat al-muṣāharah)"—and he said: This is "effective," and this is what we mean by the suitable (munāsib), as has preceded.

As for what he transmitted—among the examples of the effective—from Abū Ḥanīfah, that he said: "A person under legal interdiction (maḥjūr ʿalayhi), if he is given a deposit (wadīʿah) and then destroys it, he does not guarantee it (lā yaḍman), because when he was given the deposit, he was given authority (taslīṭ) over it." And he claimed this is "effective"—the matter is as he said; but it is not of the category of establishing the attribute of the cause of the original (waṣf ʿillat al-aṣl), for this discourse does not require an original (aṣl) even if it were established. So it is not upon the form of this analogy which we defined: by combining the original and the branch (farʿ) with a link (rābiṭah). Rather, it is PageV01P186 # of the category of subsuming a particular (tafṣīl) under a general proposition (jumlah).

And we shall mention the genus of this proof; its sum total reverts to: "Giving authority (taslīṭ) is a remover (musqit), and deposit here is giving authority, so it is a remover"—so these are two premises and a conclusion, and no disagreement is conceivable in the conclusion once the premises are granted. It is like our saying: "Every animal sleeps, and every human is an animal, so every human sleeps." And its example from jurisprudence: "Every usurped thing (maghṣūb) is guaranteed (maḍmūn), and real estate (ʿaqār) is usurped, so it is guaranteed." So this is not upon the form of the analogy we are discussing; rather, the locus of consideration is establishing usurpation (ghaṣb) in real estate; and its source is seeking the definition (ḥadd) of usurpation; and that is not known from analogy. And the locus of consideration in deposit is demonstrating that deposit is giving authority; and its source is seeking the definition of giving authority; and that is not taken from analogy.

And of this category is what he cited from Abū Ḥanīfah's statement: "If one buys half of his father, he does not pay the seller (lā yaghram lil-bāʿiʿ), because he emancipated (aʿtaqa) with his consent."

Likewise, what he cited from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, his statement: "If one says to his wife: 'If you enter the house, you are divorced three times,' then he divorces her three times, then she returns to him, then she enters the house—she is not divorced, because when he divorced her three times, he had

PageV01P187

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is relation, affinity, or proportion — that which is fitting or congruous to a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, al-munāsib denotes a descriptive attribute whose suitability for legislation is perceived by rational consideration, aligning the ḥukm with its maqṣūd (divine purpose).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for genealogical or proportional relation; metaphorically (majāz) for a legal attribute that "fits" the ruling as a cause.
- Root: م-ل-ء (m-l-’)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be suitable, agreeable, or harmonious; al-mulā’amah is concordance or compatibility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical sense — the attribute's harmony with the general aims of the Law (maqāṣid al-sharī’ah), making it a plausible ratio legis.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical fitting (e.g., a garment); metaphorical for the "fit" between a legal cause and its effect.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, testify, or attest; shahādat al-aṣl is the attestation of a specific textual origin.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, it means that a particular legal principle (aṣl) in the revealed sources corroborates the appropriateness of the attribute.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for bearing witness; metaphorical for a textual precedent "bearing witness" to the validity of an analogy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Reconstruction) — The text omits certain connective particles (e.g., "wa-in kāna" or "fa-inna"), requiring the translator to supply implicit logical connectors to render the conditional and concessive clauses accurately.
chapters.translation:
I say: The entire dispute concerning that [particular] kingship [i.e., the property in question] collapses, because the sum of it is that the oath did not encompass anything except the divorce of that kingship; and since it no longer remains, the divorce does not occur. Whoever concedes these premises cannot conceivably dispute the conclusion. Indeed, one may contest the premises, and then the discussion — in establishing them — leads to a discourse that follows the very form of the analogy (qiyās) we are presently examining.

It has become clear, in sum, that the suitable-and-harmonious (al-munāsib al-mulā’im) is affirmed as a valid ground by the consensus of the practitioners of qiyās (al-qā’isīn). The disagreement among them pertains only to: (a) the strange (gharīb) [attribute] that is not harmonious; or (b) the harmonious attribute for which no specific origin (aṣl mu’ayyan) bears witness. The latter is what jurists label "unrestricted inference" (al-istidlāl al-mursal) — meaning reliance upon the suitable, maslaha-oriented meaning (al-ma’nā al-munāsib al-maṣlaḥī) that appears in the branch case, without citing a specific origin. The school of Mālik points toward following the unrestricted interests (al-maṣāliḥ al-mursalah); al-Shāfiʿī exhibited hesitation (taraddud) on this.

As for the strange (gharīb) [attribute] that is neither harmonious nor attested by a specific origin — it is rejected (mardūd); no disagreement is known concerning it. From this it follows that whatever is not suitable cannot be installed as a cause (ʿillah) by mere opinion (ra’y); rather, its installation as a cause is known only through the indication of the text (naṣṣ), or its allusion (īmā’), or consensus (ijmāʿ).

As for what is suitable, it falls into four divisions:
1. An attribute combining both the witness of an origin and suitability — this is a proof (ḥujjah) by consensus of the qā’isīn.
2. An attribute lacking both suitability and the witness of an origin — this is not a proof by consensus.
3. An attribute attested by a specific origin, yet strange and not harmonious. By "witness of a specific origin" I mean that it is derived (mustanbaṭ) from that origin, in the sense that the ruling was established by the Law in accordance with it.
4. A harmonious attribute for which no specific origin bears witness — we shall mention examples of this under the unrestricted interests (al-maṣāliḥ al-mursalah).

As for the strange attribute that has no specific origin attesting to it, its example is what we mentioned earlier: strange appropriateness (munāsabāt gharībah), if one supposes it to be initiated for establishing a ruling de novo, not for explaining a ruling already revealed. For instance, had the [Prophetic] statement {«al-qātil lā yarith»} ("The killer does not inherit") not been revealed, and someone said: "We do not let him inherit," opposing him by the inversion of his very intent — namely, his hastening to the inheritance before its proper time — and claims this is suitable (munāsib), intending to establish the ruling thereby — this has no valid basis.

Now, it is incumbent upon me to provide a detailed exposition concerning the strange attribute derived (al-munāsib al-gharīb al-mustanbaṭ) from the very locus of the text (maḥall al-naṣṣ) — and my view (ra’y) regarding employing it as a cause (taʿlīl).
