chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-ل-ب (gh-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Predominance, overcoming, victory; a thing that prevails over its counterpart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, ghālib al-ẓann denotes the preponderant conjecture that outweighs its opposite, functioning as a cognitive state short of certainty but binding in practice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is martial conquest; metaphorically extended to the dominance of one opinion over another in the mind's balance.
- Root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Similarity, resemblance; ambiguity arising from shared attributes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, shabah (legal similitude) is a non-appropriate (ghayr munāsib) attribute that nonetheless links cases via resemblance, yielding conjecture rather than certainty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical likeness; metaphorical: juridical analogy based on superficial commonality, contrasted with munāsabah (rational suitability).
- Root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Nearness, proximity; also a means of drawing near (qurbah) to Allah.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal causation, qurbah denotes the attribute that brings the branch case near the root case, justifying extension of the ruling.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal spatial proximity; metaphorical: conceptual closeness in legal ratio.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional apodosis with fa' (الفاء في جواب الشرط) — When the protasis is a nominal clause or a verb of non-volitional import, the apodosis is introduced by fa', as in "فإن قال: نعم: قلنا" (If he says: yes, we say), marking the consequent as a fresh speech act.
chapters.translation:
I say: If he claims that [this type of similitude] is not productive of knowledge, then it is closer to producing conjecture (ẓann). And if he says: "Yes [it produces conjecture]," we reply: Conjecture is like knowledge in the obligation of annexation (ilḥāq), for we have not extracted from the appropriate attributes (munāsabāt) anything but conjectures.

If he says: "This genre has not been transmitted from the Companions," we reply: What is transmitted from them is not confined [to explicit reports]; rather, from their methodological paths (masālik) it is understood that they followed predominant conjectures — that is, ruling by the more preponderant opinion (al-ra'y al-arjaḥ).

If he says: "How many a predominant opinion did they abandon?" we reply: That was due to its contravening a text (naṣṣ), or an analogy (qiyās), or an opinion even more preponderant in conjecture than it. As for their turning away from a predominant opinion that is sound and free from defects (qawādiḥ) and countervailing evidence — that is not to be conjectured of them, nor does any Muslim deem it permissible to fabricate such a charge against a Companion or a religiously committed Imam. For whoever denies legal similitude (shabah) denies it only because the aspect of preponderance has not been clarified to him; and whoever acknowledges the occurrence of preponderant conjecture, then denies ruling by it — he is obstinate (muʿānid).

If a speaker says: "It has been established by what you mentioned that a type of nearness (qurbah) may produce conjecture; but this does not avail you in this particular question, for we do not concede that nearness by taste (ṭaʿm) produces conjecture."

We reply: It is not our purpose to settle this very question; rather, our purpose is to establish the proof of the permissibility of signifying a ruling by an attribute that is not appropriate (lā tanāsabu), such that — through approximation and participation in it — there occurs sharing in the ruling. And the purpose has been achieved.

Then the method of establishing conjecture in this question is: that we demonstrate that there is no sign (ʿalāmah) — whether exhaustive (ḥāṣirah) or comprehensive (jāmiʿah) — for dates and raisins, except: nutritive value (aqwāt), measure (kayl), monetary value (māliyyah), and taste (ṭaʿm). All have been invalidated except taste, or taste has preponderated — so it becomes more worthy. And when this path is traversed, conjecture is produced; and at that point, issuing legal opinion (fatwā) by it and acting upon it become permissible.

The principle has thus been established: there is no root case (aṣl) except that there approximates it something that is in its meaning — either by knowledge, or something that is in its meaning by conjecture. And all of that is due to its participation with it in a sign known or conjectured. If that is not found, one confines oneself to the text — for among the texts there are those whose rulings are not extended, since nothing is found that is in their meaning. As for raisins, it is known that they are in the meaning [of dates] before the sign is specified; because however the sign is conceived in the mind, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: {«من أعتق شركا له في عبد: قوم عليه الباقي»} ("Whoever frees his share in a slave: the remainder is valued against him"). The slave is known by his name, and it is known that the female slave (ummah) is in his meaning before we ascertain the limit of the cause (ʿillah) and the exhaustive sign. And if one frees half of a slave whose entirety he owns, it is not valued against him, and what he freed is not named by the name of partnership (shirkah); but we know that he is freed and that it is in his meaning. And if one frees a specific half of his slave, or a limb such as his hand or foot — it predominates in conjecture that a part of the slave is in the meaning of another part, whether the part be undifferentiated (shāʾiʿ) or specified (muʿayyan), just as the pure half in ownership was in the meaning of the half mixed with another's property. But that [first case] is known, and this [second] is conjectured. This conjecture is only dispelled by our demonstrating that the fact of [the slave being] a locus (maḥall) receptive to all dispositions has an effect on the diffusion (saryān) of manumission — then what we conjectured is cut off; or by our invalidating what he mentioned, so the first conjecture remains intact.

Every attribute that is not appropriate (ghayr munāsib) and every similitudinal sign (ʿalāmah shabahiyyah) that appears initially is at risk of being effaced (inmiḥāq) by a meaning that confronts it which is more manifest or more worthy. Likewise, every appropriate attribute (munāsib) that appears initially is under this same risk. And that does not indicate the invalidity of its genus.

When the discourse reaches this terminus, if we were to challenge and claim that the doctrine of legal similitude (shabah) is certain (qaṭʿī) in the discipline of uṣūl, we would not be far [from truth] — since it has been established with certainty that predominant conjecture is followed, and it has been established in reason that the derivation of conjecture from a type of nearness is permissible.

لا يناسب، كما جاز استفادة] العلم منه، وإنما الغموض في أحاد المسائل:
لتعارض الصفات الجامعة والفارقة فيها، وعسر مدارك الترجيح في بعضها، وإلا
فالقول بهذا الجنس يترقي إلى رتبة القطعيات، بالتقرير الذي [كنا] ذكرناه.
فإن قال قائل: فنبهونا على طريق سير العلامات الفارقة الجامعة عند
تعارضها، وطريق ترجيح البعض منها على البعض، وأهم الأمثلة مسائلة الربا:
فإنها معيار النظر، وعليها تدوار الأصوليين في أمثلة العلل؛ وهي من أغمض
المسائل.
قلنا: الطريق فيه أن نردد النظر بين الطعم والكيل أولا، ونقول: التعليل
بالكيل باطل لوجهين، أشار الشافعي إليهما:
أحدهما: أن الكيل مثل الوزن؛ والتعليل بالوزن باطل: لأنه لو علل به، لوجب
تحريم بيع الموزون بالموزون نساء، كما حرم بيع المكيل بالمكيل، وكل جنسين
مختلفين اشتركا في العلة.
PageV01P359
والإجماع منعقد على جواز إسلام النقدين في الأشياء الموزونة من النحاس
والرصاص والزعفران وغيرها، وبهذا المسلك، عرفنا وجوب التعليل لحكم الربا،
إذا لو اقتصرنا على موجب الاسم، لقلنا بامتناع إسلام الدراهم [في]
الموزونات، فإنه قال عليه السلام عقيب ذكر الأشياء الستة الستة: ((فإذا
اختلف  الجنسان فبيعوا كيف شئتم يدا بيد)).
وهذا يقتضي تحريم إسلام النقدين في الأشياء الأربعة، كما اقتضي تحريم
إسلام أحد النقدين في الآخر، وأحد الأشياء الأربعة في الباقيات، ولا دليل
-من حيث اللفظ -يوجب تقاطع النقدين عن الأشياء الأربعة؛ [فدل على] الرجوع
إلى التعليل، وإنما معناه: فإذا اختلف الجنسان من هذه الجملة المشتركة في
علامة الربا، لا من هذه الجملة المعلومة باسمها وصورتها، وهذا الإجماع نص
في وجوب البحث عن العلة، والتجاوز PageV01P360 # عن موجب اللفظ، وكيف يتماري فيه منصف مع قول أمير المؤمنين عمر -رضي الله
عنه -: أن الناس ليقولون: أن عمر أعرف الناس بأبواب الربا؛ ولو كنت عالما
بها: لكان أحب إلى من حمر النعم؛ وإن الربا من آخر ما نزل على النبي صلي
الله عليه وسلم، فمات [قبل أن] يبينه لنا، فدعوا الربا والريبة))، ولو كان
الحكم يقتصر على المسميات: لما خفي على العوام؛ [فكيف عمر] مع ما اشتمل
عليه اللفظ من التفصيل والتعديد، فكيف ينتهي أشكاله إلى أن ينسب عمر إلى
الاختصاص بدركه من بين كافة الصحابة: وهم الغواصون في علم الشريعة،
والمجتهدون في مصادرها ومواردها؟
وغرضنا الآن بطلان التعليل بالوزن، مع انعقاد الإجماع على إسلام النقدين
في الموزونات.
فإن قالوا: السلم محرم بالإجماع في الثمنية أو المثمنية؛ كان ذلك تحكما
مستحدثا [لا أصل له] دعاهم إلى ذلك مساق مذهبهم، PageV01P361 # ولا مستند له، وإن زعموا أنا فهمنا ذلك من الإجماع، قلنا: وهلا فهمتم من
الإجماع اختصاص النقدين بعلتهما، كما فهمناه حتى لا تخرجوا إلى الضبط
بالثمنية والثمنية؟
الوجه الثاني للإبطال، هو: أن التعليل بالكيل يوجب إخراج الحفنة
[والحفنتين] عن حكم الربا؛ وإخراج الحلي عن ذلك، والربا جار فيهما بحكم النقص.
قال الشافعي: وما ناقض الشبه فهو المنتقض دون الشبه؛ إذا موجب الشبه
جريان الربا في كل ما باسم البر والذهب، وذلك جار في القليل والحلي؛ والعجب
أنهم أخرجوا القليل وأدرجوا الحلي وخاتم [54 - ب] الفضة، ولم يطردوا ذلك في
خواتم الحديد، فبه عرف تناقض هذا الأصل.
فإن قيل:  أبو حنيفة أساء [في] التفريغ؛ فيمكن التعليل بالكيل وطرده في
الجنس، وإجراء الربا في الحفنة، وذلك لا يدل على أن الكيل غير صالح.
قلنا: لا، بل استد في التفريع؛ فإنه أراد بالكيل والوزن PageV01P362 # اعتبارهما لا إمكانهما، حتى قال أبو يوسف: كل مصر لا يوزن فيه اللحم، فلا
بأس بطابق طابقين، والحفنة والخواتم لا يعتاد فيه التقدير، فلو قيل: أنه من
جنس المقدر، لتعددت العلة، ولكانت العلة في الكثير أنه مقدر، وفي القليل:
أنه من جنس المقدر، ولكان كقولنا: [أن كثير] الخمر محرم بعلة الإسكار،
والقليل بعلة كونه داعيا إلى السكر؛ وهما علتان: إحداهما خفية ضعيفة،
والأخرى قوية، وتقسيم البر بتعدد علته، محال لا وجه له، فهذان وجهان لإبطال
مذهبه، وقد أشار الشافعي إلى وجهين آخرين، يصلحان للترجيح، لا [للا] بطال:
أحدهما: أن الطعم مقصود هذه الأشياء، ولأجه فطرت وخلقت؛ PageV01P363 # ولما ظهر مقصودها شح الناس عليها: فباعوها مقدرا لا جزافا، فتقدير
المقصود الخاص علامة، أولى من تقدير ما يجري مجري العاصم للمقصود، والدراهم
والدنانير متميزة بمقصودها الخاص: الذي لا يعدلهما [فيه] غيرهما؛ فكون
الخاصة علامة للحكم - أغلب على الظن من العدول إلى الوزن المعرف للمقدار،
لأجل المشاحة في المعاملات.
الثاني: أن الكيل علامة الإباحة، فيبعد أن يكون علامة التحريم وان اختلف
محله، ونحن قد عددنا علامة الإباحة وعلامة التحريم؛ وإحالة تضاد الأحكام
على اختلاف العلامات أغلب على الظن من إحالتها على اختلاف المحال، مع اتحاد
العلامة.
وقد ترجح أيضا بتأييده بقوله -عليه السلام -: ((لا تبيعوا الطعام
بالطعام)).
والعبارة المحررة لأصحابنا في الترجيح معروفة؛ وهي: أن علتنا سلمت عن
المعارضة والمناقضة، واستندت إلى عموم أسمها، ولم تخرج عن حكم أصلها، ولم
تتناقض في نفسها، وقد استقصي ذلك في التعاليق.
PageV01P364
[فلسنا للأطناب فيه، وإنما الغرض التنبيه على طريقه؛ فإن الترجيح من
المسالك الجارية في هذه المسئلة المتعينة فيها: في بعض أطرافها].
فإن قيل: [تأيدت] علتهم بقوله -عليه السلام -: ((إلا كيلا بكيل)).
قلنا: ذلك مذكور للخلاص [من الربا]؛ وهو معتبر علامة للخلاص والإباحة.
فإن  قيل: إيجاب المماثلة -في القابل للمماثلة -أولى؛ فليعلم الشرط بإمكان
حصوله، فللكيل والجنسية تأثير في إظهار محل الحكم؛ فهو أولى بأن يجعل علامة
عليه. ولأن الربا شرع مقرونا بالخلاص، وفي التعليل بالطعم إجراؤه في
السفرجل والبطيخ وما لا خلاص فيه.
قلنا: لهذا، ضم الشافعي في قول الكيل إلى الطعم، واعتبر اجتماعهما، وقال:
قول ابن المسيب في هذا من أصح الأقاويل كما سبق نقله.
وهذا قول قوي جامع لجميع أطراف الكلام، فتكون العلامة -على هذا القول
-اجتماع الأمرين. ولعله رجع في الجديد عن هذا؛ لأنه وردت أخبار في الربا في
حلي الذهب، والخرز الذي يباع عددا. فقد علم النبي -عليه السلام -طريق بيعه:
في عقد اشتمل على خرز الذهب PageV01P365 # واللآلئ وذكرت الفضة في مسائلة مد عجوة، فعرف به أن المقصود هو المتبع،
دون التقدير، وقد قررنا وجه ذلك في مسائلة الحفنة.
فإن قيل: فتدواركم على المقصود الخاص، تنبيه على متانة طريق مالك -رضي
الله عنه -في التعليل بالقوت: فإنه الأخص.
قلنا: [لولا ورود] الملح: لكان التعليل به أخص، ولكن عدل الشافعي عنه
لأجل الملح.
فأما قوله: ما يستصلح به القوت [قوت]، ففاسد: لأنه PageV01P366 # لا يخلو أما أن يكون علة على حيالها كالنقدية، فيلزم [على مسافة] جواز
أسلام البر في الملح، وهو خلاف الإجماع، أو يقال: هو يرجع إلى القوت
لاتصاله به بطريق الاستصلاح، وذلك يلزم أن يعدي إلى الحطب والتنور وما يتصل
بإصلاح القوت؛ ومهما تعدي إلى ذلك على تبعية القوت، فتعديته إلى الفواكه
التي تسد مسد القوت، وإلى الآدام التي تقع تبعا للقوت: كاللحم وغيره -أولى.
وعند ذلك يتداعي إلى القول بالطعم.
وإذا قال: للملح خاصية ليست لغيره، قلنا: أن لم يكون هو القوت فهو علة
أخرى، فليجز إسلام الأشياء الثلاثة فيه، كما جاز إسلام النقدين في الأشياء
الأربعة [55 - أ] وهو خلاف الإجماع، فلولا الملح لكان ما ذكره مالك أولى وأخص.
وعلى الجملة: تعليل الأشياء الأربعة بعلة واحدة، أولى: فإنه إذا [كثرت
الأصول، كان ككثرة الشواهد، فإذا] اشتركت في  الطعم، كان الطعم مشهودا له من
جهة الملح أيضا، فهذا يتبين بطريق الترجيح.
فإن قيل: فليكن تعليل أبي حنيفة بالتقدير للأشياء الستة PageV01P367 # أولى؛ أو ليكن تعليل ابن الماجشون بالمالية أولى.
قلنا: الوزن غير الكيل عند أبي حنيفة، كما ذكرناه، وإنما التقدير عبارة
شاملة؛ ولذلك لم يتعد إلى الذرع والعد، وهو نوع تقدير، وأما [مالية ابن
الماجشون] فهي أوسع الصفات وأعمها، وأبعدها عن الخاصية المقصودة، وهو مضطر
إلى تجويز إسلام النقدين في غيرهما؛ وفيه التفريق في العلة، وعلى لجملة: لا
تلغي أخص الصفات -مع صلاحها -بالأعم؛ فهو ليس آخذا مذهبه من الشبه
والعلامة؛ ولعله يأخذ من المنع من اجتاح المال وتفويته من غير منة ومجمدة
ومثوبة، وإليه ترجع مقابلة الشيء بمثله؛ ثم يعتذر عن الجيد بالردئ، بما
اعتذر أبو حنيفة به: من إسقاطه قيمة الجودة.
فإن قيل: فهلا جمعتم بين هذه العلل؟ قلنا: اعتذر ابن سريج عن هذا: بأن
ذلك يخرجنا عن قول العلماء، وسنذكر مستند قول العلماء، فإن التعليل - في
مثل هذا المقام - بعلتين، غير جائز إلا أن يجعل الجميع علة؛ كما قال
الشافعي في قول: أن العلة هي الطعم مع التقدير؛ وقال مالك: القوت، وفيه
الجمع بين الكل.
PageV01P368
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To recur, to follow in succession; a cause (ʿillah) as that which necessitates or justifies a ruling by repeated attachment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological-legal sense: the effective attribute (waṣf muʾaththir) that is the ratio legis for a divine command, discerned by ijtihād.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a recurring malady; metaphorical (majāz): the juridical cause — a transferred usage from physical causation to normative signification.
- Root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Resemblance, ambiguity; the root of shubhah (obscurity) and shabah (likeness).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, the ambiguous resemblance between attributes that complicates tarjīḥ (preponderance).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: visual similarity; metaphorical: conceptual parity in legal reasoning.
- Root: ك-ي-ل (k-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To measure by volume (kayl); a standard of quantity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A conventional measure (miqdār) used in transactions, distinct from weight (wazn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the act of measuring; metaphorical: the sign (ʿalāmah) of quantity in legal analogy.
- Root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Taste, food; the edible substance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The intrinsic property (maʿnā) of nutritive value, proposed as the ʿillah for ribā in the four named items.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: gustatory perception; metaphorical: the essential purpose (maqṣūd) of the commodity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-ḥukm ʿalā al-ʿillah (Attribution of a ruling to a cause) — In conditional and causal constructions, the ruling follows the effective attribute, not the mere name; this governs the parsing of "fa-idhā ikhtalafa al-jinsān" as a conditional clause whose protasis signals the operative cause.
chapters.translation:
I say: It is not fitting [that the path be obscure], just as deriving knowledge from it is permissible. Rather, the obscurity lies in the particulars of the cases: due to the conflict of unifying and differentiating attributes therein, and the difficulty of the avenues of preponderance (tarjīḥ) in some of them. Otherwise, affirming this genus ascends to the rank of certainties (qaṭʿiyyāt), by the exposition we have already mentioned.

If someone says: "Then alert us to the path of traversing the differentiating and unifying signs (ʿalāmāt) when they conflict, and the path of preferring some over others. And the most important example is the case of ribā (usury): for it is the criterion of legal inquiry (naẓar), and upon it the uṣūliyyūn revolve in their examples of causes (ʿilal); and it is among the most obscure of cases."

We say: The path therein is that we first alternate our inquiry between taste (ṭaʿm) and measure (kayl), and say: The attribution of the ruling to measure (taʿlīl bi-al-kayl) is invalid for two aspects, which al-Shāfiʿī indicated:

The first: That measure is like weight (wazn); and attribution to weight is invalid: for if it were attributed to it, then the sale of a weighed item for a weighed item of the same kind would be prohibited in deferred exchange (nisāʾ), just as the sale of a measured item for a measured item is prohibited, and [so would] every two different genera that share in the cause.

{PageV01P359}
And the consensus (ijmāʿ) is established upon the permissibility of advancing payment (salām) of the two precious metals (al-naqdayn) for weighed things such as copper, lead, saffron, and others. And by this path, we know the necessity of attributing the ruling of ribā to a cause: for if we confined ourselves to the requirement of the name, we would say that advancing the dirhams for weighed items is prohibited, since he, peace be upon him, said after mentioning the six things: {«Fa-idhā ikhtalafa al-jinsāni fa-bīʿū kayfa shiʾtum yadan bi-yad»} ("And if the two genera differ, then sell as you wish, hand to hand").

And this necessitates the prohibition of advancing the two precious metals for the four things, just as it necessitated the prohibition of advancing one of the two precious metals for the other, and one of the four things for the rest. And there is no evidence — from the perspective of the wording — that necessitates the separation of the two precious metals from the four things; thus this indicates the recourse to the cause (taʿlīl). And its meaning is only: "If the two genera differ from this aggregate that shares in the sign of ribā, not from this aggregate known by its name and form." And this consensus is an explicit text (naṣṣ) on the necessity of seeking the cause, and transcending {PageV01P360} the requirement of the wording. And how can a fair-minded person dispute this, given the saying of the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him: "The people say that ʿUmar is the most knowledgeable of people about the chapters of ribā; and if I were knowledgeable of it, it would be dearer to me than red camels; and ribā is among the last things revealed to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and he died before he explained it to us; so leave ribā and suspicion (ar-rībah)." And if the ruling were confined to the named items, it would not be hidden from the common folk; so how [could it be hidden] from ʿUmar, given what the wording contains of detail and enumeration? How then does its ambiguity reach the point of attributing to ʿUmar a special grasp of it among all the Companions — who are the divers in the science of the Sacred Law, and the mujtahids in its sources and tributaries?

And our purpose now is the invalidity of attributing the ruling to weight, given the establishment of consensus on advancing the two precious metals for weighed items.

If they say: "Advance payment (salām) is prohibited by consensus in [the case of] being a price (thamanīyah) or being a priced thing (muthammanīyah)" — that would be an innovated arbitrariness with no basis; their doctrinal trajectory led them to it, {PageV01P361} and it has no support. And if they claim that we understood that from the consensus, we say: Why did you not understand from the consensus the specificity of the two precious metals to their own cause, as we understood it, so that you would not resort to the restriction by price-ness and priced-ness?

The second aspect of invalidation is: That attributing the ruling to measure necessitates excluding a handful (al-ḥufnah) or two handfuls from the ruling of ribā, and excluding jewelry (al-ḥulī) from it; yet ribā applies to both by virtue of the deficiency [in exchange]. Al-Shāfiʿī said: "What contradicts the resemblance (shabah) is the one that is refuted (muntaqiḍ), not the resemblance itself." For the requirement of the resemblance is the application of ribā to everything bearing the name of wheat (burr) and gold; and that applies to the small amount and to jewelry. And the wonder is that they excluded the small amount but included jewelry and the silver ring {54-b}, yet did not extend that to iron rings — by this, the contradiction of this principle is known.

If it is said: "Abū Ḥanīfah erred in his branching (tafrīʿ); it is possible to attribute the ruling to measure and extend it consistently within the genus, and apply ribā to the handful; that does not indicate that measure is unsuitable."

We say: No, rather he erred in the branching; for he intended by measure and weight their being considered (iʿtibāruhumā), not their possibility (imkānuhumā), such that Abū Yūsuf said: "Any city where meat is not weighed, there is no harm in [selling] two portions for two portions." And the handful and rings are not customarily subject to estimation (taqdīr). So if it were said that [the handful] is of the genus of the estimated, the cause would become multiple: the cause in the large amount would be that it is estimated, and in the small amount that it is of the genus of the estimated. And that would be like our saying: The large amount of wine is prohibited by the cause of intoxication (iskār), and the small amount by the cause of its being an enticement to intoxication — and these are two causes: one hidden and weak, the other strong. And dividing wheat by a multiplicity of causes is impossible and baseless. So these are two aspects for invalidating his doctrine, and al-Shāfiʿī has indicated two other aspects, suitable for preponderance (tarjīḥ), not for invalidation:

The first: That taste is the purpose (maqṣūd) of these things, and for it they were created by nature (fiṭrah) and formed; {PageV01P363} and when their purpose became manifest, people became stingy over them: so they sold them by estimation, not by guesswork (jizāf). Thus, the estimation of the specific purpose is a sign more fitting than the estimation of what runs as a protector (ʿāṣim) of the purpose. And the dirhams and dīnārs are distinguished by their specific purpose, which nothing else equals therein; so the specific being a sign for the ruling — is more dominant in conjecture (ghalabah ʿalā al-ẓann) than resorting to weight, which indicates quantity, due to stinginess in transactions.

The second: That measure is a sign of permissibility (ibāḥah), so it is unlikely to be a sign of prohibition, even if its locus differs. And we have enumerated the sign of permissibility and the sign of prohibition; and attributing the contradiction of rulings to differing signs is more dominant in conjecture than attributing it to differing loci, with the sign being unified.

And it is also preponderated by its support through his saying, peace be upon him: {«Lā tabīʿū al-ṭaʿāma bi-al-ṭaʿām»} ("Do not sell food for food").

And the refined expression (al-ʿibārah al-muḥarrarah) of our companions regarding preponderance is well-known; namely: That our cause is safe from opposition (muʿāraḍah) and contradiction (munāqaḍah), and is supported by the generality of its name, and does not depart from the ruling of its principle, and does not contradict itself. And this has been exhaustively treated in the commentaries (taʿālīq).

{PageV01P364}
[So we are not for prolixity therein; rather, the purpose is to alert to its path; for preponderance is among the avenues operative in this case, specific to it, in some of its aspects.]

If it is said: "Their cause is supported by his saying, peace be upon him: {«Illā kaylan bi-kayl»} ('Except measure for measure')."

We say: That is mentioned for deliverance (khalāṣ) from ribā; and it is considered a sign of deliverance and permissibility.

If it is said: "Imposing equivalence (mumāthalah) — in what is receptive to equivalence — is more fitting; so let the condition be known by the possibility of its occurrence; for measure and genus have an effect in manifesting the locus of the ruling; so it is more fitting to make it a sign thereof. And because ribā is legislated in conjunction with deliverance, and in attributing the ruling to taste, it is applied to quince and watermelon and what has no deliverance therein."

We say: For this, al-Shāfiʿī joined measure to taste in his [later] saying, and considered their conjunction, and said: "The saying of Ibn al-Musayyib in this is among the soundest sayings," as previously transmitted.

And this is a strong saying, gathering all aspects of the discourse; so the sign — on this saying — is the conjunction of the two matters. And perhaps he reverted from this in the new [doctrine] (al-jadīd); for reports came regarding ribā in gold jewelry, and beads sold by count. For the Prophet, peace be upon him, knew the path of its sale: in a contract that included gold beads {PageV01P365} and pearls, and silver was mentioned in the case of a mudd of ʿajwah dates; so it was known thereby that the purpose (maqṣūd) is what is followed, not the estimation. And we have established the aspect of that in the case of the handful.

If it is said: "Then your reliance on the specific purpose is an alert to the soundness of the path of Mālik — may God be pleased with him — in attributing the ruling to sustenance (qūt): for it is more specific."

We say: Were it not for the occurrence of salt, attributing the ruling to it would be more specific; but al-Shāfiʿī turned away from it because of salt.

As for his saying: "What is used to rectify sustenance (mā yustaṣliḥu bihi al-qūt) [is sustenance]" — it is corrupt: for it is {PageV01P366} either a cause on its own, like monetary-ness (naqdīyah), in which case it would necessitate, on that path, the permissibility of advancing wheat for salt — contrary to consensus; or it is said: It reverts to sustenance due to its connection to it by way of rectification (istiṣlāḥ) — and that would necessitate its transference to firewood, the oven, and what is connected to rectifying sustenance; and whenever it is transferred to those as a follower of sustenance, then its transference to fruits that serve as sustenance, and to condiments (ādām) that fall as followers of sustenance — like meat and others — is more fitting. And at that point, it collapses into the saying of taste.

And if he says: "Salt has a specificity (khāṣṣīyah) not shared by others," we say: If it is not itself sustenance, then it is another cause; so let him permit advancing the three things for it, just as advancing the two precious metals for the four things is permitted — {55-a} and that is contrary to consensus. So were it not for salt, what Mālik mentioned would be more fitting and more specific.

And in sum: Attributing the four things to a single cause is more fitting: for when the principles (uṣūl) multiply, it is like the multiplication of witnesses (shawāhid); so when they share in taste, taste is attested to from the direction of salt as well. Thus this is clarified by the path of preponderance.

If it is said: "Then let the attribution of Abū Ḥanīfah to estimation (taqdīr) for the six things be more fitting; or let the attribution of Ibn al-Mājishūn to monetary value (mālīyah) be more fitting."

We say: Weight is not measure according to Abū Ḥanīfah, as we mentioned; rather, estimation is a comprehensive expression; and for that reason, it did not extend to linear measure (dharʿ) and count (ʿadd), which are a type of estimation. As for the monetary value of Ibn al-Mājishūn, it is the broadest and most general of attributes, and the farthest from the specific purpose; and he is compelled to permit advancing the two precious metals for other than them; and therein is a division in the cause. And in sum: Do not nullify the most specific attributes — when they are sound — by the more general; for he is not taking his doctrine from resemblance and sign; perhaps he takes it from the prohibition of squandering wealth (ijtāḥ al-māl) and wasting it without recompense, gratitude, or reward; and to that reverts the equivalence of a thing to its like; then he excuses the good for the defective, with what Abū Ḥanīfah excused: of dropping the value of quality.

If it is said: "Then why do you not combine these causes?" We say: Ibn Surayj excused this: That it would take us out of the saying of the scholars (qawl al-ʿulamāʾ); and we will mention the basis of the scholars' saying. For attributing the ruling — in such a station — to two causes is not permissible, unless all are made a single cause; as al-Shāfiʿī said in his saying: That the cause is taste with estimation; and Mālik said: Sustenance, and therein is the combination of all.

{PageV01P368}

### ||| CHECK الفارق بين الطرد والشبه

### ||| AUTO القول في بيان الفارق بين الشبه والطرد

فإن قال قائل: رجع حاصل نظركم -في القاعدة السابقة -إلى أن الوصف الذي لا
يناسب، يجوز أن يكون علامة على الحكم؛ وزعمتم: أنها علامة متضمنة لوجه
المصلحة وملتزمة لها، وإن كان لا يطلع على وجه المصلحة، فما الفرق بين ذلك
وبين الوصف الطردي الذي اتفق المحققون على رده، مع الاعتراف بأن كل واحد
منهما ينفك عن المناسبة بنفسه وإنما يتوهم اشتماله على مناسبة خفية، وقضية
مصلحية: غابت عنا، وما من وصف طردي إلا ويمكن أن تدعي فيه هذه القضية، فكيف
يتميز عن الطرد المردود، مع الاستواء في هذه الخاصية؟
قلنا: هذه غمرة عظيمة خاض فيها فريق: فدرات رؤوسهم، وخارت عقولهم، ولم
يحصلوا على طائل، فمن طلب ما لم  يخلق، تعب ولم يرزق؛ فإنهم التمسوا فرقا
بين الطرد والشبه [بأمر] يرجع إلى تمييز أحدهما عن الآخر، بوصف [في] ذاته،
وأنشئ، لا يتميز عن جنسه ومثله، بوصف يرجع إلى ذاته، وها نحن نكشف الغطاء
عن هذا السر، ونقول:
الأحكام أنما تظهر -في حقنا -بعلامات منصوبة عليها؛ والعلامات للأحكام
تنقسم: إلى الأسامي اللغوية، وإلى الأوصاف الزائدة على الأسامي.
فأما المسميات المعلومة بعلامة الأسامي فهي التي يقتصر فيها PageV01P369 # على مورد النص، ولا حاجة في بيانها إلى أطناب.
وأما المعلومات بعلامات زائدة على الأسامي، فهي التي يقال فيها: أنها
قياسية، وتلك العلامات تنقسم: إلى ما يناسب الحكم في ذاتها، على ما أوضحنا
معني المناسبة، وإلى ما لا يناسب، ويعرف كونه علامة بالطرق أنتي ذكرناها في
علة الربا.
فما يناسب كله جنس واحد، يندرج تحته الشعب المنتشرة التي قدمناها.
وما لا يناسب -أيضا- كله جنس واحد: من حيث الذات والنفس؛ وهو متناول لما
سماه المسمون: شبها، ولما سموه: طردا، أيضا، فلا فرق بين الشبه والطرد، عند
النظر إلى ذات الأوصاف التي لا تناسب الأحكام.
[فالكيل والقوت والطعم] كله طرد في لغة هؤلاء واصطلاحهم؛ وإن سموه شبها:
فلا حرج في الإطلاق، وإنما الغرض بيان أن الوصف الذي لا يناسب جنس واحد
بالنظر إلى ذاته، فطلب الفرق بتمييز البعض عن البعض بالجنسية، طلب لما لا
ينال أبد الدهر.
فإن قال قائل: كيف تنكرون هذا الفرق: وأنتم مضطرون إلى الاعتراف بأن كل
وصف من الأوصاف وجد مع الحكم، لا يجوز أن يعلل الحكم به، وأن يجعل علامة
عليه، ويتبع في إثبات الحكم ونفه؛ بل هو منقسم: إلى ما يصلح الاعتماد، وإلى
ما لا يصلح؟ فما الفيصل الفارق؟ وقد سامحناكم بحذف لفظ الطرد والشبه.
قلنا: نعم؛ الأوصاف التي لا تناسب -أيضا -تنقسم [55 - ب] إلى [ما تصلح
للاعتماد عليها، وإلى ما لا تصلح]؛ كما أن المناسب أيضا
PageV01P370
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ب-ه (Sh-B-H)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Resemblance, similarity; ambiguity arising from shared attributes between two entities.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, shabah denotes an attribute that is not intrinsically suitable (munāsib) to the ruling's rationale but bears a formal likeness to a recognized effective cause (ʿillah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is visual or conceptual resemblance; here it is metaphorical (majāz) — a juristic marker that mimics suitability without substantive connection.
- Root: ط-ر-د (Ṭ-R-D)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To chase away, drive out; continuous sequence without internal coherence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṭard in legal theory is a purely arbitrary attribute — one that accompanies the ruling but has no discernible ratio legis (munāsabah); rejected by the majority of jurists.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical extension — an attribute that "runs alongside" the ruling like a shadow, lacking causal import.
- Sībawayh Rule: Distinction by Essential Genus (Tamyīz bi-al-Jins) — When two items share the same essential category (jins wāḥid), no intrinsic differentiator can be posited; differentiation must come from external criteria (e.g., evidentiary method), not from the essence itself.
chapters.translation:
I say: If a questioner asks: "The upshot of your inquiry in the preceding principle has returned to this: that an attribute which is not suitable (ghayr munāsib) may still serve as a marker (ʿalāmah) for the ruling; and you have claimed that it is a marker which embodies a facet of benefit (wajh al-maṣlaḥah) and is committed to it, even if the facet of benefit is not discerned. What then is the difference between this and the purely arbitrary attribute (al-waṣf al-ṭardī) which the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) have unanimously rejected — while acknowledging that each of the two is, in itself, dissociated from suitability (munāsabah), and that one merely conjectures its inclusion of a hidden suitability and a beneficial import (qaḍiyyah maṣlaḥiyyah) that has escaped us? For there is no arbitrary attribute except that this very claim can be made for it. How then does it become distinguished from the rejected ṭard, given their equality in this particular property?"

I reply: This is a formidable deep-water (ghamrah) into which a group plunged — their heads sank, their intellects faltered, and they obtained no gain. For whoever seeks what was not created, wearies and is not provisioned. They sought a distinction between ṭard and shabah by something that reduces to differentiating one from the other through an attribute in its own essence (dhāt) — yet a thing is not distinguished from its genus and its like by an attribute that reverts to its own essence. But here we now lift the veil from this secret, and say:

The rulings, in relation to us, become manifest only through markers (ʿalāmāt) erected upon them. And the markers of rulings divide into: linguistic names (al-asmāʾ al-lughawiyyah), and attributes superadded to the names (al-awṣāf al-zāʾidah ʿalā al-asmāʾ).

As for the named things known by the marker of names, these are those confined to the locus of the text (mawrid al-naṣṣ), and no prolixity is needed in explaining them.

As for the things known by markers superadded to the names, these are those of which it is said that they are analogical (qiyāsiyyah). And those markers divide into: what is suitable to the ruling in its own essence (yunāsib al-ḥukm fī dhātihā), according to what we have clarified of the meaning of suitability (munāsabah); and what is not suitable, yet is known to be a marker through the methods we have mentioned in the cause of ribā (ʿillat al-ribā).

Now, whatever is suitable is entirely one genus (jins wāḥid), subsuming under it the spreading branches (al-shuʿab al-muntashirah) we have previously presented.

And whatever is not suitable — likewise — is entirely one genus, in terms of essence and self (min ḥaythu al-dhāt wa al-nafs); and it encompasses what the namers have called "shabah" and what they have called "ṭard" alike. Thus there is no difference between shabah and ṭard when one looks to the essence of the attributes that are not suitable to the rulings.

[For example, the measures (kayl), the staple-ness (qūt), and the taste (ṭaʿm)] — all of these are ṭard in the language and terminology of these people; and if they call them shabah, there is no harm in the expression. The sole purpose is to clarify that the attribute which is not suitable is one genus with respect to its essence. So seeking a distinction by differentiating some from others through genus-ness (jinsiyyah) is seeking what shall never be attained for all eternity.

If a questioner says: "How can you deny this distinction, when you are compelled to acknowledge that every attribute found with a ruling — it is not permissible to make it the cause (ʿillah) of the ruling, nor to make it a marker upon it, nor to follow it in affirming or negating the ruling? Rather, it divides into what is fit for reliance and what is not fit. So what is the decisive separator (al-fayṣal al-fāriq)? And we have indulged you by dropping the terms ṭard and shabah."

I reply: Yes; the attributes that are not suitable — likewise — divide into [what is fit for reliance upon it, and what is not fit], just as the suitable also divides.

### ||| CHECK تقسيم الكلام في التعليل بما لا يناسب إلى طرفين: طرف المجتهد، وطرف المعلل

ينقسم: إلى ما يصلح للاعتماد وإلى ما لا  يصلح، ولكن ليس انقسامه لافتراق
راجع إلى الذات؛ وإنما هو بالإضافة إلى السلامة عن المعارضة بما [نقول:
أنه] أولى منه؛ وإلى عدم السلامة عنه، وهذا يستوي فيه المناسب وغير
المناسب.
وإيضاحه [هو]: بأن نقسم الكلام ونجربه في طرفين؛ أحدهما: فيما يعتمده
المجتهد، ويجوز له أن يفتي به والآخر: فيما يسمع من المعلل، ويسوغ له
الاقتصار عليه في مبتدأ التعليل، إلى أن يستنزل عنه بالاعتراض والمعارضة
بما هو أولى منه.
أما المجتهد، فلا يحل له الاعتماد على مجرد ظهور الوصف الذي لا يناسب، ما
لم يسبر سائل الأوصاف سبرا حاصرا: من حيث الإمكان والاستطاعة في حق
المجتهد، وما لم يقابل الوصف الذي ظهر هل أولا بسائر الأوصاف، فإذا قابله
بها، وأبطل جميعها أو رجح ما ظهر أولا على غيرها - على ما ذكرناه في مسئلة
علة [الربا]-حل له الاعتماد عليه: في العمل والفتوى، وهذا السبر -أيضا
-واجب [عليه] في المناسب؛ فإنا سنبين أنه لا يجوز تعليل الحكم بعلتين
مناسبتين: عرفنا PageV01P371 # بشهادة الحكم، فلا بد أن تبطل سائر الأقسام، إذا لو ظهر مناسب أقوى مما
ظهر أولا: لصار الأول بالإضافة إلى الثاني كالطرد المهجور، ولذلك لم يلتفت
إلى سلامته عن النقض والمعارضة وغيره.
وكذلك لا بد من استقصاء السبر في الأوصاف التي لا تناسب، فإن ظهر وصف لا
يناسب فبحث وسبر، فعثر على مناسب -انمحق الوصف الأول واضمحل؛ وإن لم يعثر
على مناسب، ولكن عثر على وصف آخر لا يناسب - وهو أمس للمقصود، وأخص منه
بالغرض -انمحق الأول وبطل، كما ذكرناه في الطعم بالإضافة إلى الكيل.
فإذا: كل وصف ظهر وسلم -بعد السبر -عن البطلان بظهور ما هو أولى منه، جاز
الاعتماد عليه، وهو الذي عبر عنه: بالشبه.
وكان وصف ظهر أولا، ولكن ظهر في مقابلته وصف آخر -أما على البديهة أو
بالتأمل -هو أولى وأخص من الأول: فالأول لا يجوز الاعتماد عليه، وهو الذي
يعبر عنه: بالطرد، فرجع الافتراق بين القسمين، إلى الإضافة، لا إلى الذات،
وهذا الافتراض جار في المناسبات.
فلأجل  هذا، رأينا أن نهجر عبارة الطرد والشبه: كيلا نخيل افتراقا من حيث
الذات؛ فإن فهم ما إليه رجع الافتراق، فلا حرج بعده في الإطلاقات،
والاصطلاحات بالتعريفات.
PageV01P372
وعبارة الشبه [أيضا] مستكرهة من وجه آخر، وهو: أنا قد بينا أن ذلك لا
يقوم إلا بفرع وأصل؛ وأنا نعلل النقدين بالنقدية القاصرة، ونظن أنها هي
الصفة الملتزمة المتضمنة للمصلحة الخفية الغائبة عنا، ولا فرع لهذا الأصل،
وسنذكر ما نريده بالعلة القاصرة، وندرأ عنه [اعتراض الخصوم، واستبعادهم]
وقد تبين أن الوصف الذي لا يناسب جنس واحد، وأن ظهور الفرق: بالإضافة؛
فالكيل يظهر أولا: فيظن أنه علامة؛ فيظهر الطعم -بالطريق الذي ذكرناه
-ويصير أولى منه؛ فينقلب الكيل ساقطا مطرحا؛ وقد يعبر عنه: بالطرد، وعن
الطعم - الذي صار أولى-: بالشبه، وقد يظهر بالتأمل للناظر في الطعم ويطرحه،
ويعبر عنه: بالطرد، وعن القوت: بالشبه، ثم قد يتبين له بطلان القوت بالملح
كما سبق، فينعطف إلى الطعم ويقول: هو الوصف المعتبر الذي يغلب على الظن
كونه علامة؛ ويجعل القوت طردا مهجورا.
ولا فرق بين هذه الأوصاف الثلاثة: من حيث الذات؛ وإنما
PageV01P373

### ||| CHECK الأولى التعبير بما يناسب وبما لا يناسب واطراح الشبه والطرد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-س-م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, partitioning into parts; a category or class (qism).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Logical division of a genus into species or of a whole into its constitutive parts, as in the division of legal causality (ʿillah) into valid and invalid types.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) here for actual partitioning of discourse, not metaphorically.
- Root: س-ب-ر (s-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Probing, testing, examining thoroughly; to gauge or measure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The exhaustive survey (sabr) of all possible attributes (awṣāf) to determine which qualifies as a legal cause—a technical method in uṣūl al-fiqh.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical probing extended metaphorically (majāz) to intellectual examination of attributes.
- Root: ط-ر-د (ṭ-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To drive away, expel; a rejected or discarded thing (ṭard).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, a description that is merely coincidental (ṭard) without suitability (munāsabah)—rejected as a valid cause.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical usage—an attribute "driven out" from consideration due to being superseded by a more appropriate one.
- Root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Resemblance, similarity; ambiguity (shubhah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, the "suitable" attribute (munāsib) that is deemed a valid indicator (shabah) of the ratio legis, though its suitability may be subtle.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of resemblance; here used technically for the attribute that "resembles" a true cause due to its appropriateness.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Relational Predication (al-ḥukm bi-al-iḍāfah)—when a predicate like "valid" or "invalid" is attributed not to the essence (dhāt) of a thing but to its relation (iḍāfah) to another, the syntactic structure requires clarifying the relatum (muḍāf ilayh) to avoid false essentialism.
chapters.translation:
I say: The discourse on legal causality (taʿlīl) by what is inappropriate (mā lā yunāsib) divides into two extremes: the extreme of the mujtahid, and the extreme of the one who provides the legal rationale (al-muʿallil).

It divides into what is fit for reliance (ṣāliḥ lil-iʿtimād) and what is not fit, but its division is not—due to a distinction—referable to the essence (al-dhāt); rather, it is relative (bi-al-iḍāfah) to safety from opposition (al-muʿāraḍah) by what we say is more appropriate (awlā) than it; and to the lack of safety from it. And in this, the appropriate (al-munāsib) and the inappropriate (ghayr al-munāsib) are equal.

Its clarification is this: that we divide the discourse and test it (nujarribuhu) across two extremes. One of them: what the mujtahid relies upon, and it is permissible for him to issue a legal ruling (fatwā) based on it. The other: what is heard from the muʿallil, and it is permissible for him to confine himself to it at the inception of the causal explanation (mubtadaʾ al-taʿlīl), until he is dislodged from it by objection (iʿtirāḍ) and opposition (muʿāraḍah) with what is more appropriate than it.

As for the mujtahid, it is not lawful for him to rely upon the mere emergence (ẓuhūr) of a description that is inappropriate, so long as he has not surveyed (sabara) the surveying attributes (sāʾil al-awṣāf) with an exhaustive survey (sabran ḥāṣiran)—in terms of possibility and capacity (al-imkān wa-al-istiṭāʿah) with respect to the mujtahid—and so long as he has not compared the description that emerged first with the rest of the attributes. When he compares it with them, and nullifies all of them, or gives preponderance (rajjaḥa) to what emerged first over the others—as we mentioned in the issue of the cause (ʿillah) of usury (al-ribā)—then it becomes lawful for him to rely upon it in action (al-ʿamal) and in legal ruling (al-fatwā). And this survey (al-sabr)—likewise—is obligatory upon him in the appropriate (al-munāsib); for we shall clarify that it is not permissible to explain a ruling by two appropriate causes (ʿillatayn munāsibatayn) that we have known by the testimony of the ruling (shahādat al-ḥukm). Thus, it is necessary that he nullify the rest of the categories (al-aqsām), for if an appropriate [attribute] stronger than what emerged first were to appear, the first would become—relative to the second—like the rejected coincidence (al-ṭard al-mahjūr). For this reason, no heed is paid to its safety from refutation (al-naqḍ) and opposition and other things.

Likewise, it is necessary to exhaust the survey (istiqṣāʾ al-sabr) over the attributes that are inappropriate. For if an inappropriate description emerges, and one investigates and surveys, and then stumbles upon an appropriate one—the first description is effaced (inmaḥaqa) and dissolved (iḍmaḥalla). And if he does not stumble upon an appropriate one, but stumbles upon another inappropriate description—which is more attached to the intended purpose (amassu lil-maqṣūd) and more specific to the aim (akhassu bihi bil-gharaḍ)—then the first is effaced and nullified, as we mentioned regarding taste (al-ṭaʿm) in relation to measure (al-kayl).

Thus: every description that emerges and remains safe—after the survey—from nullification by the emergence of what is more appropriate than it, it is permissible to rely upon it. And it is this that is expressed as: the suitable indicator (al-shabah).

And any description that emerged first, but then another description emerged in opposition to it—either by immediate intuition (al-badīhah) or by reflection (al-taʾammul)—which is more appropriate and more specific than the first: then the first is not permissible to rely upon, and it is this that is expressed as: the rejected coincidence (al-ṭard). So the distinction (al-iftirāq) between the two categories reverts to relation (al-iḍāfah), not to essence (al-dhāt). And this supposition (al-iftirāḍ) is operative in the appropriate [attributes] as well.

For this reason, we have seen fit to abandon the expressions "ṭard" and "shabah"—so that we do not suggest a distinction in terms of essence. For once one understands that to which the distinction reverts, there is no harm thereafter in the unrestricted usages (al-iṭlāqāt) and the technical terminologies (al-iṣṭilāḥāt) with their definitions.

And the expression "shabah"—likewise—is objectionable (mustakrahah) from another aspect, namely: that we have clarified that it does not stand except upon a branch (farʿ) and a root (aṣl). And we explain the two monetary commodities (al-naqdayn) by the deficient suitability (al-naqdiyyah al-qāṣirah), and we suppose that it is the binding attribute (al-ṣifah al-multazimah) that entails the hidden interest (al-maṣlaḥah al-khafiyyah) that is absent from us. And there is no branch for this root. And we shall mention what we intend by the deficient cause (al-ʿillah al-qāṣirah), and we shall repel against it the objection of the opponents and their deeming it improbable (istibʿāduhum).

And it has become clear that the inappropriate description is a single genus (jins wāḥid), and that the emergence of the distinction is by relation (bi-al-iḍāfah). For measure (al-kayl) emerges first, so one supposes it is a sign (ʿalāmah); then taste (al-ṭaʿm) emerges—by the path we mentioned—and becomes more appropriate than it; so measure is overturned, becoming discarded and cast aside (sāqiṭan maṭraḥan). And it may be expressed as: ṭard, and taste—which has become more appropriate—as: shabah. And it may emerge by reflection to the examiner that taste [itself] is [superseded], and he discards it, and expresses it as: ṭard, and nourishment (al-qūt) as: shabah. Then it may become clear to him the nullification of nourishment by salt (al-milḥ)—as previously mentioned—so he turns back to taste and says: it is the considered attribute (al-waṣf al-muʿtabar) that predominates in conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann) that it is a sign; and he makes nourishment a discarded ṭard.

And there is no difference among these three attributes—in terms of essence; rather, [the difference is] only by relation.

The first [section]: the expression by what is appropriate and what is inappropriate, and the abandonment of "shabah" and "ṭard."

chapters.title_en: The Division of Attributes into Suitable and Unsuitable, and the Refutation of the Terms "Ṭard" and "Shabah"
chapters.arabic_text:
افترقت: بالإضافات، فلهذا استكرهنا عبارة الطرد والشبه: فإنه يوهم جنسين
مختلفين، ولا اختلاف: إذ الطارد يزعم أنه شبه بين الفرع والأصل، بما ذكره
من الوصف؛ وتسميته شبها -بهذا التأويل -صحيح، والمشبه يسمي: طاردا، من حيث
أنه أتي بوصف لا يناسب، وتسميته طاردا -بهذا التأويل -صحيح.
فلم يكن [لفظ] الطرد والشبه إلا مشوشا ومعميا لمقصود الكلام؛ فوجب اطراحه
والقول بأن الأوصاف تنقسم إلى [ما يناسب] وإلى [ما لا يناسب]؛ وغير المناسب
ينقسم إلى ما يسلم عن المعارضة [56 - أ] بعلامة هي أولى منه؛ فيصلح لاعتماد
المجتهد [عليه] بعد البر؛ وإلى ما لا يسلم عن وصف هو أولى منه، وهذا ينقسم
فمنه: ما يكون قرب وصف آخر معلوما بالبديهة، [ومنه: ما يعلم بالنظر.
فما يعلم بعده، وقرب غيره، وكونه أولى منه بالديهة]-فهو: الطرد القبيح
الذي لا يتصور أن  يكون معول مجتهد.
وما يعلم كون غيره أولى منه بالتأمل، يتصور أن يختلف في العثور عليه
المجتهدون بحسب اختلاف قرائحهم؛ فيسميه من لم يعثر على PageV01P374 # الأولى: شبها، ومن عثر على الأولى يسمي الآخر: طردا.
فإن قيل: فهلا حددتم الوصف المعتمد -الذي عبر عنه فريق بالشبه -[بالوصف]
الخاص، أو بالمقصود - كما قاله المعبرون - لتمييز الشبه عن الطرد؟
قلنا: لأن الخاص إضافة؛ فالشيء يكون خاصا: بالإضافة إلى شيء، عاما:
بالإضافة إلى غيره، فالطعم خاص بالإضافة إلى المالية، عام بالإضافة إلى
القوت، والقوت خاص بالإضافة إلى الطعم، عام بالإضافة إلى الذات المسمي باسم
البر والتمر، والأخص غير مشروط بالاتفاق عند القائلين بالشبه؛ فإن الأخص في
النقدين: النقدية؛ ولم يبطل الوزن بالإضافة إليه لأنه أعم: إذا لو بطل
لذلك، لبطل الطعم بالإضافة إلى القوت: لأنه أعم.
وأما المقصود فليس يشترط في صحة التشبيه -عند المطلقين لهذه اللفظة -أن
يقع التشبيه بالمقصود؛ وإنما يساعد ذلك في الربا، وقد يكون الشبه خلقيا،
وقد يكون حكميا؛ فكيف يصح [حد الشبه] بهذا؟
فإن قيل: وهلا حددتموه بما حده به القاضي -رضي الله عنه -: من أنه الذي
يغلب على الظن كونه في معنى الأصل؟
PageV01P375
قلنا: لا حجر في هذه العبارات؛ وهي حاوية للمقصود إجمالا، ولكن لا بيان
فيه، فلم يشكل إلا تمييز الوصف: الذي يغلب على الظن الاشتراك [فيه
الاشتراك] في الحكم؛ عن الوصف: الذي لا يغلب -بحد فاصل، ومعيار صادق: نرتفع
به المنازعات، وهذه عبارة متسعة تشمل جميع أنواع القياس.
ونحن الآن في طلب الوصف الذي يغلب، وتمييزه عما لا يغلب؛ أهو متميز
[بذاته]؟ أم بالإضافة؟ فأقول: إذا كان الكل لا يناسب، فالتمييز: بالإضافة
التي ذكرناها.
فإن قيل: فهلا حددتموه: بأنه الوصف الذي يوهم الاجتماع في مخيل مبهم هو
مأخذ الحكم، كما قاله القاضي؟
قلنا: ولا حجر -أيضا -في إطلاق هذه العبارة، لمن يبغي عبارة حاصرة؛ لا
لمن يبغي كشفا ووضوحا، فإنا رأينا جملة من الأوصاف تذكر [في محافل ومجامع،
تجمع أفاضل وأكابر]؛ فتختلف آراؤهم [وتتفرق أهواءهم] في  أنها من الأوصاف
التي توهم الاجتماع في المخيل: فتسمي شبها؛ أو لا توهم: فتسمي طردا، فلم
يتجنس هذا PageV01P376 # الوصف عندهم، ولم يتميز بعلامة يترفع معها النزاع، وإذا رد الأمر إلى ما
يغلب [على الظن] أو ما يوهم؛ اختلف ذلك بالطباع والقرائح: على ما نشاهد ذلك
من الفقهاء في المناظرات، وهي الخصومة الناشبة التي لا سبيل إلى قطعها.
فيقول القائل: طهارة حكمية، فتفتقر إلى النية كالتيمم؛ أو: عبادة يبطلها
الحدث، فتفتقر إلى الموالاة كالصلاة؛ أو: عبادة مختلفة الأركان يستحب
الترتيب في متماثلاتها، فيستحق في مختلفاتها قياسا للوضوء على الصلاة.
ويقول في افتراض الفاتحة في الصلاة: عبادة ذات تحليل وتحريم، فيشترط في
أركانها ما يتعدد سبعا كالحجج.
فهذا وأمثاله يعرض على الجمع من الفقهاء، فلا يتفق رأي اثنين منهم في أن
هذه [هل] تغلب على الظن، أو هل توهم الاجتماع؟ بل يقول فريق: الكل طرد،
ويقول آخرون: الكل شبه، وتقول طائفة: ما ذكره في نية الطهارة تشبيه، لكثرة
تكررها على اللسان، فهو مغلب؛ وما ذكره -من القياس على الحجج -فطرد، وما
ذكره -من الترتيب والموالاة في الطهارة -فمعتدل؛ وهو محتمل لأن يقال: أنه
طرد ولأن يقال: أن شبه، وكل ذلك لعدولهم عن المنهاج السديد PageV01P377 # [والصراط المستقيم]، وظنهم أن الفرق راجع إلى ذات هذه الأوصاف، هيهات
هيهات، إنما افتراقها: لخفاء الأوصاف المقابلة لها مرة، ولجلائها [أخرى]،
فقولنا: حكمية، يقابلها: أنها طهارة بالتراب والوضوء بالماء، وقولنا:
يبطلها الحدث كالصلاة، يعارضها: أن الكلام لا يبطلها، بخلاف الصلاة، إلى
أمثال لذلك لا نستقصيها، بل [نجتزي بالتنبيه لمن يفهمها ويعيها]، فهذه
الأوصاف المتقابلة، كلها طرد غير مناسب كما ذكرناه في الربا، فطريق نصبها
علامة وترجيح البعض منها على البعض -ما سبق، فإذا استنهج المجتهد الطريق
[56 - ب]، واستتم السبر والتحقيق، [وشاء الله التوفيق] يحصل بالآخرة على ظن
[غالب مستقر: يتكل عليه، و] يطمئن إليه.
الطرف الثاني: الكلام في المعلل، فإن قيل: ما ذكر تموه سياق نظر المجتهد،
فما الموظف على المجادل في ابتداء التعليل؟ وبماذا تنقطع عنه  المطالبة؟
أيلزم أن يستوفي السبر ويبطل الصفات الفارقة بعد أن يحصرها؟ أم يكتفي منه
بالاقتصار على ما أبداه، ويقال: على من ادعي بطلانه، إظهار ما يراه أولى أو
مماثلا له، حتى يتكلم عليه،
PageV01P378
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ر-د (ṭ-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To drive away, repel, expel; a thing that is cast off or rejected.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, ṭard denotes an attribute that is merely concomitant without any rational suitability (munāsabah) for the ruling—thus it is "repelled" from consideration.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical expulsion; metaphorically, it is the dismissal of an attribute from legal efficacy due to its lack of appropriateness.
- Root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Resemblance, similarity, ambiguity; that which is alike in form or quality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic method, shabah is an attribute that suggests a commonality (jāmiʿ) between the branch (farʿ) and root (aṣl) in the ratio legis (ʿillah), even if not fully suitable.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: visual likeness; metaphorical: a conjectural parity in legal causation, distinct from ṭard which lacks any such parity.
- Root: م-خ-ي-ل (m-kh-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To imagine, to fancy; a place of imagination (makhīl).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "imaginal locus" (makhīl) is the mental construct where the attribute is perceived as the source (maʾkhadh) of the ruling—central to Ghazali's theory of munāsabah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: imaginative faculty; technical: the conceptual space where suitability is intuited, not empirically verified.
- Root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To look, consider, deliberate; theoretical reflection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Naẓar is the disciplined intellectual inquiry that distinguishes the suitable from the unsuitable in legal analogy (qiyās).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: sight; metaphorical: rational scrutiny (ijtihād) as opposed to mere intuition (badīhah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqābūl (Contrastive Pairing) — In conditional and disjunctive constructions, the syntactic balance between opposing terms (e.g., "what is suitable" vs. "what is unsuitable") requires parallel grammatical structures to preserve logical clarity, as seen in the repeated "fa-minhu... wa-minhu" (from it... and from it) divisions.
chapters.translation:
I say: They have diverged [in terminology] due to relational additions (bi-al-iḍāfāt). For this reason, we have found the expressions "ṭard" (repulsion) and "shabah" (resemblance) objectionable—since they suggest two distinct genera, whereas there is no real distinction. For the one who employs ṭard claims that there is a resemblance between the branch (al-farʿ) and the root (al-aṣl) by virtue of the attribute he mentions; and calling it "shabah" under this interpretation is correct. Likewise, the one who employs shabah calls it "ṭard" insofar as he has brought an attribute that is not suitable (lā yunāsib); and calling it "ṭard" under this interpretation is also correct.

Thus, the terms "ṭard" and "shabah" have become nothing but confusing and obscuring of the intended meaning of the discourse. It is therefore obligatory to discard them and to state instead that attributes are divided into [what is suitable (munāsib)] and [what is not suitable (ghayr munāsib)]. The unsuitable is further divided into: that which is immune from counter-argument (muʿāraḍah) [56-a] by a marker (ʿalāmah) that is more appropriate (awlā) than it—this being fit for the mujtahid to rely upon after thorough investigation (baʿd al-barr); and that which is not immune from an attribute more appropriate than it. This latter division itself splits: from it, there is that whose remoteness, the proximity of another attribute, and its being more appropriate are known by immediate intuition (bi-al-badīhah)—and this is the reprehensible ṭard (al-ṭard al-qabīḥ) which cannot conceivably serve as a support for any mujtahid. And there is that whose being surpassed by another attribute is known through reflection (bi-al-naẓar); it is conceivable that mujtahids differ in discovering it according to the variance of their natural faculties (qarāʾiḥ). Thus, the one who has not discovered the more appropriate [attribute] (al-awlā) calls it "shabah," while the one who has discovered the more appropriate calls the other "ṭard."

If it is said: "Why did you not define the relied-upon attribute—which a group has termed 'shabah'—by [the attribute of] specificity (al-khāṣṣ), or by purposiveness (al-maqṣūd), as those who used these expressions have said, in order to distinguish shabah from ṭard?"

We say: Because specificity is a relational matter (iḍāfah). A thing is specific relative to one thing and general relative to another. Thus, taste (al-ṭaʿm) is specific relative to monetary value (al-māliyyah) but general relative to nutritive substance (al-qūt); and nutritive substance is specific relative to taste but general relative to the essence named "wheat" or "dates." Moreover, the more specific (al-akhaṣṣ) is not conditioned upon agreement (al-ittifāq) according to those who affirm shabah. For the more specific in the two precious metals (al-naqdayn) is their monetary character (al-naqdiyyah); yet weight (al-wazn) is not invalidated relative to it merely because it is more general—for if it were invalidated for that reason, then taste would be invalidated relative to nutritive substance, since it is more general.

As for purposiveness (al-maqṣūd), it is not a condition for the validity of shabah—according to those who employ this term absolutely—that the resemblance be grounded in the purpose. Rather, this holds only in the case of ribā (usury). For shabah may be of a natural/creational kind (khilqī) or of a legal/verdictive kind (ḥukmī). So how could the definition of shabah be sound through this?

If it is said: "Why did you not define it as the Qāḍī (Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī)—may God be pleased with him—defined it: that it is what predominantly prevails upon conjecture (ghalabat ʿalā al-ẓann) that it is in the meaning of the root?"

We say: There is no restriction in these expressions; they encompass the intended meaning in summary (ijmālan), but they contain no elucidation (bayān). The difficulty lies solely in distinguishing the attribute whose sharedness in the ruling is predominantly conjectured from the attribute whose sharedness is not so conjectured—by a decisive boundary (ḥadd fāṣil) and a truthful criterion (miʿyār ṣādiq) through which disputes are elevated. This expression is expansive, encompassing all types of qiyās.

We are now in pursuit of the attribute that prevails [upon conjecture], and its distinction from that which does not prevail. Is it distinguished by its own essence (bi-dhātihi) or by relation (bi-al-iḍāfah)? I say: When the whole [set of attributes] is unsuitable, then the distinction is by the relation we have mentioned.

If it is said: "Why did you not define it as the attribute that suggests (yūhim) commonality in an indeterminate imaginal locus (makhīl mubham) that is the source of the ruling, as the Qāḍī said?"

We say: There is likewise no restriction in uttering this expression for one who seeks a comprehensive phrase; but not for one who seeks disclosure and clarity. For we have observed a number of attributes mentioned in assemblies and gatherings that bring together the virtuous and the eminent; yet their opinions diverge and their inclinations scatter as to whether these attributes are of the kind that suggest commonality in the imaginal locus—thus termed "shabah"—or do not suggest it—thus termed "ṭard." This attribute has not been rendered a distinct genus (mutajannisan) for them, nor has it been distinguished by a marker that would remove dispute. And when the matter is referred to what prevails upon conjecture or what suggests [commonality], it varies according to natural temperaments (ṭibāʿ) and faculties (qarāʾiḥ)—as we witness this among jurists in disputations, which are the entrenched contentions that have no way to be severed.

Thus one says: "It is a verdictive purity (ṭahārah ḥukmiyyah), so it requires intention (niyyah) like tayammum." Or: "It is an act of worship (ʿibādah) that is nullified by hadath (ritual impurity), so it requires continuity (muwālāh) like prayer." Or: "It is an act of worship with diverse pillars (mukhtalifat al-arkān) where sequencing (tartīb) is recommended in its homogeneous parts, so it is owed in its heterogeneous parts, by analogy (qiyāsan) of wuḍūʾ upon prayer." And he says regarding the obligation of the Fātiḥah in prayer: "It is an act of worship possessing tahlīl (opening takbīr) and taḥrīm (closing salām), so its pillars require that which is repeated sevenfold, like the circuits (ashwāṭ) of the ḥajj."

Such examples are presented to assemblies of jurists, yet no two of them agree in opinion as to whether these [attributes] prevail upon conjecture or suggest commonality. Rather, one group says: "All of it is ṭard." Another group says: "All of it is shabah." And a faction says: "What he mentioned regarding the intention in purity is a resemblance (tashbīh), due to its frequent repetition on the tongue—so it prevails; what he mentioned—of the analogy upon the circuits of ḥajj—is ṭard; and what he mentioned—of sequencing and continuity in purity—is moderate (muʿtadil), admitting both the claim that it is ṭard and the claim that it is shabah." All of this stems from their deviation from the sound path (al-minhāj al-sadīd) [and the straight road], and their assumption that the difference reverts to the essences of these attributes themselves. Far be it, far be it! Their divergence is only due to the concealment of the opposing attributes (al-awṣāf al-muqābilah) at times, and their clarity at others. For our statement "verdictive" is countered by [the opponent's saying]: "It is a purity by earth (turāb) and wuḍūʾ by water." Our statement "nullified by hadath like prayer" is countered by: "Speech (kalām) does not nullify it, unlike prayer." And so on with similar examples that we do not exhaust, but suffice with an indication for those who understand and comprehend them. These opposing attributes are all ṭard, unsuitable, as we mentioned in the case of ribā. So the way to establish one of them as a marker and to prefer some over others is what has preceded. When the mujtahid follows this path [56-b], completes the examination (al-sabr) and verification (al-taḥqīq), and God wills success (tawfīq), he will ultimately attain a settled predominant conjecture (ẓann ghālib mustaqirr) upon which he relies and to which his heart is at peace.

The second side: The discourse on the one who provides the ratio (al-muʿallil). If it is said: "What you have mentioned is the course of the mujtahid's reflection. So what is incumbent upon the disputant (al-mujādil) at the inception of the causal explanation (taʿlīl)? And by what does the demand for proof (al-muṭālabah) cease against him? Is he obligated to exhaust the examination (sabr) and invalidate the distinguishing attributes (al-ṣifāt al-fāriqah) after enumerating them? Or is he content with restricting himself to what he has presented, and it is said: 'Upon the one who claims its invalidity is to show what he deems more appropriate or equivalent to it, so that he may be engaged upon it'?"

chapters.title_en: The Variation of Terminologies Across Different Regions
chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| CHECK إختلاف بعض المصطلحات باختلاف الأمكنة

ويجعل الوصف الذي ذكره أول رتبة من مراتب النظر، ومرقاة من مراقية؛ إلى
أن يستنزل عنه بالمعارضة بمثله، أو بما هو أولى منه.
قلنا: ليس هذا السؤال عن مسئلة شرعية، حتى يفتي فيها بتحليل أو تحريم، أو
إثبات أو نفين لا كالطرف السابق: فإن النظر فيه يتعلق بقطب ديني عظيم،
وإنما هذه مسئلة جدلية؛ والجدليات رسميات واصطلاحات، وكل فريق اصطلحوا على
أمر، فالوجه أن يساعدهم الواحد الفرد، ويندس في غمارهم، ويكلمهم بمعتادهم،
هذا هو الأصل بعد استمرار العادات، وترسخ الاصطلاحات.
نعم: لو سئلنا عن أولى ما يصطلح عليه، وأليقه بمقصود الجدال ومصلحته؛ فقد
نبدي فيه ما نبديه، فنقول: أما الذين ذهبوا إلى [أنه لا يقبل] إلا المؤثر
-وهو المراوزة وأهل سمرقند في عصرنا هذا -فلا يقطعون المطالبة إلا بإبداء
التأثير؛ وقد يطلق الإنسان فيما بينهم الإخالة، فتنفر طباعهم، [وتشمئز
نفوسهم] لرؤيتهم في كتاب أبي زيد -أن الإخالة باطلة في الجدال.
فطريق المناظر معهم، أولا: أن يهجر لقب الإخالة، ويسمي مخيلة: مؤثرا؛
ووجه الإخالة: تأثيرا، ويظهر الإخالة بلقب التأثير، فيروح عليهم -بعد
التلقيب بهذا اللقب -كل ما سميناه مخلا PageV01P379 # مناسبا، كما [تقدم التفصيل فيه]. فمن استمسك- مع هؤلاء- بعلامة لا تناسب،
ولم تقطع المطالبة عنه- فطريقه: أن يقيم البرهان الأصولي على جواز التعليل
بالوصف الذي لا يناسب، كما قدمناه، فيبتدئ بالإيماء، والإضافة اللفظية، ثم
ينحدر إلى الحكم عقيب الوقائع، ثم إلى الطرد والعكس، ثم إلى الشبه، وهو:
إعلام الحكم بعلامة لا تناسب. أو يضرب لهم الأمثال نقلا عن الأئمة، ويقرر
طريق الظن وثورانه من الوصف الذي لا يناسب، كما تقدم في مسئلة علة الربا-:
إن صادف من نفسه منة التقرير، وساعدته حشمة: يستميل [بها] أساعهم للإصغاء
إلى كلامه، إلى أن ينهيه إلى تمامه. فإن لم  يجد هذه المنة، ولم تساعده هذه
القوة [والحشمة] فليكلمهم بلسانهم، وليلقب كل ما سنح له-: من الخيالات
البعيدة الإقناعية- بلقب التأثير؛ فيروج عليهم الغث والسمين، والنازل
والثمين؛ وتنقطع عنه المطالبة وينغمس في غمرة المسئلة.
PageV01P380
وإن جرت المناظرة مع فريق: يجوزون التعليل بغير المؤثر؛ فهؤلاء- أيضا-
ينقسمون:
فأهل بغداد وسائر العراقيين، يلقبون هذا الجنس: بقياس الدلالة؛ فإذا ذكر
وصفا غير مؤثر: فليلقبه بهذا اللقب، ليقطع المطالبة عنه.
وإن جرت المناظرة بنيسابور-[ومجامعها- في غالب الأمر، غاصة بالمتلقفين]
من أستاذنا إمام الحرمين- قدس الله روحه- فليذكر من الأوصاف غير المناسبة،
ما يراه سديدا: غالبا على الظن، سليما عن المعارضة؛ وليلقبه بلقب الشبه،
وإياه والاعتراف بأنه طرد؛ فيعظم ثوران المستمعين وإنكارهم عليه، وتنفر عنه
الطباع، وتنبو عن كلامه الأسماع؛ بحيث لا يصغى بعده إلى كلامه، ولا يزاد
على الاستهزاء والتهجين، وليروج عليهم كل وصف طردي لا يناسب، بلقب الشبه
[فهو رائج]؛ ولا تتوجه عليه إلا مطالبات بيان وجه التشبيه. فإذا أخذ في
كلامه، وقرر وجه الجمع، وذكر: أنه لا فارق إلا كيت وكيت وهي باطلة، وأن لا
مسلك للقول بالتشبيه إلا هذا- تلقى ذلك منه بالقبول، وانقلب الاستبعاد من
جملتهم إلى المطالب، فهذا هو الطريق في [مجاملة هؤلاء الفرق ومجادلتهم].
PageV01P381
