chapters.arabic_text:
الحكم، وهو- على التحقيق- راجع إلى تتمة المقدمة الأولى. وهو الاشتراك في
السبب. فإن كانت المقدمتان معلومتين: لم تختلف فيه القرائح، وعبر عنه: بأنه
في معنى الأصل. وإن كانتا مظنونتين: أمكن تقرير النزاع فيه. ومن عرف هذه
الحقائق فلا حرج عليه في إطلاق العبارات.
مثال القسم الثاني- وهو: ما عرف كونه مناطا بالإضافة اللفظية- كقوله عليه
السلام: «من أعتق شركا له في عبد قوم عليه الباقي». فهذا بطريق الترتيب
بصيغة الجزاء والشرط. وقوله عليه السلام: «إذا ولغ الكلب في إناء أحدكم،
فليغسله سبعا إحداهن بالتراب» وهذا من طريق الترتيب بفاء التعقيب، وهو-
أيضا- للتسبيب. فقد علم- على الجملة- بمجرد سماع الحديث الأول أن إعتاق أحد
الشريكين نصيبه سبب للسراية إلى الباقي، وأنه موجب له ومناط لحكمه، وإنما
النظر: في تنقيح المناط بإلغاء قيود وإبقائها.
ففي قوله: أعتق «قيد عن البيع والطلاق وسائر التصرفات، وفي قوله: شركا»
قيد عن نصف العبد المستخلص، والبعض المعتق من العبد.
PageV01P422
[وفي قوله: له» قيد عن إعتاقه ملك الغير]. وفي قوله: من عبد قيد عن الأمة.
فأما قيد العتق فمرعى؛ فمن باع شركا له في عبد: لا يسري إلى الباقي ولا
يقوم عليه؛ إذ عرف بالشرع نوع قوة وغلبة المعتق لم تعرف للبيع؛ ولذلك
يستدعى البيع شرائط يفسد بفواتها، ويفسد بزيادة شرط فاسد، إلى غير ذلك من
الأمور، فلم يلغ هذا القيد.
نعم: لو ألحق به طلاق البعض وحكم بسرايته، فله وجه: لأن الطلاق والعتاق
قريبان [61 - ب] في الشرع: في القوة والنفوذ وقبول التعليق بالاغرار  وغيره
فيظهر تساويهما في عدم قبول التجزي.
وأما قوله: شركا فهو قيد عن نصف العبد المستخلص، وهو ملغي: فإن السراية
إلى ملكة تلتحق بالسراية إلى ملك الغير بطريق الأولى، وجرى التقييد بالشرك
للعادة.
وقوله: له قيد معتبر لا يلتحق به توجهه العتاق على نصيب الشريك، لأن ذلك
يخرج العتق عن كونه عتقا: [فإنه] لا ينفذ بنفسه.
وأما قوله: من عبد» فقيد محذوف: لأن الأمة في السبب كالعبد؛ PageV01P423 # ولا مدخل للأنوثة في تغيير ما يناط بالعتق والرق، وإنما جرى ذكر العبد
وفاقا بسبقه إلى اللسان. كقوله عليه السلام: «أيما رجل مات أو أفلس، فصاحب
المتاع أحق بمتاعه». والمعني بالرجل: الجنس. وكان إلغاء هذه القيود مستندا
إلى فهم عادة البيان، إذ الفصيح قد يبين الجنس بذكر بعض الصور. كقول القائل
مثلا: من باع ثوبا زال ملكه، وهو يريد به جميع الأمتعة: من الفرش والدار.
ولكن نبه بالبعض على الكل. وبذكر واحد من الجملة على الجملة. فهذا ما يجزئا
على إلغاء هذه القيود المصرح بها، مع [ما] تقدم: من الاشتراك في السبب،
ورجوع الافتراق إلى ما يعرف أنه لا مدخل له [في الحكم]. وذلك قد يعلم كما
ذكرناه. وقد يظن كقولنا في إعتاق البعض المعين. فإنا نقول: السبب- بعد
التنقيح- هو: إعتاق بعض الرقيق، وهذا بعض، ولا أثر للشيوع؛ ولكن خروج
الشيوع عن كونه داخلا في التأثير، مظنون غير معلوم.
والغرض أن المظنون والمعلوم من هذه الجملة، دائر على مراتب في النظر
معقولة، تترقى عن لا شبه المختلف فيه. والمنكرون لذلك الجنس قائلون بهذا
الفن، لا محالة.
فأما قوله عليه السلام «إذا ولغ الكلب في إناء أحدكم فليغسله»، فالولوغ
مقيد عن الكروع وغيره. والكلب قيد عن سائر الحيوانات، حتى PageV01P424 # الخنزير، والإناء قيد عن الثوب وغيره. وقوله: فليغسله» قيد عن فعل آخر:
من لفرك والتشميس وغيره؛ وقيد عن غسل غير صاحب الإناء. وقوله: سبعا» قيد عن
سائر الأعداد سواه. وقوله: إحداهن بالتراب» قيد عن الصابون والأشنان وغيره.
فلينظر الناظر: كيف يتصرف في هذه القيود؟ فنقول: المعقول  الجملي أو تغليظ
الشرع نجاسة هذا الحيوان.
فأما الولوغ، ففي معناه الكروع: لأنه دل على نجاسة سؤره، وعرقه عند
الشافعي- رضي الله عنه- في معنى لعابه، وأبو حنيفة لا يراه في معناه، ويرى
هذا القيد مرعيا. وذلك: لتنازعهما في آن PageV01P425 # المعقول من الحديث نجاسة الكلب، أو نجاسة سؤره على الخصوص؟ وهذا أمر فهمي
عقلي، وقد يستمد من [شواهد] الشرع. فعند الشافعي- رضي الله عنه- جرى ذكر
الولوغ على الغالب، تنبيها على النجاسة المطلقة، كما جرى ذكر الإناء على
الغالب: فإنه يغسل الثوب من لعابه اتفاقا، كما يغسل من ولوغه الإناء، فذكر
الإناء تنبيه على الجنس: إذ العادة أن الكلب [إنما] يلغ في الأواني.
وأما تخصيص الكلب، [< ف > لم يمكن الغاؤه]، وإلحاق سائر الحيوانات أو
الحيوان الذي لا يؤكل لحمه، أو السباع [به]. فإن الكلب سبع وحيوان وغير
مأكول اللحم وكلب؛ فكان لخصوص وصفه، أثر في التنجيس؛ عرف ذلك من شواهد
الشرع: في تخصيصه بمزايد التغليظ والتشديد، فلم يلغ هذا القيد. نعم: ينقدح
تردد في الخنزير؛ فإنه أخوه: في نظر الشرع، والأمر باجتنابها وتحريمها
وتنجيسها، فيحتمل أن يقال: يغسل من [نجاسته سبعا]، فإنهما أخوان كالطلاق
والعتاق. على ما ذكرناه في قضية السراية؛ فكأنا نعلل نجاسته بتغليظ أمره في
الشرع؛ PageV01P426 # ونلحق به الخنزير على رأي، وهو من قبيل القياس المناسب المستنبط، لا من
قبيل المناط.
أما قوله: فليغسله» فلا يلتحق به الفرك والتشميس [ولا غيره]، لما عرف: من
أثر الغسل في الشرع. ثم هو متناول للغسل بكل مائع؛ ولكنا نزيد قيدا: فنقيده
بالغسل بالماء، لما عرف: من اختصاص الماء.
وكما أن ذكر بعض القيود بالعادة من جملة البيان، فإخلال البعض- أيضا-
اتكالا على الفهم بالعادة- من جملة البيان.
فأما تقييده عن غسل غير صاحب الإناء، فساقط؛ فالمفهوم وجوب الإزالة [62 -
أ] ولكن ذكر صاحب الإناء على العادة.
وأما قوله: سبعا» فلا يقوم مقامه عدد آخر.
وأما قوله: بالتراب» فاختلف فيه؛ فمنهم من ألحق به الصابون والأشنان،
وقال: المعقول مزيد تغليظ بجمع غير الماء إلى الماء، وذكر
PageV01P427
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is prevention and sound judgment; al-ḥukm is the firm decisiveness that prevents one from proceeding otherwise.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, al-ḥukm is the divine address (khiṭāb) concerning the acts of the legally responsible (mukallaf), whether by way of requirement, prohibition, or permission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is the binding verdict; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the ratio legis (ʿillah) as the "judge" of the case.
- Root: س-ب-ب (s-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A rope by which water is drawn; hence, a means or path leading to an end.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Al-sabab is that by which one reaches a goal; in legal theory, it is the manifest attribute (waṣf ẓāhir) that is made the sign (amārah) for the ruling.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is the physical cord; metaphorical is any causal connection, as in "his wealth was the cause of his ruin."
- Root: ن-ط-ق (n-ṭ-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To articulate, to utter; al-manāṭ is the place where something is tied or suspended.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Al-manāṭ is the locus of attachment; in uṣūl, it is the attribute upon which the ruling is hung (taʿlīq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is the tied cord; metaphorical is the operative attribute (al-waṣf al-muʾaththir) that the jurist seeks to identify.
- Root: ق-ي-د (q-y-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bind, to fetter; al-qayd is a restriction or condition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taqyīd is the specification of a general term by an attribute; ilghāʾ al-qayd is the nullification of that restriction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is the physical shackle; metaphorical is any limiting condition in speech.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq and Jazāʾ (Conditional Suspension) — In the Prophetic statement «من أعتق شركا له في عبد قوم عليه الباقي», the conditional particle (man) and the resumption (jazāʾ) with the verb (qawwama) establish a causal nexus (sababiyyah) between the act of manumission and the financial assessment, requiring the interpreter to isolate the operative attribute.
chapters.translation:
I say: The ruling — and in truth, it reverts to the completion of the first premise — is the commonality in the cause (al-ishtirāk fī al-sabab). For if the two premises are known (maʿlūmatān), then natural dispositions (qarāʾiḥ) do not differ concerning it, and it is expressed by saying: it is in the meaning of the original (fī maʿnā al-aṣl). But if they are merely probable (maẓnūnatān), then the dispute concerning it can be established. Whoever knows these realities incurs no blame in employing the expressions [freely].

An example of the second division — namely, that whose being the locus (manāṭ) is known by way of verbal addition (al-iḍāfah al-lafẓiyyah) — is his saying, peace be upon him: «من أعتق شركا له في عبد قوم عليه الباقي» ("Whoever manumits a share he owns in a slave, the remainder is assessed against him"). This is by way of ordering (al-tartīb) through the formula of the condition and the consequent (ṣīghat al-jazāʾ wa al-sharṭ). And his saying, peace be upon him: «إذا ولغ الكلب في إناء أحدكم، فليغسله سبعا إحداهن بالتراب» ("When a dog laps from the vessel of one of you, let him wash it seven times, one of them with earth") — this is by way of ordering through the fāʾ of immediate succession (fāʾ al-taʿqīb), and it too indicates causation (al-tasbīb). Thus it is known, in sum, merely by hearing the first hadith, that the manumission of one of two partners of his share is a cause (sabab) for the transmission (al-sarāyah) to the remainder, that it necessitates it, and that it is the locus (manāṭ) of its ruling. The only consideration is in refining the locus (tanqīḥ al-manāṭ) by nullifying certain restrictions (qayūd) and retaining others.

For in his saying "manumits" (aʿtaqa), there is a restriction excluding sale, divorce, and all other dispositions. In his saying "a share" (shirkan), there is a restriction excluding the half of the slave that is singled out (al-niṣf al-mustakhlaṣ) and the part manumitted from the slave. [And in his saying "he owns" (lahu), there is a restriction excluding the manumission of another's property.] In his saying "from a slave" (min ʿabd), there is a restriction excluding the female slave (al-amah).

As for the restriction of manumission (al-ʿitq), it is observed (murʿan); for whoever sells a share he owns in a slave, [the sale] does not transmit to the remainder, nor is [the remainder] assessed against him — since it is known by the Law (al-sharʿ) that manumission possesses a kind of force and dominance (qūwah wa ghalabah) not known for sale. For this reason, sale requires conditions whose absence corrupts it, and it is corrupted by the addition of a corrupt condition, and other such matters. Thus this restriction is not nullified.

Indeed, if one were to annex to it the divorce of a part (ṭalāq al-baʿḍ) and rule its transmission, that would have a basis: for divorce and manumission are close in the Law — in force, effectiveness, and their acceptance of suspension upon hazard (al-ighrār) and other things — so their equivalence appears in their non-acceptance of partition (tajazzī).

As for his saying "a share" (shirkan), it is a restriction excluding the half of the slave that is singled out, and it is nullified (mulghā): for the transmission to a female slave owned [by the manumitter] attaches to the transmission to another's property by way of priority (bi-ṭarīq al-awlā), and the restriction to "a share" was mentioned merely out of custom (al-ʿādah).

His saying "he owns" (lahu) is a restriction that is considered (muʿtabar); the directing of manumission toward the share of the partner does not attach to it, because that would remove manumission from being manumission: for it does not execute by itself.

As for his saying "from a slave" (min ʿabd), it is a nullified restriction: for the female slave is, in the cause, like the male slave; and femaleness has no entry in altering what is attached to manumission and slavery. The mention of the male slave occurred merely in agreement with its precedence upon the tongue — like his saying, peace be upon him: «أيما رجل مات أو أفلس، فصاحب المتاع أحق بمتاعه» ("Whichever man dies or becomes bankrupt, the owner of the goods has greater right to his goods"). By "man" (al-rajul), the genus (al-jins) is meant. The nullification of these restrictions was based upon understanding the custom of elucidation (ʿādat al-bayān), for the eloquent speaker may express the genus by mentioning some of its instances — as when one says, for example: "Whoever sells a garment, his ownership ceases," intending thereby all goods: furnishings and house. But he alerts by the part to the whole, and by the mention of one of the totality to the totality. This suffices for the nullification of these explicitly stated restrictions, along with what preceded: the commonality in the cause, and the return of the divergence to what is known to have no entry in the ruling. That may be known, as we have mentioned; and it may be merely probable (maẓnūn), as in our saying concerning the manumission of a specific part (al-baʿḍ al-muʿayyan). For we say: the cause, after refinement, is the manumission of some part of the slave (baʿḍ al-raqīq), and this is a part, and commonality (al-shuyūʿ) has no effect; but the exclusion of commonality from being included in the effect is probable, not known.

The purpose is that the probable and the known from this totality revolve upon intelligible grades of consideration (marātib fī al-naẓar maʿqūlah) that rise above the ambiguous (al-shubhah) that is disputed. Those who deny that genus affirm this art, necessarily.

As for his saying, peace be upon him: «إذا ولغ الكلب في إناء أحدكم فليغسله» ("When a dog laps from the vessel of one of you, let him wash it") — the lapping (al-wulūgh) is a restriction excluding drinking by the snout (al-kurūʿ) and other things. The dog (al-kalb) is a restriction excluding all other animals, even the pig (al-khinzīr). The vessel (al-ināʾ) is a restriction excluding the garment and other things. His saying "let him wash it" (fal-yaghsilhu) is a restriction excluding another act — such as rubbing (al-fark), sunning (al-tashmīs), and other things — and a restriction excluding the washing by someone other than the owner of the vessel. His saying "seven times" (sabʿan) is a restriction excluding all other numbers besides it. His saying "one of them with earth" (iḥdāhunna bil-turāb) is a restriction excluding soap (al-ṣābūn), ash (al-ushnān), and other things.

Let the inquirer consider: how does one dispose of these restrictions? We say: the intelligible meaning (al-maʿqūl) in sum is the Law's intensification (taghlīẓ) of the impurity (najāsah) of this animal.

As for lapping (al-wulūgh), drinking by the snout (al-kurūʿ) is in its meaning: for it indicates the impurity of its leftover water (sawr) and its sweat — according to al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, [sweat] is in the meaning of its saliva. Abū Ḥanīfah does not see it as being in its meaning, and he regards this restriction as observed. That is due to their disagreement over whether the intelligible meaning of the hadith is the impurity of the dog itself, or the impurity of its leftover water specifically. This is a matter of intellectual understanding (amr fahmī ʿaqlī), and it may draw support from [evidences] of the Law. According to al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, the mention of lapping occurred according to the predominant case (al-ghālib), as an alert to absolute impurity — just as the mention of the vessel occurred according to the predominant case: for one washes the garment from its saliva by agreement, just as one washes the vessel from its lapping. Thus the mention of the vessel is an alert to the genus: since the custom is that the dog only laps in vessels.

As for the specification of the dog, it could not be nullified, nor could other animals — or the animal whose flesh is not eaten, or beasts of prey — be annexed to it. For the dog is a beast of prey, an animal, non-edible of flesh, and a dog; so its specific attribute had an effect in rendering impure (al-tanjīs), known from the evidences of the Law in its specification with additional intensification and severity. Thus this restriction is not nullified. Indeed, a hesitation arises concerning the pig: for it is its brother in the view of the Law — in the command to avoid it, its prohibition, and its impurity. So it is possible to say: one washes from its impurity seven times, for they are brothers, like divorce and manumission, as we mentioned in the case of transmission (al-sarāyah). It is as if we were to attribute its impurity to the intensification of its matter in the Law, and annex the pig to it on one view — and this belongs to the category of appropriate analogical reasoning (al-qiyās al-munāsib al-mustanbaṭ), not to the category of the locus (al-manāṭ).

As for his saying "let him wash it" (fal-yaghsilhu), rubbing, sunning, and other things do not attach to it, because of what is known of the effect of washing in the Law. Then it is inclusive of washing with any liquid; but we add a restriction, restricting it to washing with water, because of what is known of the specificity of water.

And just as the mention of some restrictions by custom is part of elucidation (al-bayān), so too the omission of some — relying upon understanding by custom — is part of elucidation.

As for the restriction excluding the washing by someone other than the owner of the vessel, it is dropped (sāqiṭ): for what is understood is the obligation of removal (wujūb al-izālah), but the mention of the owner of the vessel occurred according to custom.

As for his saying "seven times" (sabʿan), no other number stands in its place.

As for his saying "with earth" (bil-turāb), there is disagreement concerning it: some annexed soap and ash to it, saying: the intelligible meaning is the intensification of severity by joining something other than water to water, and the mention of earth occurred according to the predominant case.

chapters.title_en: Section 78 — On What Is Known by Occasioning (Munāṭ) Through the Occurrence of a Ruling Following a Newly Emergent Matter
chapters.arabic_text: ### ||| CHECK القسم الثالث:  ما عرف المناط فيه بحدوث حكم عقيب أمر حادث
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Certain knowledge (yaqīn) or firm cognition (maʿrifah) attained through evidence, not mere opinion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, ʿilm denotes the settled comprehension of a ratio legis (ʿillah) or occasioning factor (munāṭ) as established by textual or rational proof.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — direct apprehension; metaphorical (majāz) — used here for juristic inference (istidlāl) where the "knowledge" is of the connection between a temporal event and a divine ruling.
- Root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Origination after non-existence; a newly emergent affair (ḥādith) that was not previously.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥudūth contrasts with qidam (eternity); in legal theory, it marks the temporal occurrence that triggers a fresh ruling (ḥukm).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — temporal inception; metaphorical — the "occasioning" (ʿillah) as a newly arisen attribute that necessitates a new legal status.
- Root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Following immediately or subsequently; succession without necessary interval.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿUqbā denotes consequence; here, the ruling's occurrence "after" (ʿaqība) the event signals a causal linkage (taʿlīl) by way of indication (dalālah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — temporal sequence; metaphorical — causal implication, where the sequence is not mere accident but reveals the munāṭ.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "عقيب أمر حادث" functions as a genitive construction (muḍāf ilayh) specifying the temporal proximity, and the entire clause is a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) with an implied predicate, indicating a settled legal principle rather than a transient observation.
chapters.translation: I say: The third division — that whose occasioning factor (munāṭ) is known by the occurrence of a ruling (ḥukm) immediately following a newly emergent matter (amr ḥādith). This is the case where the Lawgiver (al-Shāriʿ) establishes a legal effect upon the advent of a temporal event, such that the sequence itself — when consistently observed and not contradicted by another indicator — reveals the occasioning attribute (ʿillah) that the jurist seeks to identify. For the occurrence of the ruling after the event, when the event is the sole novel factor, points to the event's attribute as the effective cause, not by mere temporal adjacency, but by the evidentiary import (dalālah) that the Lawgiver's wisdom attaches the ruling to that which is suitable and pertinent. Thus, this division is distinguished from the prior ones in that the munāṭ is not known by explicit text (naṣṣ) nor by consensus (ijmāʿ), but by the very sequence of the ruling upon the event, which serves as a sign (amārah) of the causal connection.

chapters.title_en: The Third Category of Legal Causality: Refining the Locus of the Ruling (Tanqīḥ al-Manāṭ) and Its Application in Juristic Disputes
chapters.arabic_text:
التراب لوجوده غالبا، وهذا كالضعيف الذي لا يصلح للاعتماد عليه.
فهذا مساق هذه التصرفات؛ ومآخذها أمور معقولة من سياق الكلام، مفهومة من
موارد الشرع. وليس من قبيل الشبه [المقدم ذكره] المختلف فيه بين الفقهاء
والأصوليين.
مثال القسم الثالث- وهو: ما عرف مناط الحكم فيه بحدوث حكم عقيب أمر حادث؛
يعلم على الجملة أن الحادث موجبه، ثم ينظر في تنقيح قيوده-: كالحكم بلزوم
الوضوء بخروج الخارج من السبيلين؛ وقد اختلف العلماء فيه:
فقال أبو حنيفة- رضي الله عنه- مناط الحكم خروج النجاسة؛ فألحق به الفصد
والحجامة وكل نجاسة سالت، وقال: إحالة وجوب الطهارة على النجاسة- وقد عرف
تأثيرها في الطهارة في محله- أولى من إحالته على المحل الذي منه ينفصل؛
فسائر أجزاء البدن وأعضائه له حكم واحد في الطهارة والنجاسة، فلا يعرف
للمحل مدخل فيه.
وقال الشافعي- رضي الله عنه-: المعتبر خروج خارج من PageV01P428 # [المسلك] المعتاد، ولا يتبع [خروج] النجاسة؛ بل يجب بخروج الدود والريح
وغيرهما. وتعلقه بالريح يدل على أنه لا تتبع النجاسة؛ وأن قدر اشتمال
الهواء المنفصل بالريح على نجاسة، فيمكن تقدير ذلك في الريح الخارج من غير
المسلك المعتاد، وفي الجشاء المتغير؛ ولا تتعلق به الطهارة بالإجماع. فكان
المسلك المعتاد متبعا من حيث [أن] [سبب وجوب] الوضوء: الصلاة؛ ولكن جعلت
الأحداث- التي تتكرر بالطبع على الدوام- مواقيت لها، فليس في معناها الفصد
والحجامة؛ وفي معناها انفتاح ثقبة تحت المعدة مع انسداد المسلك المعتاد
فإنه قائم مقامه.
وقال مالك- رضي الله عنه- بما ذكره الشافعي رضي الله عنه؛ وزاد عليه
الاعتياد في الخارج، فلا ينتقض بالدم إذا خرج من السبيلين، وبما يندر: لأنه
لا يتكرر بالطبع.
وأنكر الشافعي هذا: من حيث أنه رأى تتبع النجاسة والبحث عنها خبيثا
قبيحا، مع اختلاف الطبائع، واختلاط العلل بالأمزجة.
PageV01P429
فأقام المحل مقام الخارج، فما يخرج من المحل المعتاد يلتحق بالخارج
المعتاد كيفما كان.
فهذا منهم نظر في تنقيح المناط، ومدركه شواهد الشرع وإبقاء ما يقدر له
أثر، وإلغاء ما لا يعقل له أثر.
وكذلك  عفا الشرع عن قريب [من] مقدار درهم من النجاسة، على محل النجو.
فقال أبو حنيفة- رضي الله عنه-: [عفى عنه] لقلته وقدره؛ فهذا القدر معفو
عنه على سائر المواضع: إذ جميع البدن- في وجوب تطهيره، وملابسته للصلاة-
على وتيرة.
وقال الشافعي- رضي الله عنه-: لهذا المحل اختصاص في تكرر نجاسته، ومسيس
الحاجة إلى العفو والرخصة فيه؛ ولا يدرأ هذا قول أبي حنيفة- رضي الله عنه-:
أن الواقف على شاطئ البحر جاز له PageV01P430 # الاقتصار على [قدر] الحجر؛ فتبين به أنه ليس في محل الرخصة، فإن تكرار
الحاجة إلى الغسل على الدوام- هو السبب في العفو، وهو الذي فهمه الأولون،
ولذلك اخترزوا عن رشاش النجاسة، وتساهلوا في الاستنجاء.
ومن هذا القبيل: طريان الخيار بعتق الأمة تحت العبد، فإنه تجدد بطريان
حادث علم أنه متعلقه وموجب حدوثه، وهو- أيضا- متسع لوجه آخر، وهو: ورود
الحكم مرتبا على واقعة؛ إذ عتقت بريرة، فخيرها رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم. والنظر في هذه المسألة بتعيين مناط الحكم لا بتنقيحه؛ فإنه احتمل أن
يكون سببه ملكها نفسها، فيطرد في الحرة. ويحتمل أن يكون سببه نقيصة الزوج
وظهورها عند حدوث الحرية، فالنظر في ترجيح أحد المناطين بالسبر، والامتحان
بشواهد الشرع، وبقوة المناسبة والتأثير.
والأمثلة السابقة وقع الاتفاق فيها على جملة، فانقسم الناظرون: إلى ن يضم
الزيادة إلى المزيد، وإلى من يلغي الزيادة ويقتصر على الأصل: فسميناه
تنقيحا. وفي هذا المثال تعدد المأخذ وتباين. وهو كالتنازع في أن الصغيرة
زوجت لبكارتها أو لصغرها؛ فهما مناطان ليس PageV01P431 # أحدهما مضموما إلى الآخر عند فريق. بل كل فريق يعتبر أحد المناطين.
واعتبار النقيصة في الخيار أظهر تأثيرا؛ إذ لا تطرق لخيار التروي إلى
النكاح؛ ولذلك إذا بلغت الصغيرة [لم] تتخير، فليس خيارها اعتراضا على ما
سبق من العقد بالرد، بل هو لمستأنف الحال فيعتبر النقصان. وتأثير الصغر- في
مسئلة التزويج- أظهر من حيث العموم؛ إذ ظهر أثره في المال، وفي أمور فارق
فيها الصبي البالغ.
والشافعي- رضي الله عنه- يقول: للبكارة والثيابة تأثير في النكاح على
الخصوص؛ ويشهد له أخبار وردت في إدارة  أمر النكاح على الثيابة والبكارة.
والغرض: أن متعلق كل فريق- في مسئلة الصغيرة، وخيار الأمة- مناسب مطرد؛
والنظر في التعيين بالترجيح، وهو دليل على امتناع تعليل الحكم [62 - ب]
بعلتين، على ما سنذكره. فإن الجمع يمكن في المسئلتين، ولم يذهب إليه فريق.
والمقصود من جميع هذه الأمثلة: أن مناط الحكم إذا صار معلوما [أما] على
الجملة، أو على التفصيل- فالنظر في تنقيحه وتعيينه: بالتدوار على طلب
التأثير. والمناسبة في PageV01P432 # الإلغاء والإبقاء ليس من باب الشبه المجتهد فيه، الذي قدمنا مثاله في علة الربا.
والعجب من بعض المصنفين في الأصول-: من أفاضل قدماء الأصحاب- أنه قال:
إلحاق السفرجل بالبر برابطة الطعم، من قياس المعنى والعلة. وإلحاق النكاح
الفاسد بالصحيح في أحكامه، من قياس الشبه؛ لدورانه بين الزنا والحلال،
وغلبة الشبه الحلال.
ونحن نقول: الأمر على العكس. فأما قاعدة الربا فقد قدمناها. وأما النكاح
الفاسد فالمتبع [فيه] في إثبات النسب والمصاهرة، والعدة، والمهر، وسقوط
الحد- المعني. فإن الأصل أن المولود على فراش الرجل والمخلوق من مائه،
منسوب إليه. وإنما قطع النسب بجناية الزنا وعدوانه؛ ولا عدوان من صاحب
الظن. والمهر جيب بالتفويت وقد حصل. والمصاهرة تتبع النسب؛ وإذا ثبت النسب:
فلابد من صون الماء- عن الخلط- بالعدة. وأما الحد فيسقط بالشبهة، فكيف لا
يسقط عمن لا يوصف بالمعصية؟
نعم: لو عبر معبر عن هذه المعاني: بالشبه، وعما تقدم في الربا: بالمعنى؛
وأفسد هذه المعاني في النكاح الفاسد- ليضطر إلى الأخذ من مجرد الشبه- فلا
يبعد شيء من ذلك، بعد الوقوف على المقاصد التي نبهنا عليها.
[وظني] أنه لا يبقى- بعد هذا التقرير والتفصيل والتمثيل- PageV01P433 # أشكال في قواعد الشبه والطرد والمخيل، على كل من أتقن هذه القواعد، وأمعن
النظر فيها بعين الإنصاف. وسنأتي على بقية البيان [في الطرد والشبه
والمخيل].-[إن بقى منه شيء في الإمكان]- في [باب] بيان القياس على المعدول
عن سنن القياس، إن شاء الله عز وجل.
* * *
PageV01P434
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ر-ب (t-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Earth, dust; that which is base, lowly, or weak in substance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The elemental, perishable substrate; metaphorically, that which lacks intrinsic firmness or reliability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: soil. Metaphorical (Majāz): a feeble support—one that cannot bear weight or be depended upon.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq al-Ḥukm bi al-ʿIllah (Attributing a ruling to its cause via conditional linkage); the particle "fa" (فـ) marks the consequential occurrence of a ḥukm upon a ḥādith, requiring the mujtahid to isolate the operative attribute.
chapters.translation:
I say: This is like the weak (al-ḍaʿīf) that is unfit for reliance. Such, then, is the course of these legal dispositions (taṣarrufāt); their points of attachment (maʾākhidh) are rational matters derived from the flow of discourse (siyāq al-kalām), understood from the sources of the Law (mawārid al-sharʿ). They are not of the kind of ambiguous resemblance (shubhah) [previously mentioned] over which jurists and legal theorists (uṣūliyyūn) differ.

An example of the third category—namely, that wherein the locus of the ruling (manāṭ al-ḥukm) is known by the occurrence of a ruling consequent upon a novel event (amr ḥādith), such that one knows in general that the event is its cause (mūjib), then proceeds to refine its conditions (tanqīḥ quyūdihi)—is the ruling on the obligation of ablution (wuḍūʾ) due to the emission of anything from the two passages (al-sabilān). The scholars differed concerning it:

Abū Ḥanīfah—may God be pleased with him—held that the locus of the ruling is the emission of impurity (khurūj al-najāsah); he thus annexed to it cupping (al-faṣd), leeching (al-ḥijāmah), and any impurity that flows forth. He said: Attributing the obligation of purification to impurity—whose effect upon purification is known in its proper place—is more fitting than attributing it to the locus from which it issues; for all parts and organs of the body share one status regarding purity and impurity, and no role for the locus is recognized therein.

Al-Shāfiʿī—may God be pleased with him—held that what is considered is the emission from the customary passage (al-maslak al-muʿtād), and impurity is not followed per se; rather, ablution becomes obligatory due to the emission of worms, wind (al-rīḥ), and other things. Its attachment to wind demonstrates that impurity is not the criterion; for even if one could estimate that the air separated with the wind contains some impurity, one could equally estimate this in wind emitted from other than the customary passage, or in altered belching (al-jushāʾ al-mutaghayyir)—yet purification is not attached to these by consensus. Thus the customary passage is followed insofar as the cause of the obligation of ablution is the prayer (al-ṣalāh); but the events (al-aḥdāth) that recur naturally and perpetually were made its temporal markers (mawāqīt). Cupping and leeching are not of their meaning; but the opening of a perforation below the stomach, with the obstruction of the customary passage, is of their meaning, for it stands in its place.

Mālik—may God be pleased with him—adopted what al-Shāfiʿī mentioned, and added to it the condition of habitual recurrence (al-iʿtiyād) in the emitted matter; thus ablution is not nullified by blood when it exits from the two passages, nor by what is rare, because it does not recur by nature.

Al-Shāfiʿī rejected this, on the ground that he deemed the pursuit and investigation of impurity to be vile and repugnant, given the diversity of natural temperaments (ṭabāʾiʿ) and the intermingling of ailments with humors (amzijah). He therefore substituted the locus for the emitted matter: whatever exits from the customary locus is annexed to the customary emission, however it may be.

This, then, is their consideration in refining the locus (tanqīḥ al-manāṭ), and its source is the evidences of the Law (shawāhid al-sharʿ), preserving whatever effect can be estimated for it, and nullifying whatever no effect can be rationally conceived for it.

Likewise, the Law pardoned (ʿafā) an amount close to a dirham of impurity upon the locus of excretion (maḥall al-najw). Abū Ḥanīfah—may God be pleased with him—said: It is pardoned for its smallness and quantity; hence this amount is pardoned upon all other places, for the entire body, regarding the obligation of cleansing it and its contact with prayer, is upon one footing.

Al-Shāfiʿī said: This locus has a particular distinction in the recurrence of its impurity and the pressing need for pardon and concession therein. This is not repelled by Abū Ḥanīfah’s—may God be pleased with him—argument that one standing at the seashore is permitted to suffice with the amount of a stone; for this shows that he is not within the locus of concession. Rather, the recurrence of the need for washing perpetually—this is the cause of the pardon, and it is what the early scholars (al-awwalūn) understood; for this reason they were lenient regarding the splashes of impurity and were tolerant in the matter of istinjāʾ (cleansing after excretion).

Of this kind, too, is the occurrence of the option (al-khiyār) upon the manumission of a slave-woman who is under a slave-husband; for it is renewed by the occurrence of a novel event, of which it is known that it is its correlate and the cause of its occurrence. It also admits of another aspect, namely: the ruling is reported as attached to a particular incident; for when Barīrah was manumitted, the Messenger of God—peace be upon him—gave her the choice. The consideration in this question is the determination of the locus of the ruling (taʿyīn al-manāṭ), not its refinement (tanqīḥ); for it is possible that its cause is her ownership of herself, in which case it would apply universally to the free woman. And it is possible that its cause is the deficiency of the husband and its manifestation upon the occurrence of freedom. The consideration, then, is the preponderance of one of the two loci by examination (al-sabr) and testing against the evidences of the Law, and by the strength of suitability (al-munāsabah) and effect (al-taʾthīr).

In the previous examples, there was agreement upon the general principle, and the investigators divided into those who annex the addition to the augmented (al-ziyādah ilā al-mazīd) and those who nullify the addition and restrict themselves to the original—this we have called refinement (tanqīḥ). But in this example, the points of attachment are multiple and divergent. It is like the dispute over whether a minor girl is married for her virginity (bakārah) or for her minority (ṣighar); these are two loci, neither of which is annexed to the other by one party. Rather, each party considers one of the two loci.

The consideration of deficiency (al-naqīṣah) in the option is more evidently effective; for the option of deliberation (khiyār al-tarawwī) does not attach to marriage. For this reason, when a minor girl reaches majority, she does not have a choice; her choice is not an objection to the prior contract by way of rescission, but rather pertains to the newly commenced state, and thus deficiency is considered. The effect of minority in the matter of marriage is more evident in terms of generality; for its effect appears in matters of property and in other matters wherein the minor differs from the adult.

Al-Shāfiʿī—may God be pleased with him—says: Virginity and defloration (thayyūbah) have an effect upon marriage in particular; and this is attested by reports (akhbār) that have come concerning the orientation of the marriage affair upon defloration and virginity.

The purpose is: that the correlate of each party—in the question of the minor girl and the option of the slave-woman—is suitable (munāsib) and consistent (muṭṭarid); and the consideration is in determination by preponderance (tarjīḥ). This is evidence for the impossibility of attributing a ruling to two causes (ʿillatān), as we shall mention. For combination is possible in both questions, yet no party adopted it.

The aim of all these examples is: that when the locus of the ruling becomes known—either in general or in detail—the consideration of its refinement and determination consists in the circulation (al-tadawwur) upon seeking effect (al-taʾthīr) and suitability (al-munāsabah) in nullification (al-ilghāʾ) and preservation (al-ibqāʾ). This is not of the kind of ambiguous resemblance (al-shubhah) subject to ijtihād, of which we gave the example in the cause of ribā (usury).

It is astonishing that one of the authors on uṣūl—among the virtuous early companions (al-aṣḥāb)—said: Annexing quince (al-safarjal) to wheat (al-burr) by the link of taste (al-ṭaʿm) is qiyās of meaning and cause (qiyās al-maʿnā wa al-ʿillah); while annexing a void marriage (al-nikāḥ al-fāsid) to a valid one in its rulings is qiyās of resemblance (qiyās al-shabah), because it oscillates between fornication (zinā) and the lawful, with the resemblance of the lawful predominating.

We say: The matter is the reverse. As for the principle of ribā, we have already stated it. As for the void marriage, what is followed therein—in establishing lineage (al-nasab), affinity (al-muṣāharah), the waiting period (al-ʿiddah), the dower (al-mahr), and the dropping of the ḥadd punishment—is the meaning (al-maʿnā). For the principle is that a child born upon the bed of a man and created from his fluid is attributed to him; lineage is severed only by the offense of fornication and its transgression, and there is no transgression on the part of one who acts upon a semblance (shubhah). The dower is owed for the consummation (al-tafwīt), and it has occurred. Affinity follows lineage; and when lineage is established, the preservation of the fluid from mixture by the waiting period becomes necessary. As for the ḥadd, it is dropped by doubt (al-shubhah)—how, then, would it not be dropped for one who is not described as disobedient?

Indeed, if one were to express these meanings as "resemblance" (shabah), and what preceded in ribā as "meaning" (maʿnā), and were to corrupt these meanings in the void marriage—so as to be compelled to take from mere resemblance—none of that would be far-fetched, once one has grasped the purposes (maqāṣid) to which we have drawn attention.

It is my conviction that after this exposition, detailing, and exemplification, no obscurity remains in the principles of resemblance (al-shabah), formal consistency (al-ṭard), and indicant cause (al-mukhayyil) for anyone who has mastered these principles and pondered them with the eye of fairness. We shall come to the remainder of the exposition [on al-ṭard, al-shabah, and al-mukhayyil]—[if anything of it remains possible]—in the chapter on the explanation of qiyās upon that which is diverted from the path of qiyās (al-maʿdūl ʿan sanan al-qiyās), God Almighty willing.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-ر-ه-ن (burhān)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Clear, decisive proof; that which renders a matter evident and incontrovertible.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Demonstration (burhān) as apodictic syllogism yielding certainty (yaqīn), distinct from dialectical or rhetorical argument.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense — a "white mark" (barhān) on a camel distinguishing it; metaphorically, the decisive sign that separates truth from falsehood.
- Root: ش-ك-ل (shakl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Form, figure, configuration; in logic, the mood or figure of a syllogism.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The structural arrangement of premises yielding valid inference; in juridical analogy (qiyās), the formal pattern of co-extensiveness and co-exclusiveness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical shape; metaphorical — the logical architecture of proof.
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿillah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cause, reason, effective motive; that which necessitates an effect.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ratio legis (ʿillah) in legal reasoning — the attribute upon which a ruling is predicated and by which analogy is validated.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a recurring illness; metaphorical — the persistent, operative cause in legal causation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate expansion (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — the topic (al-qawl fī bayān...) governs a genitive chain, indicating a structured exposition of subordinate classifications.
chapters.translation: I say: Now we turn to the discourse on the forms of theoretical demonstrations that run through juridical questions. Know that the demonstration of legal causation (burhān al-iʿtilāl) is divided into its definition and its divisions. The forms of these demonstrations are not confined to a single pattern; rather, they vary according to the variation of the causes (al-ʿilal) and the modes of their attachment to the rulings. So we shall expound, in this section, the enumeration of these forms and the clarification of their conditions, so that the seeker may discern the sound from the corrupt, and the complete from the deficient, in the proofs of the jurists.

chapters.title_en: The Three Demonstrative Methods in Juridical Analogy (Masālik al-ʿIllah)
chapters.arabic_text:
والغرض: بيان المسالك الجارية في المسائل التي يعدها الفقهاء قياسية، لا
نقلية. فأقول: هذه البراهين ثلاثة: برهان اعتلال، وبرهان استدلال، وبرهان خلف.
أما برهان الاعتلال، فهو: الجمع بين الفرع والأصل، برابطة العلة؛ كما
تقدم ذكره في القياس. وشكل هذا البرهان يرجع إلى مقدمتين ونتيجة، وبيانه
أنك تقول: المغصوب مضمون. فهذه مقدمة، وتقول: العقار مغصوب. فهذه مقدمة
ثانية، فنتيجتهما: أن العقار مضمون. وتقول: المغصوب مضمون، وولد المغصوبة
مغصوب: فكان مضمونا. وتقول: المال مضمون بالإتلاف، والمنفعة مال: فتضمن
بالإتلاف. وتقول: السارق مقطوع، والنباش سارق: فكان مقطوعا. وتقول: المطعوم
ربوي، والسفرجل مطعوم: فكان ربويا.
وكل ذلك راجع- في أول التمهيد- إلى دعوى دخول واحد معين، تحت جملة
معلومة. وإن شئت قلت: الطعم علة الربا، والطعم موجود في السفرجل: فجرى
الربا فيه. والغصب علة الضمان، وقد وجد في العقار: فوجب الضمان.
وعبارة الفقهاء- في هذا الجنس- أنه مطعوم، فأشبه البر. أو جرى فيه الربا:
قياسا على البر. أو مغصوب: فيضمن كالمنقول.
وكل ذلك يرجع إلى دعوى دخول واحد معين، تحت جملة شاملة. وشكله من
البراهين العقلية؛ مقدمتان ونتيجة؛ كما تقدم.
PageV01P435
ثم قد يفرض النزاع في المقدمة الأولى مع تسليم الثانية؛ كقول الخصم: أسلم
أن السفرجل مطعوم. ولكن لا نسلم أن الطعم علة الربا، وأن المطعوم ربوي، بل
بعض المطعوم ربوي لا بعلة كونه مطعوما. وقد يسلم [المقدمة] الأولى وينازع
في الثانية؛ كقوله: سلمت أن الغصب علة الضمان، ولكن لا نسلم وجود الغصب في
العقار وولد المغصوبة والمنفعة. وسلمت أن السرقة علة القطع، ولكن لا أسلم
أن النباش سارق.
فإذا وقع النزاع في المقدمة الأولى، لم تثبت إلا بالأدلة الشرعية: فإن
المتنازع فيه قضية شرعية، وهو: كون الطعم علة مثلا، فيثبت ذلك: بالنص، أو
الإيماء، أو الترتيب على الواقعة، أو الحدوث بحدوث الوصف، أو بالتأثير،
وهو: أن يثبت أثره في عين الحكم، في محل آخر، بنص أو إجماع، أو بالمناسبة
كما تقدم، أو بالطرد والعكس، أو بالإجماع المنعقد على أنه لابد من طلب
علامة، والسبر الواقع بعده في  نفي علامة سوى المذكور، كما ذكرناه في مقدمات
قياس الشبه. وهو يسمى علة أيضا عند أكثر الأصوليين؛ وإليها أشار كلام
الشافعي في الطعم والنقدية.
أما إذا وقع النزاع في المقدمة الثانية، وهو: وجود العلة في الفرع، بعد
تسليم كون الوصف علة- فهذا يعرف تارة بالحس: إن كان الوصف حسيا؛ وقد يعرف
بالعرف، وقد يعرف باللغة، وقد يعرف [63 - أ] بطلب الحد وتصور حقيقة الشيء
في نفسه، وقد يعرف بالأدلة الشرعية النقلية.
مثال الحسي؛ قولنا في الماء الكثير المتغير بالنجاسة- إذا زال تغيره PageV01P436 # بوقوع التراب فيه-: أنه سبب مبطل للتغير الحاصل بالنجاسة، فصار كهبوب
الريح، وطول المكث. وشكله: أن المزيل لتغير النجاسة يبطل حكم النجاسة
[والتراب مزيل: فكان مبطلا. فيقول: نسلم أن المزيل للتغير مزيل حكم
النجاسة]، ولكن لا نسلم أن التراب مزيل، بل هو ساتر كالزعفران والمسك.
فيعلم ذلك بأدلة حسية طبيعية.
ومثال العرفي: قولنا: إن بيع الغرر باطل، وبيع الغائب غرر: فكان باطلا.
فيقول: أسلم المقدمة الأولى، ولكن لا أسلم أن بيع الغائب بيع غرره فيقال:
إنما يعرف هذا من العادة، فيحكم العرف فيه.
وأما مثال اللغوي، فكقولنا: العتاق يحصل بالكناية المحتملة، والطلاق
محتمل للعتاق: فيحصل به. فيسلم المقدمة الأولى، وينازع في الثانية، وهي:
كون الطلاق محتملا للعتاق، فيطلب من مدارك الكنايات ومآخذ التجاوزات
والاستعارات.
وأما ما يثبت بالنقل، <ف> كإثباتنا كون النباش سارقا، بقول عائشة رضي
الله عنها «سارق أمواتنا كسارق أحيائنا» وإثباتنا PageV01P437 # [كون] العقار مغصوبا، بقوله- عليه السلام-: «من غصب قيد شبر من الأرض»
الحديث. وإثباتنا كون اللائط زانيا، بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا أتى
الرجل فهما زانيان». وشكل القياس فيه: [أن] الزنا موجب للحد، واللائط زان،
فوجب عليه الحد.
وأما ما يعرف بتصور ذات الشيء، وطلب حده الجامع المانع- < ف > كقولنا:
ولد المغصوب مغصوبا، لأن حد الغصب: إثبات يد عادية على المال على وجه تقصير
يد المالك [عنه]؛ وقد جرى. فربما ينازع في هذا الحد وصحته، وربما يسلم،
وينكر من وجود في ولد المغصوب، ويقول: ليس اليد عادية، ذا  لا مانع من جهته
أو لم تقصر يد PageV01P438 # المالك عنه، فإنه غير دافع له عنه. فيثبت منعه بالتسبب: بإثبات اليد على
الأصل، ويستشهد عليه بولد الصيد. ويثبت قصور يد الملك: بيان ثبوت يد
الغاصب، وأن يد الملك منتفية شرعا لثبوت يده؛ فالانتفاء كالزوال.
فإذا نوزع في أصل الحد، وقيل: لا، بل الغصب عبارة: عن إثبات يد تزيل يد
المالك؛ ولا يد للمالك على الولد ولا على المنفعة حتى تزال- الغصب أو حكمه،
حاصل دون تقدير الزوال؛ كالمودع إذا جحد الوديعة، فإنه لم يزل يدا ومع ذلك
جعل غاصبا. فهذا ترتيب النظر في التحديات.
وقد يتصل النظر- في هذا الجنس- بتنقيح مناط الحكم؛ مثل أن نسلم أن اسم
الغصب غير حاصل، ولكن مناط الضمان من الغصب: حصول اليد العادية، ونسلم أن
اسم السرقة غير حاصل للنباش، ولكن مناط القطع من السرقة: أخذ مال محترم من
حرز مثله، ونسلم أن اللائط ليس بزان، ولكن مناط الحد من الزاني: تضييع
النساء بقضاء شهوة الفرج في الفرج. وعلى هذا يتغير شكل القياس ويرتد النزاع
إلى PageV01P439 # المقدمة الأولى؛ إذ لا نقول على هذا الطريق: إن الزنا موجب، وإن اللائط
زان؛ ولا أن السرقة موجبة، وأن النباش سارق، بل نقول: تضييع الماء بقضاء
شهوة الفرج موجب، واللائط متصف بذلك. وأخذ المال المحترم من حرز مثله موجب،
وقد وجد في النباش. فينازع الخصم في المقدمة الأولى، ويقول: لا أسلم أن
الموجب ما ذكرته؛ بل الموجب: فعل يسمى زنا وسرقة.
فليدرك المسترشد الفرق بين المسلكين؛ فإن النزاع يتحول من مقدمة إلى
مقدمة. [فهذا هو] الطريق.
وغرضنا أن [نبين أن] جميع براهين الاعتلال إلى مقدمتين ونتيجة يرجع
حاصلها إلى [دعوى] علة لحكم، ودعوى وجودها في محل [النزاع]، ومحاولة ترتيب
الحكم عليها.
ومثاله في العقليات: أن العلم علة كون الذات عالمة، وقد قام العلم بذات
الله تعالى: فكان عالما. ومثاله من الحسيات، أن نقول: [أن] الحيوانية علة
التغذي، والإنسان حيوان: فكان متغذيا. وشكله من البراهين أن نقول: كل حيوان
متغذ، وكل إنسان حيوان؛  فكل انسان متغذ، فلا يعقل
PageV01P440
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Repetition of a cause; the secondary cause (ʿillah) that necessitates an effect; also "sickness" (ʿillah) as that which alters the body's state.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The effective cause in legal-theological reasoning—that attribute (waṣf) which is the divine law's (ḥukm) rationale, established via textual or rational proof.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a recurrent condition. Metaphorical: the legal ratio—since it "recurs" in every branch (farʿ) to justify the same ruling.
- Root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To come after, to succeed; opposition; contradiction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The argumentum per impossibile (burhān al-khalf)—proving a thesis by showing the absurdity of its negation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: succession in time. Metaphorical: logical entailment where the consequent's denial entails the antecedent's denial.
- Root: س-ب-ر (s-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To test, to examine; to try a thing to know its condition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The method of "examination and division" (al-sabr wa al-taqsīm)—exhaustively testing all candidate attributes to isolate the sole ʿillah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: probing a wound. Metaphorical: intellectual scrutiny of all possible causes, negating all but one.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jazāʾ) — The protasis (sharṭ) and apodosis (jazāʾ) structure governs the syllogistic form: "If A is ʿillah, and A exists in B, then B takes the ḥukm." The syntactic dependency mirrors the logical entailment.
chapters.translation:
I say: The purpose here is to expound the pathways (masālik) operative in those cases which the jurists deem analogical (qiyāsiyyah), not textually transmitted (naqliyyah). I therefore state: These demonstrative proofs (barāhīn) are three: the proof of causal attribution (burhān al-iʿtilāl), the proof of inferential indication (burhān al-istidlāl), and the proof of contradiction (burhān al-khalf).

As for the proof of causal attribution, it is: the unification of the branch (farʿ) and the root (aṣl) through the nexus of the cause (ʿillah), as previously mentioned in the discussion of analogy (qiyās). The form (shakl) of this proof reduces to two premises and a conclusion. Its elucidation: You say, "The usurped (al-maghṣūb) is guaranteed (maḍmūn)"—this is one premise. You say, "Real estate (al-ʿiqār) is usurped"—this is a second premise. Their conclusion: "Real estate is guaranteed." You say, "The usurped is guaranteed, and the offspring of the usurped female is usurped—therefore it is guaranteed." You say, "Wealth is guaranteed by destruction (itlāf), and usufruct (al-manfaʿah) is wealth—therefore it is guaranteed by destruction." You say, "The thief is amputated, and the grave-robber (al-nabbāsh) is a thief—therefore he is amputated." You say, "The edible (al-maṭʿūm) is subject to ribā, and quince (al-safarjal) is edible—therefore it is subject to ribā."

All of this reverts—at the outset of the preamble (al-tamhīd)—to the claim that one specific particular (wāḥid muʿayyan) falls under a known universal (jumlah maʿlūmah). If you wish, you say: "Edibility (al-ṭaʿm) is the cause of ribā, and edibility exists in quince—therefore ribā applies to it." Or: "Usurpation (al-ghaṣb) is the cause of guarantee, and it exists in real estate—therefore guarantee is necessitated."

The jurists' expression in this genre is: "It is edible, so it resembles wheat (al-burr)" or "Ribā applies to it, by analogy to wheat," or "It is usurped, so it is guaranteed like movable property (al-manqūl)." All of this reverts to the claim that one specific particular falls under a comprehensive universal. Its form, among the rational proofs, is two premises and a conclusion, as previously stated.

Then the dispute may be posited regarding the first premise while the second is conceded—as when the opponent says: "I concede that quince is edible, but I do not concede that edibility is the cause of ribā, nor that the edible is universally subject to ribā; rather, some edible things are subject to ribā, not by virtue of being edible." Or he may concede the first premise and dispute the second—as when he says: "I concede that usurpation is the cause of guarantee, but I do not concede the existence of usurpation in real estate, the offspring of the usurped female, or usufruct. I concede that theft is the cause of amputation, but I do not concede that the grave-robber is a thief."

When the dispute falls on the first premise, it is established only by legal-evidentiary means (al-adillah al-sharʿiyyah). For the disputed matter is a legal proposition (qaḍiyyah sharʿiyyah)—namely, that edibility is a cause, for example. This is established by: the explicit text (al-naṣṣ), or the textual indication (al-īmāʾ), or the ordering of the ruling upon the occasion (al-tartīb ʿalā al-wāqiʿah), or the co-occurrence of the ruling with the attribute's occurrence (al-ḥudūth bi-ḥudūth al-waṣf), or by causal efficacy (al-taʾthīr)—namely, that the attribute's effect is established in the very ruling (ʿayn al-ḥukm) in another locus, by text or consensus (ijmāʿ)—or by suitability (al-munāsabah) as previously mentioned, or by co-extensiveness and co-exclusiveness (al-ṭard wa al-ʿaks), or by the consensus that a marker (ʿalāmah) must be sought, followed by the examination (al-sabr) which negates any marker other than the one mentioned—as we have stated in the premises of analogy of resemblance (qiyās al-shabah). This [attribute] is also called a "cause" by most uṣūliyyūn; and it is to this that al-Shāfiʿī's words allude regarding edibility and monetary value (al-naqdiyyah).

As for when the dispute falls on the second premise—namely, the existence of the cause in the branch, after conceding that the attribute is a cause—this is known sometimes by sense-perception (al-ḥiss) if the attribute is sensible; sometimes by custom (al-ʿurf); sometimes by language (al-lughah); sometimes by seeking the definition (al-ḥadd) and conceptualizing the thing's true nature (ḥaqīqah) in itself; and sometimes by transmitted legal evidences (al-adillah al-sharʿiyyah al-naqliyyah).

An example of the sensible: Our statement concerning abundant water altered by impurity (al-najāsah)—when its alteration ceases by the falling of dust into it—that it is a cause nullifying the alteration produced by impurity, so it becomes like the blowing of wind or the prolongation of time. Its form: "That which removes the alteration of impurity nullifies the ruling of impurity, and dust is a remover—therefore it is a nullifier." The opponent says: "I concede that the remover of alteration removes the ruling of impurity, but I do not concede that dust is a remover; rather, it is a concealer (sātir), like saffron and musk." This is known by natural sensible evidences.

An example of the customary: Our statement: "The sale of deception (gharar) is void, and the sale of an absent object (al-ghāʾib) is deceptive—therefore it is void." He says: "I concede the first premise, but I do not concede that the sale of an absent object is a deceptive sale." It is said: "This is known only from habitual practice, so custom (al-ʿurf) judges therein."

As for the linguistic example: Our statement: "Emancipation (al-ʿitāq) is effected by an ambiguous allusion (al-kināyah al-muḥtamalah), and divorce (al-ṭalāq) is ambiguous for emancipation—therefore it is effected by it." He concedes the first premise and disputes the second—namely, that divorce is ambiguous for emancipation—so recourse is sought to the sources of allusions (madārik al-kināyāt), the bases of figurative usages (al-tajāwuzāt), and metaphors (al-istiʿārāt).

As for what is established by transmission: Such as our establishing that the grave-robber is a thief, by the saying of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her: {«سارق أمواتنا كسارق أحيائنا»} ("The thief of our dead is like the thief of our living"). And our establishing that real estate is usurped, by his saying, peace be upon him: {«من غصب قيد شبر من الأرض»} ("Whoever usurps a span of land")—the hadith. And our establishing that the sodomite (al-lāʾiṭ) is a fornicator (zānin), by his saying, peace be upon him: {«إذا أتى الرجل الرجل فهما زانيان»} ("When a man comes to a man, they are both fornicators"). The form of the analogy therein: "Fornication necessitates the prescribed punishment (al-ḥadd), and the sodomite is a fornicator—therefore the punishment is incumbent upon him."

As for what is known by conceptualizing the thing's essence and seeking its comprehensive, exclusive definition: Such as our statement: "The offspring of the usurped female is usurped, because the definition of usurpation is: the establishment of a transgressing hand (yad ʿādiyah) over wealth in a manner that causes the owner's hand to fall short (taqṣīr) of it; and this has occurred." He may dispute this definition and its soundness, or he may concede it and deny its existence in the offspring of the usurped female, saying: "The hand is not transgressing—either because there is no impediment from its side—or the owner's hand has not fallen short of it, for he is not repelling it from it." Its establishment is then sought by way of causation (al-tasabbub): by establishing the hand over the root [i.e., the mother], citing as evidence the offspring of game (walad al-ṣayd). And the falling short of the owner's hand is established by demonstrating the usurper's hand's establishment, and that the owner's hand is legally negated (muntafiyah sharʿan) due to the usurper's hand's establishment—for negation is like removal (al-intifāʾ ka-al-zawāl).

If the dispute falls on the definition itself, and it is said: "No—rather, usurpation is the expression for the establishment of a hand that removes the owner's hand; and there is no hand of the owner over the offspring or the usufruct to be removed"—then [we say]: Usurpation, or its ruling, is realized without positing removal; like the depositary (al-mūdaʿ) who denies the deposit (jāḥada al-wadīʿah)—for he did not remove a hand, yet he is deemed a usurper. This is the ordering of inquiry in matters of definition (al-taḥdīdāt).

The inquiry in this genre may also connect to the refinement of the ratio (tanqīḥ al-manāṭ) of the ruling—such as our conceding that the name "usurpation" is not realized, but the ratio of guarantee from usurpation is: the realization of a transgressing hand; and our conceding that the name "theft" is not realized for the grave-robber, but the ratio of amputation from theft is: the taking of protected wealth (māl muḥtaram) from its equivalent place of custody (ḥirz mithlih); and our conceding that the sodomite is not a fornicator, but the ratio of the punishment from fornication is: the dissipation of women (taḍyīʿ al-nisāʾ) by satisfying the sexual urge (shahwat al-farj) in the private part (al-farj). On this basis, the form of the analogy changes, and the dispute reverts to the first premise. For on this path we do not say: "Fornication is a cause, and the sodomite is a fornicator"; nor "Theft is a cause, and the grave-robber is a thief." Rather, we say: "The dissipation of the seminal fluid (al-māʾ) by satisfying the sexual urge is a cause, and the sodomite is characterized by that. The taking of protected wealth from its equivalent place of custody is a cause, and it is found in the grave-robber." The opponent then disputes the first premise, saying: "I do not concede that the cause is what you mentioned; rather, the cause is an act named 'fornication' or 'theft.'"

Let the seeker of guidance (al-mustarshid) grasp the difference between the two pathways; for the dispute shifts from one premise to another. This is the method.

Our purpose is to show that all proofs of causal attribution revert to two premises and a conclusion, whose sum total is: the claim of a cause for a ruling, the claim of its existence in the locus of dispute, and the attempt to order the ruling upon it.

Its example in rational matters: "Knowledge (al-ʿilm) is the cause of the essence's being knowing (ʿālim), and knowledge has obtained in the essence of God, Exalted—therefore He is knowing." Its example from sensible matters: "Animality (al-ḥayawāniyyah) is the cause of nutrition (al-taghaddī), and the human is an animal—therefore he is nourished." Its form among the proofs: "Every animal is nourished, and every human is an animal—therefore every human is nourished." This is rationally intelligible.

chapters.arabic_text:
### ||| CHECK النوع الثاني: الاستدلال بالنتيجة

### ||| CHECK النوع الأول: الاستدلال بالخاصية

النزاع في النتيجة بعد تسليم المقدمتين. وإذا وقع النزاع في المقدمات
أثبت بطريقة. ولا تفارق الفقهيات العقليات [في ذلك]، إلا أن المسلك الذي
[يثير ظنا] في المقدمتين -كاف في الفقه، ولا يكفي في العقليات.
البرهان الثاني:

### ||| AUTO برهان الاستدلال

. [وهو: الاستدلال] على الشيء بما ليس علة موجبة له، ولكن تثبت علته بوجه
من الدلالة معقولة.
ولا حرج في تسمية برهان الاعتلال: استدلالا. فإن العلة مع الإيجاب
للمعلول، تدل على المعلول. ولكن المعلول قد يدل على العلة، ولا يوجبها.
وهذا النوع -وهو الاستدلال بما ليس موجبا -ينحصر في ثلاثة: الاستدلال على
الشيء بوجود خاصيته، أو بوجود نتيجته، فوجود الخاصية [63 - ب] يدل على وجود
ذي الخاصية، وعدمها يدل على عدمه. وكذلك وجود النتيجة يدل على وجود المنتج.
وعدمها يدل على عدمه.
والاستدلال على الشيء بمثله ونظيره، فإن ما يثبت للشيء: يثبت لنظيره
ومساويه، على الضرورة.
مثال الاستدلال بالخاصية، كقولنا: الوتر نفل، لأنه يؤدي على الراحلة،
ويطرد هذا في النوافل، وينعكس في الفرائض. ووجه PageV01P441 # دلالته؛ أن الأداء على الرواحل خاصية النوافل، فلا تؤدي فريضة على
الراحلة بحال. وإذا وجد خاصية الشيء: دل على وجود ذلك الشيء .. وهذه
الدلالة لا خفاء بها بعد تسليم الخاصية؛ إذ معنى الخاصية؛ الملازمة لذاته
على وجه لا ينفصل عنه، ووجود الشيء يدل على وجود ما يلازمه، ولا ينفك عنه.
فإن قال الخصم: لست أسلم أن جواز الأداء على الراحلة خاصية النفلية؛ لأني
أقول: الوتر ليس بنفل، ويؤدي على الراحلة. فالسؤال على هذا الوجه فاسد:
لأنا نقدر -في ابتداء النظر -حكم الوتر في الفرضية والنفلية مشكلا: يتلقى
من الأدلة، ويتعرف منها؛ ونقدر أنه لم يقم دليل فيه على النفي والإثبات،
فوجدناه ينجذب إلى النفل في خاصية: لا تعرض قط في فريضة، فيغلب على الظن
كونه نفلا.
ونحن نجوز أن يقوم للخصم دليل على كون الوتر فرضا؛ فيبين بذلك الدليل
بطلان هذه الخاصية. أما  هذه الخاصية، فثابتة، وبها يعرف حكم الوتر، ولا
دليل فيه، فإن قام عليه دليل مقصود: سقطت هذه الدعوى؛ وعلى الخصم أن يذكر
دليلا: إن كان عنده.
نعم: للخصم أن يقول: جواز الأداء [على الراحلة] خاصية عدم الفريضة؛ فلذلك
تؤد الفرائض، وأنا أسلم أن الوتر ليس فرضا PageV01P442 # ولكنه واجب؛ فقد وفيت بموجب الخاصية.
وهذا السؤال واقع، ولكن شرطه: أن يبين فرقا بين الواجب والفرض، وعندنا لا
فرق بينهما، فنبطل عليهم ما ذكروه، ويسلم الاستدلال بالخاصية.
ومن هذا القبيل -أيضا -قولنا: عتق المكاتب لا ينصرف إلى جهة الكفارة،
لأنه وقع عن جهة الكتابة، ونستدل على وقوعه عن جهة الكتابة، باستتباعه
الإكساب والأولاد؛ [وهو] من خاصية الكتابة، فدل على بقاء الكتابة وعدم
انفساخها. وهي دلالة ظاهرة إلى أن يبين الخصم أن PageV01P443 # الكتابة باقية فيما على السيد، ومنفسخة فيما له؛ بدليل انفساخها في حق
قرار النجوم، حتى يسقط باعتاقه، وهلم جرا إلى كلامه في تلك المسئلة.
وغرضنا: أن هذا ليس استدلالا بالعلة الموجبة؛ فليس الأداء على الراحلة
[موجبا لفرضية] أو نفلية، ولا علة لها. ولا استتباع الإكساب [والأولاد]
موجبا للكتابة، ولكنها خاصية ملازمة للذات؛ غرف ملازمتها بالشرع.
ويمكن أن نقرر وجه التمسك بهاتين الخاصيتين، بطريق الاطراد والانعكاس،
وبطريق الشبه. ولكن ذلك جار فيما لا يعد من الخاصية؛ ولهذا وجه في الدلالة
يزيد على المشابهة والاطراد والانعكاس.
النوع الثاني: الاستدلال بالنتيجة على المنتج، وبعدمها على عدم المنتج.
ووجه دلالتها -بعد تسليم كونها نتيجة -واضح: فالعالمية نتيجة العلم وقيامه
بالذات. فنقول: البارى سبحانه وتعالى عالم، فدل على قيام العلم به. ومأخذ
هذا الجنس -أيضا -الملازمة؛ فإن الموجب يلازم الموجب، كالخاصية الملازمة؛
فدل وجوده على وجوده: فإنه ملازم.
PageV01P444

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ت-ج (n-t-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to produce, yield, result" — the outcome (natījah) that follows from a productive cause (muntaij).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological reasoning, the natījah is the entailed effect whose existence signals the existence of its productive ground, without necessarily being caused by it in a reciprocal sense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes actual production (ḥaqīqah); here it is extended (majāz) to logical entailment where the consequence indicates the antecedent.
- Root: خ-ص-ص (kh-ṣ-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes exclusivity, particularity — a property (khāṣṣiyyah) unique to a thing's essence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A khāṣṣiyyah is an inseparable concomitant (lāzim) of the essence, whose presence entails the presence of the subject and whose absence entails its absence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally as a distinguishing mark; metaphorically extended to legal indicants (amārāt) that yield predominant conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Concomitance Structure (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The argument hinges on biconditional entailment: existence of the property implies existence of the subject; non-existence implies non-existence. This is parsed as a conditional sentence where the protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) are mutually implicative in the legal context, though not in strict syllogistic necessity.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second type — namely, inference by the consequence (al-istidlāl bi-al-natījah) — and the first type, inference by the property (al-istidlāl bi-al-khāṣṣiyyah). The dispute concerning the consequence arises after the two premises are conceded. If the dispute falls upon the premises, it is established by another method. The jurisprudential matters do not depart from the rational ones in this respect, except that the path which [engenders predominant conjecture] concerning the premises suffices in jurisprudence, but does not suffice in rational matters.

The second proof: The proof of inference (burhān al-istidlāl). It is: inferring a thing from that which is not an efficient cause (ʿillah mūjibah) of it, but whose cause is established by a certain mode of indication that is rationally intelligible. There is no objection to naming the proof of causation (burhān al-iʿtilāl) an "inference," for the cause, by virtue of its necessitation of the effect, indicates the effect. But the effect may indicate the cause without necessitating it. This type — namely, inference by that which is not necessitating — is confined to three [kinds]: inference to a thing by the existence of its property, or by the existence of its consequence. For the existence of the property [63-b] indicates the existence of the possessor of the property, and its non-existence indicates its non-existence. Likewise, the existence of the consequence indicates the existence of the producer, and its non-existence indicates its non-existence. And inference to a thing by its like and its counterpart — for whatever is established for a thing is established for its counterpart and equal, by necessity.

An example of inference by the property is our saying: The witr prayer is supererogatory (nafl), because it is performed upon the riding beast, and this [practice] is consistent in the supererogatory prayers and is inverted in the obligatory ones. The aspect of its indication is that performance upon riding beasts is a property of supererogatory prayers, so no obligatory prayer is ever performed upon a riding beast. When the property of a thing exists, it indicates the existence of that thing. This indication is not obscure after the property is conceded; for the meaning of "property" is the concomitance with the essence in a manner that does not separate from it, and the existence of a thing indicates the existence of what is concomitant with it and inseparable from it.

If the opponent says: "I do not concede that the permissibility of performance upon the riding beast is a property of supererogatoriness, because I hold that the witr is not supererogatory, yet it is performed upon the riding beast" — then this objection is invalid in this respect. For we suppose, at the outset of consideration, that the ruling of the witr regarding obligatoriness and supererogatoriness is problematic, to be received from the evidences and known through them; and we suppose that no evidence has been established concerning it for negation or affirmation. We find it drawn toward supererogatoriness by a property that never occurs in an obligatory prayer, so predominant conjecture prevails that it is supererogatory.

We do allow that the opponent may establish an evidence that the witr is obligatory, whereby that evidence demonstrates the invalidity of this property. As for this property, it is established, and by it the ruling of the witr is known when there is no evidence concerning it. If a direct evidence is established against it, this claim falls; and upon the opponent is to mention an evidence, if he has one.

Indeed, the opponent may say: "The permissibility of performance [upon the riding beast] is a property of non-obligatoriness; therefore obligatory prayers are not performed upon it. And I concede that the witr is not obligatory, but it is incumbent (wājib) — so I have fulfilled the requirement of the property." This objection is valid, but its condition is that he demonstrate a distinction between the incumbent (wājib) and the obligatory (farḍ). In our view, there is no distinction between them, so we invalidate what they have mentioned, and the inference by the property stands.

Of this kind, also, is our saying: The emancipation of the mukātab (slave under contract of manumission) does not apply to the direction of expiation (kaffārah), because it occurred for the direction of kitābah (the contract). We infer its occurrence for the direction of kitābah from its entailment of acquisition and children — which is a property of kitābah — so it indicates the persistence of the kitābah and its non-dissolution. This is a manifest indication until the opponent demonstrates that the kitābah remains in what is owed by the master and is dissolved in what is owed to him, by the evidence of its dissolution regarding the installments of the price, such that it falls by his emancipation, and so forth to his discourse in that issue.

Our purpose is that this is not inference by the necessitating cause; for performance upon the riding beast is not a necessitating cause for obligatoriness or supererogatoriness, nor a cause thereof. Nor is the entailment of acquisition [and children] a necessitating cause for kitābah, but it is a property concomitant with the essence, whose concomitance is known by the Law (sharʿ).

We can establish the mode of adhering to these two properties by the path of consistency (iṭṭirād) and inversion (inʿikās), and by the path of similarity (shabah). But that applies to what is not counted as a property; for this [property] has an aspect of indication that exceeds similarity, consistency, and inversion.

The second type: Inference by the consequence to the producer, and by its non-existence to the non-existence of the producer. The aspect of its indication — after conceding that it is a consequence — is clear: For "being knowledgeable" (al-ʿālimiyyah) is a consequence of knowledge and its subsistence in the essence. We say: The Exalted Creator is knowledgeable, so this indicates the subsistence of knowledge in Him. The source of this kind, also, is concomitance; for the necessitator is concomitant with the necessitated, like the concomitant property. So His existence indicates its existence, for it is concomitant.

PageV01P444
