chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Repetition of an affair; the secondary occurrence that follows upon a primary cause; that which necessitates an effect.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The efficient cause (ʿillah) in juridical theology is that attribute (waṣf) upon which the divine command (ḥukm) is predicated, whether by textual indication or by rational suitability (munāsabah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes the cause that produces its effect; metaphorical usage extends to legal attributes that are mere indicators (amārāt) of the divine will.
- Root: ش-ر-ط (sh-r-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The mark or sign; that which is stipulated as a prerequisite for the validity or obligation of an act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A condition (sharṭ) is that whose existence is required for the existence of the effect, but which does not itself necessitate the effect; it is a prerequisite, not a participant in the causal efficacy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the rope tied to the leg of a beast; metaphorical: that which binds the effect to its cause without contributing to its essence.
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Relation, lineage, attribution; the connection between two entities.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Relative attributes (iḍāfāt) are among the intelligible qualities (ṣifāt ʿaqliyyah) that may attach to a substance without altering its essence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: genealogical kinship; metaphorical: any relational predicate that qualifies an object, such as "the adulterer who is married" (muḥṣan).
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Sabab (Coordination on the Cause) — When two attributes are coordinated in a legal predicate, the later may be a condition of the former's efficacy, not an independent cause; the syntactic structure of "the cause is X qualified by Y" (al-ʿillah: X al-mawṣūf bi-Y) shows that Y is an integral qualifier, not a separate entity.
chapters.translation:
I say: You have mentioned these attributes, and that they are either conditions (shurūṭ) or parts and pillars (ajzāʾ wa arkān) of the cause (ʿillah). So what is the true criterion (al-miʿyār al-ṣādiq), and the decisive separator (al-fayṣal al-fāriq) in the loci of ambiguity (maẓānn al-ishtibāh)?

We say: That which appears to us for regulating the courses of inquiry therein — and knowledge is with Allah, Glorified and Exalted — is that every attribute (waṣf) that is suitable to the ruling (munāsib lil-ḥukm), or that entails the suitable meaning (mutḍammin lil-maʿnā al-munāsib), whether with certainty or with conjecture (taḥqīqan aw tawahhuman): it is the cause. And whatever is beyond that — namely, attributes for which the ruling's dependence upon them is known, yet there is no suitability between them and the ruling: neither by way of suitability in themselves, nor by way of entailing the suitable — that is the condition (al-sharṭ).

Then the conditions divide into: that which the cause is affected by, like iḥṣān (being married) with zinā (adultery); and that whose consideration is known from the Law by pure stipulation (taḥakkuman), with no intelligible effect known for it — neither in the ruling nor in the cause. This latter is rare in its occurrence, but its occurrence is permissible, in general.

If it is said: Why did you not rely in the criterion upon that which produces the ruling immediately after it, such that it is said: that is the cause? And whatever preceded in existence without the ruling arising from it is the condition — like zinā with iḥṣān, and the falling into a well (al-tardiyah) with the digging (al-ḥafr), and the attributes of the eligible person and the locus (ṣifāt al-ahl wa al-maḥall) in the rest of the causes?

We say: There is no reliance upon this criterion; for the divorce (ṭalāq) suspended upon entry (al-dukhūl) appears immediately after entry; yet the cause is the prior divorce: because it is the suitable one. And whoever purchases his relative: emancipation occurs immediately after the purchase; yet the cause is the kinship (al-qarābah): because it is suitable for the connection of kindness through emancipation.

If it is said: How then did you distinguish taste (al-ṭaʿm) from genus (al-jinsiyyah) in ribā (usury), with no suitability [in the latter]?

We say: There is obscurity in this; and it may occur to the inquirer that al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — said that by virtue of the attribution (al-iḍāfah) understood from his saying: «Do not sell food for food» (lā tabīʿū al-ṭaʿām bil-ṭaʿām), just as the attribution of amputation to theft, and of flogging to zinā, is known. But this is corrupt: because monetary status (al-naqdiyyah) is distinguished from genus in this case, and there is no attribution therein. And because the attribution to genus is more apparent, since he said: «So if the two genera differ, then sell however you wish, hand to hand» (fa-idhā ikhtalafa al-jinsāni fa-bīʿū kayfa shiʾtum yadan bi-yad). Thus he clarified that the ribā of excess (ribā al-faḍl) is removed by the removal of genus. And among the strongest degrees of efficacy is: that the ruling exists with the existence of the attribute and is negated with its negation; this is more apparent than the verbal attribution in his saying: «Do not sell food for food.»

And it may also occur to the inquirer in the answer that taste is the attribute that manifests the ruling, because when the four items — which are the locus of ribā — are compared with slaves and garments, in which ribā does not run, the differentiation by taste appears therein; as we mentioned in the mode of establishing the indicator (taqrīr al-ʿalāmah). This too is corrupt: for the non-existence of the ruling due to the non-existence of genus is understood from his saying — peace be upon him —: «So if the two genera differ» and is more apparent than what we mentioned. How so? If it were said: if one sells a ṣāʿ of wheat for two ṣāʿs of wheat, it is prohibited; and for two ṣāʿs of barley, it is permissible. And there is no differentiator except genus — is this not more apparent than what preceded?

And perhaps one might say: There is no meaning in naming one of them a cause and the other a locus (maḥall); for this was not transmitted from the speech of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him. Rather, what is transmitted from the speech of our companions is: that taste in the single genus is the cause. [Just as Abū Ḥanīfah says: measurement (al-kayl) in the genus is the cause.] From this very expression, one might imagine that genus is a locus, since it was made like a container (ẓarf) for taste.

Upon this, it is said: The question of prohibiting women (al-nisāʾ) by bare genus is not built upon this principle; rather, we concede that it is an attribute, but it does not independently effect the prohibition of women; unlike the other attribute, because its prohibition by the mere attribute of taste is taken from his saying: «So if the two genera differ, then sell however you wish, hand to hand.» Thus it is known that what remains after the removal of genus is a cause for the prohibition of women, and that the removal of genus does not negate the ribā of women. This is more fitting to indicate the fall of genus's efficacy than to indicate its being an independent cause.

And this imagination, although we established it in the Book of Sources (Kitāb al-Maʾākhidh) and the Book of Fortifying the Sources (Kitāb Taḥṣīn al-Maʾākhidh), yet therein is consideration: because when it is established that the cause of ribā al-faḍl is composed of taste and genus, and that they are two attributes not distinguished from one another in efficacy in ribā; then it is established that one of the two attributes independently produces one of the rulings — this indicates the independence of the [equal] attribute: because what is established for a thing is established for its like, as we established in the modes of inference in the chapter on the forms of proofs (ashkāl al-barāhīn). And its being like it is known by relation to ribā; and he who claimed it is one of the two attributes conceded its being like it, with no distinction in terms of efficacy.

So we say: The path of differentiation and its perception is: [the conjecture of entailing] the suitable meaning. For we have shown that we conjecture that taste is an indicator (amārah) of a hidden interest (maṣlaḥah khafiyyah) concealed from us, and it is a sign upon it. And we do not conjecture that in genus: thus genus is in the status of the locus devoid of suitability and its entailment, and it has no efficacy — by itself — in necessitating the genus of the ruling of the original; like bare iḥṣān: it does not effect the necessitation of punishment. As for taste, it entails the interest: so it is intelligible that it effects by itself, even if its locus is lost, with a diminished efficacy; and it does not follow from this that the locus, detached from the conjecture of suitability, equals it. And there is joined to it another matter, namely: that genus is not affected by taste; while the purpose of taste is affected by genus. And among the signs of the condition is: that the cause is affected by it, not the ruling; and the ruling is affected by the cause.

And this, if conceded, is clear. But if one said: What compelled you to this arbitrary stipulation (taḥakkum)? And why did you deem it far that genus also entails a type of suitability and interest that you have not perceived? For if you judge upon the unseen by what you do not know nor perceive, with insensible conjectures — then let that be conjectured in genus as in taste; since each one by itself is not suitable.

We say: This conjecture's basis is a predominant supposition (ẓann ghālib), namely: that taste is the intended purpose by which the subsistence of creation, the order of the world, and the preservation of the species are maintained; it is the livelihood and nourishment, and to it is the necessity of every animal.

Likewise, monetary status (al-naqdiyyah): it is the intended purpose of dirhams and dīnārs; upon it revolve transactions, in it is the life of wealth, and by it are established compensations for destroyed properties. So it predominates in supposition that the imagined, conjectured interest is entailed by these great, apparent purposes, even if we do not perceive the mode of that interest. So genus — in relation to these purposes — is far from the intended aim.

And by this measure, the distinction of taste from genus has become apparent, and it is impossible for the opponent to claim: that what is established for a thing is established for its like. For by this measure, the supposition of similarity is cut off, and his claim is repelled. And we did not mean by its being a locus of the cause except that it does not equal the cause in independence in producing what the cause — namely taste — independently produces. So if this measure is conceded to us, there is no harm upon whoever expresses it as a pillar of the cause (rukn al-ʿillah) and its attribute; there is no constraint in the expressions.

This is the path of establishing the doctrine of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — and it is subtle and hidden: because the very establishment of the cause is hidden, and its distinction from the condition falls beyond it in hiddenness; and due to its subtlety, the disposition of one whose intellect does not expand except to perceive evident matters recoils from accepting it, and his mind falls short of encompassing subtleties and hidden things.

If it is said: This is your [disposal] regarding the suitable or the entailer of the suitable. And among the causes are those known to be causes by verbal attribution from the Law, and by the occurrence of the ruling immediately after their occurrence, even if there is no suitability — as you have presented. So by what is the condition distinguished from the pillar therein? Do you rely therein upon occurrence, such that it is said: the ruling is referred to the last occurring [attribute], and the prior is in the rank of the condition?

We say: No. Rather, when it is established that the prior is considered in the ruling like the later accident, then there is no preponderance by priority and posteriority. Rather, if one of them is conjectured to entail the hidden interest — as in taste and genus — that is followed. Otherwise, all these attributes are equalized, and the non-suitable is not preponderated over the suitable by posteriority and the consequent occurrence of the ruling; just as the suitable attribute is not preponderated over the suitable by posteriority. Rather, the last attribute is not exclusively entitled to attribution.

And Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — held: that the ruling is attributed to the last attribute of the cause; because the prior attribute became an effecter through it, thus it becomes in the status of the cause of the cause. And he built upon this that the purchase of a relative is an emancipation: because ownership of the relative is the cause, and ownership has occurred such that the prior kinship became effectual with it; so it is in the meaning of the direct agent (al-mubāshir).

And we say: Ownership is a locus; for it is not suitable to emancipation, which is its opposite. Rather, the suitable is kinship. And even if it is conceded to be an attribute, the last attribute is not exclusively entitled to attribution. For this reason, we say: if a group of people transgressed by placing loads upon a ship until it sank, then liability (al-ḍamān) is upon all, not upon the last placement.

[And the prohibition of an intoxicant necessitates the prohibition of all other cups, and it is not exclusive to the last cup,] because intoxication is produced by all, not by the last. The evidence for this: the consensus (ijmāʿ) is established that in offer and acceptance (ījāb wa qabūl) in sale, neither is preponderated over the other by posteriority. Thus, if a wife purchased her husband, and the marriage was dissolved, and we wish a basis for the referral of the dissolution — whether for halving the dowry or for dropping it — we do not take that from priority and posteriority.

Likewise, the witnesses of entry (shuhūd al-dukhūl): the occurrence of separation is ordered upon their testimony — after the precedence of the witnesses of suspension (shuhūd al-taʿlīq). And no one may say: they, by their testimony, made the prior suspension a divorce, so they are exclusively liable.

In general: when the matter leads to these attributions in rulings, they are ijtihādī (based on juristic reasoning). And the position of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — and the view of our companions have differed in most of them; and their positions differed regarding the witnesses of suspension and zinā: if they retract, are they exclusively liable for the indemnity, or do the witnesses of the iḥṣān attribute share with them?

And there are many analogues to this. All of this clarifies the agreement of the scholars upon the distinction between the condition and the cause, and that this is an important principle that must be known, and negligence therein is not permissible: relying upon the fact that the ruling is suspended upon all of them, and that the causes of the Law are indicators: for the obligation therein is known from the Law as well, so it runs upon the taste of rational necessitators (mūjibāt ʿaqliyyah).

If it is said: The owner of the ship, when he loaded it with loads, and a stranger threw a load into it and it sank — why is the stranger exclusively liable? And why was it not apportioned, and the owner's share dropped, if there is no reliance upon the last attribute?

We say: Because the owner's act is not fit to have the destruction referred to it, nor liability attached to it; so it is referred to the transgressor's act, [for some] attributes of the cause do not fall short of the condition.

And liability is obligatory upon the digger of the well: when the passerby falls into it out of ignorance; because his walking is not fit to be a cause and be attributed to it; so the destruction is attributed to the condition. And this is a basis not free from disagreement.

And we now turn to questions in which the inquiry revolves upon the investigation of the locus and the condition, and the cause.

Among these: the purchase of a relative with the intention of expiation (al-kaffārah). It does not count toward it in our view: because what is obligatory upon him is emancipation (al-taḥrīr), and emancipation is an expression for effecting the cause of emancipation by way of direct agency; and the cause of emancipation is kinship, not purchase; for purchase is a cause of ownership. So it is not fit to be made a cause for its removal. And kinship is a relation that demands connection and kindness (al-ṣilāt wa al-mabārr), and emancipation is a connection and kindness. So his intention at the purchase is like his intention at the attribute upon which emancipation was suspended — [and despite that, emancipation was suspended upon it] and not upon the intention.

And we only obligated upon him the liability for the consequential harm (ḍamān al-sirāyah): because liability is attached to the condition and the locus when it cannot be referred to the cause. And kinship cannot have the obligation of liability referred to it, nor to that which causes it; so it is referred to the purchase, as in the case of suspension.

And Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — claims: that it is one of the two attributes of the cause, and it is the last; so it is attributed to it. And we do not concede that it is one of the two attributes; for there is no suitability in it. And even if conceded, the last is not exclusively determined for attribution, like the two halves of offer and acceptance.

Among these: the question of the partner of the father (sharīk al-ab). It has been turned upon the distinction between the cause and the locus. And I have exerted myself in the Book of Sources (Kitāb al-Maʾākhidh) with a path by which one is spared from plunging into the peril of the distinction between the cause and the locus; and I showed that the obligator (al-mūjib) with the completion of its conditions has run its course; and that qiṣāṣ (retaliation) is in the status of a fallen obligatory (al-sāqiṭ al-wājib); and that the repulsion of qiṣāṣ by it is in the meaning of its cessation: by the supervention of pardon (al-ʿafw), or the supervention of the son's entitlement (istiḥqāq al-ibn). And it is solid and sufficient.

But it is not sufficient to support the doctrine of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — in all aspects; for al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — decisively ruled the obligation of qiṣāṣ upon the partner of the Muslim and the free man in the killing of the disbeliever and the slave, when the partner is equivalent (kufʾ). And equivalence is a condition; the killing does not become a cause for necessitating qiṣāṣ in our view except with its existence. Thus the cause has lost its condition. And the disparity in equivalence is not among the repellers (al-dawāfiʿ); therefore, if it supervened, the obligation would not cease; unlike the son's entitlement. So another path is necessary for establishing the doctrine.

And the method of the "Sources" is sufficient in disputation. For we do not meet Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — in these two questions: for he obligates qiṣāṣ in them upon both partners.

So we mention the path of the distinction between the cause and the locus in the case of the partner of the father; and its formulation is that we say: There is no partnership in the locus of ambiguity (maḥall al-shubhah), and no ambiguity in the locus of partnership. For the partnership is in the killing — which is pure premeditation (ʿamd maḥḍ) — there is no ambiguity in it; and the ambiguity is in the killer, and partnership therein is inconceivable; rather, the ambiguity only transfers from the partner to the partner: through participation; and participation occurred only in the act. And there is no defect in the essence of the act: for it is a cause for necessitating qiṣāṣ; the defect is only in the father, who is a locus for the operation of the cause in necessitating [the ruling] upon him.

If it is said: How is it said that it is an obligator (mūjib), yet it did not obligate, [and the cause is what obligates] the ruling?

We say: We have spoken on this in the question of the specification of the cause (takhṣīṣ al-ʿillah); we showed the intended meaning of the unrestricted naming of the cause. So let the one who has reached this station first review that question, so that he may draw from it. And we now mention what pertains specifically to this question, and we say:

We mean by the cause: that to which the ruling is attributed from among the totality of what the ruling is ordered upon; or that which is suitable to the ruling. And the ruling is attributed to premeditated killing, not to [paternity]; and it is the suitable one. And being a stranger (al-ajnabiyyah) is not suitable to [the ruling]. And this is easy with the jurists: for they conceded the distinction between zinā and iḥṣān, and that one is a cause and the other a condition. The obscurity is only with one who denies the principle, as we shall alert to — Allah willing. So when we observe — in distinguishing the cause from the condition — the path of rational attribution (al-iḍāfah al-ʿaqliyyah), and we say: it is attributed to the killing, not to the attribute of the killer — a problematic inquiry confronts in its course regarding the details. For it occurs to al-Muzanī to say:

The partner of the mistaken killer (sharīk al-khāṭiʾ) is killed, because the cause is: the killing upon the existence of intent and knowledge in the essence of the killer. And it is attached to the killing, not to the attribute of the killer. For it may be imagined that the act is qualified by it, since it is said: premeditated killing; and the mode of its being qualified by it: is the attribution of intent to it. And just as intent is attributed to the act, so the act is qualified by it; likewise, the act is attributed to the agent, so it is qualified by it. And among the rational attributes are: the attributions and relations (al-iḍāfāt wa al-nisab). And brotherhood is an attribute whose existence and non-existence are intelligible; it is a pure relation, whose meaning is: that the brother is the son of the father and the son of the mother. And the meaning of his being the son of the father: is a relation; so lineage (al-nasab) is among the rational attributes.

But al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — did not make lineage among the attributes, and made the act among the attributes. And from this arose the disturbance of the position regarding the partner of the beast (sharīk al-sabuʿ), the partner of the self (sharīk al-nafs), the partner of the one entitled to qiṣāṣ (al-mustaḥaqq), the authorized one (al-maʾdhūn), the combatant (al-ḥarbī), the insane (al-majnūn), and the minor (al-ṣabī), and the partner of the master (sharīk al-sayyid).

Sometimes he suffices with the premeditated act, and makes the act of the beast and the minor premeditated. Sometimes he joins to it the guaranteed (al-maḍmūn), saying: there must be pure, guaranteed premeditation. Then sometimes he suffices with the guarantee of expiation (ḍamān al-kaffārah), and obligates it upon the partner of the self and the partner of the master. And sometimes he stipulates the guarantee of blood-money (ḍamān al-diyah), and does not obligate it upon these, nor upon the partner of the combatant and the beast, and obligates it upon the partner of the minor. And this is a hidden path and an ambiguous inquiry.

And when we support the position of obligation in this case, we say: The cause is premeditated killing; and the killing of the beast, the insane, and the combatant is premeditated. But the defect is in the locus of obligation (maḥall al-luzūm) regarding the beast: by the loss of the attribute of humanity; regarding the combatant: by the loss of commitment (al-iltizām); regarding the minor [and the insane]: by the loss of intellect and legal responsibility (al-ʿaql wa al-taklīf).

And the act of the beast may be excepted from this, and it is said: it is not a cause. And the effect of [nullifying] the act by bestiality (al-bahīmiyyah) exceeds its effect by error (al-khaṭaʾ). So if we decisively rule the dropping [of qiṣāṣ] for the partner of the mistaken killer, then for the partner of the beast it is more fitting.

And there is no case except that a type of obscurity attaches to it. But that arises from the obscurity of the distinction between the pillar of the cause and its condition.

This is what we intended to establish upon the taste of the jurists' discourse. And examples of it have preceded: in the question of the specification of the cause.

And here we make a raid (nukīru ʿakrah) upon the jurists' discourse, and we show the basis of the one who says: that the condition and the locus have no meaning, and that the ruling does not depend except upon the cause; then the cause may be an absolute essence (dhāt muṭlaqah), and may be an essence qualified by attributes. And we present the discourse on zinā and iḥṣān: to measure others by it, and we say:

The cause is an expression for the obligator of the ruling (mūjib al-ḥukm); and the obligator is: what the [Law] made an obligator, whether suitable or not. And it is like the rational causes: in obligation; except that its obligation is by the Law's making it an obligator, not by itself. And the cause for stoning (al-rajm) is: [the zinā of the muḥṣan] not absolute zinā. And the attribution to muḥṣan is an attribute of the zinā; and attributions and relations are intelligible attributes; just as one intelligibly describes a man by tallness and blackness, one intelligibly describes him by brotherhood and paternity. Except that brotherhood is among the attributes of lineage, and it is established: for its negation and existence are intelligible; and it subsists in another: so it is an attribute.

Yes, it is not permissible to call it an accident (ʿaraḍ) upon the terminology of the theologians (al-mutakallimīn); rather, we mean by it the attributes and propositions (al-awṣāf wa al-qaḍāyā), just as blackness is intelligibly a color and an accident, and these are multiple propositions. And the attributes of blackness are intelligible, upon the path established in proving states (al-aḥwāl) in the art of kalām. And we say: zinā, by attribution to muḥṣan, is an attribute that is negated when it issues from the non-muḥṣan; and that attribution is an attribute of the cause. And the basis of stoning is: the attributed, qualified zinā. And it is as we established: from the explanation of killing by blackness, when the Lawgiver said: Kill Zayd because he is black. And its course necessitates killing every black person. So if it became clear that none is killed except Zayd by text, then a restriction (qayd) turns back upon blackness, and it becomes clear that absolute blackness is not a cause; rather, the cause is: Zayd's blackness.

Likewise, it becomes clear that absolute zinā is not a cause; rather, the cause is: the zinā of a muḥṣan. So the attribution is among the attributes of the cause. And this runs in killing, for we say: absolute killing is not a cause; rather, the cause is: premeditated killing attributed to a specific agent, namely: the sane, legally responsible, stranger, equivalent, who is neither entitled to qiṣāṣ nor authorized; and so on, to the rest of the killer's attributes. And the attributes of the killed — likewise. So when the killing issues from a minor: the cause is deficient; for the attribute of attribution to the adult has been diminished from it. And likewise in every attribute that is negated.

Likewise, the cause of ownership: is a specific sale qualified by restrictions and attributions, not absolute sale. It is: the sale of a sane, legally responsible person of a valuable, known, deliverable property. And it is not said: ownership occurred by intellect, legal responsibility, value, knowledge, and the attributes of the eligible person and the locus; rather: by the sale qualified by the restrictions of attributions to these attributes. So the sale of wine is void: for the deficiency of the cause; the sale of a minor is void: [for the deficiency of the cause. But the modes of deficiency differ; so the sale of a minor is void]: for the deficiency of an attribute of the sale, which attribute is obtained by attribution to the [sane] agent. And the sale of wine is void: for the deficiency of the attribute of attribution to the locus. So when the modes of deficiency differed, the sources of inquiry therein and their perceptions diverged; and all of that reverts to a deficiency in the cause. And the cause is an expression for the totality of matters upon which the Law ordered the ruling; except that those matters divide: among them is what is qualified (mawṣūf), and among them is what is a subordinate attribute (waṣf tābiʿ). And the individual attributes are equal, and the individual parts of the qualified — likewise — are equal.

And we mean by the equality of the individual attributes: that the deficiency of attribution to a non-sane [person] in sale, is like the deficiency of attribution to wine: in the case of attribute-ness. And we mean by the equality of the parts of the qualified: that offer is like acceptance, in that each one of them is a part of the form of the sale; and neither is a subordinate attribute of the other. And they are in equality like the individual loads in the sinking of the ship, and the individual cups in stirring the intoxication (ithārat al-kar). [Such that] no part is preponderated over another — from this aspect — when the aspects multiply, distribute, and conflict. And the qualified may be preponderated over the attribute: when they multiply and compete in the preponderance of attribution.

And from this [distinction] arose the difference of inquiry in the questions that were turned upon the distinction between the cause and the locus. And the cover is only lifted from this by presenting the juristic questions, as objections to this principle, and the resolution from them.

**A Conjecture and Alert:**

If it is said: How do you deny the distinction between the cause and the locus, when you have ruled that liability is obligatory upon the one who causes the fall (al-murdi), not upon the digger, and the destruction does not occur except by both of them? Likewise, you obligate the indemnity upon the witnesses of [zinā in stoning], not upon the witnesses of iḥṣān, when they retract. And you obligate upon the witnesses of suspension, not upon the witnesses of the attribute, when they retract?

We say: As for the question of the fall (al-tardiyah), the obligation of the indemnity therein upon the one who causes the fall, [not upon] the digger, does not indicate a distinction between the condition and the cause; for we may obligate the liability upon the digger: when the passerby is ignorant of it; and by ignorance, the transgression does not cease to be a cause of the fall. But the effect of digging in the destruction is not like the effect of causing the fall. Rather, they are different, and the opinion therein is two opinions: either apportionment (taqsīṭ), or preponderance (tarjīḥ). And apportionment is only intelligible in equals: like the individual loads in the sinking of the ship; for they are equal in course in efficacy, and like the two halves of the contract: for each is like the other half; so apportionment may occur therein. As for the effect of digging, it is not of the genus of the effect of causing the fall. So we sought the path of preponderance, and we saw the obligation upon the one who causes the fall as more fitting: for the connection of his act to the destruction with premeditation. And the digger's act has ceased with the digging. And what is connected [to the destruction is: what he effected by his digging]. And if the passerby is ignorant: we preponderated the digging; because walking is not intended for falling. Likewise, digging is not intended for falling; but digging is originally an aggression (ʿudwān): so it is preponderated. And if a man dug in his own property, and a man fell into it ignorantly — it is ruled as wasted (ihdār): for there is no suitability between the two acts to be apportioned, nor preponderance. Or it is ruled that the fall and walking are preponderated and wasted, for their issuing from the right-holder. This is its source, and it is in the locus of ijtihād: disagreement therein is conceivable. And there is nothing in it that contradicts our discourse.

As for the witnesses of iḥṣān and zinā, the source of inquiry therein is: that whoever established iḥṣān did not establish what necessitates stoning, nor a part of the obligator; for stoning is obligatory by zinā attributed to the muḥṣan; and the attribution is an attribute of the zinā. So the witnesses of zinā established zinā, which is part of the obligator. And the attribution remained, and it occurred upon the establishment of freedom, generated from iḥṣān and zinā: not from zinā specifically, nor from iḥṣān specifically. For the attribution is a relation between the attributed and the attributed-to.

So it is possible to say: this attribution was generated from the two sides upon one pattern; so the indemnity is apportioned: for neither side has preponderance; and they are like a single genus — namely, the two pillars of the attribution — in generating the attribution.

And it is possible to preponder the side of zinā: because stoning is attached to the attributed zinā, not to the iḥṣān attributed-to. For when the attribution becomes an attribute of zinā, the qualified zin

### || AUTO القول في بيان معنى السبب في لسان الفقهاء

لا ينبغي أن يظن [أن] السبب جنس زائد على [جنس] العلة والشرط. ولكن لما
تداولته الألسنة، وأطلقه الفقهاء لمعان مختلفة -أحببنا بيانه.
فالسبب -في وضع اللسان- هو: الحبل والطريق أيضا؛ ثم عرف أن نزح الماء لا
يتأتى دون الحبل، وأنه إذا حصل: حصل بالاستقاء لا بالحبل. والاستقاء -الذي
هو علة نزح الماء من البئر- ليس حاصلا أيضا بالحبل. وكذلك الوصول أيضا إلى
البلد المقصود:  لا يحصل دون الطريق؛ وإذا حصل: كان حاصلا بالسير لا
بالطريق؛ ولا يحصل السير أيضا بالطريق.
فلما فهم نسبة الحبل والطريق من المقصود، استعير اسم السبب لكل ما يقع من
المقصود هذا الموقع. وهو: كل ما لا يحصل المقصود دونه؛ وإذ حصل: حصل بعلة
مستقلة لا بذلك السبب.
PageV01P590

### || CHECK أطلق على علة العلة

### || CHECK أطلق في مقابلة المباشر

### || CHECK معنى السبب في لسان الفقهاء

ثم أطلق الفقهاء لفظ السبب على أربعة أوجه:
الوجه الأول: إطلاقه في مقابلة المباشرة، فإذا قوبل بالمباشرة: أريد به
الشرط المحض. واستعملوا هذه اللفظة في الضمان، وقالوا: الضمان على المباشر
لا على المتسبب. فيراد بالمباشرة: إيجاد العلة، وبالتسبب: إيجاد الشرط.
فقالوا: الحافر متسبب، والمردي مباشر؛ من حل قد العبد حتى أبق فهو متسبب؛
والمباشر هو العبد: إذ [الفرار حصل] بالأباق عند حل القيد، لا بحل القيد.
وزعموا: أن الإحصان من الرجم، يقع موقع الشرط. فهذا أقرب وجوه الإطلاق إلى
وضع اللسان.
الوجه الثاني: تسميتهم علة العلة سببا، كالرمي، فإنه يقال فيه: إنه سبب
الموت، لأن الموت لا يحصل بالرمي، فكان الرمي سببا من هذا الوجه. ولكن لما
حصل بالسراية والجرح -وهي حاصلة بالرمي- كان الرمي علة العلة. [فلهذا كان]
موافقا لوضع اللسان، من أحد الوجهين. فهذا مأخذ الاستعارة، وهو: أن الحكم
لم يحصل به إلا بواسطة العلة، كما لا يحصل الوصول بالطريق إلا بواسطة
العلة. إلا أن السير ليس حاصلا بالطريق؛ والعلة ها هنا حاصلة بالسبب. وهذا
الجنس

chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ب-ب (s-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A rope (ḥabl) by which water is drawn; also a road/path (ṭarīq). Core sense: that which connects or leads to an end.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, a cause is that whose existence entails another's existence but is not itself the direct agent of that effect—distinct from ʿillah (efficient cause) and sharṭ (condition).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = rope/road; metaphorical (majāz) = any intermediary that is necessary for an outcome yet does not produce it directly. The juristic extension is a recognized metaphor (istiʿārah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-muḍāf (Ellipsis of the genitive construct) — phrases like "cause of the cause" (ʿillat al-ʿillah) require supplying an omitted noun to parse the relational chain correctly.
chapters.translation:
I say: One ought not to suppose that "cause" (sabab) is a genus additional to the genus of "efficient cause" (ʿillah) and "condition" (sharṭ). Rather, because tongues have circulated it and jurists have employed it for diverse meanings, we wished to clarify it.

Now, "cause" — in the lexical convention (waḍʿ al-lisān) — is: the rope and also the road. Then it became known that the drawing of water cannot be achieved without the rope, and that when it is achieved, it is achieved by the act of drawing (istiqāʾ), not by the rope. And the drawing — which is the efficient cause of extracting water from the well — is likewise not produced by the rope. Similarly, arrival at the intended town: it is not achieved without the road; and when it is achieved, it is achieved by traveling (sayr), not by the road; nor is the traveling itself produced by the road.

So when the relation of the rope and the road to the intended end was understood, the name "cause" was borrowed (ustuʿīra) for everything that occupies this position relative to the intended end. Namely: that without which the intended end is not achieved, yet when it is achieved, it is achieved by an independent efficient cause, not by that "cause" itself.

Then the jurists employed the term "cause" in four modes:

**The First Mode:** Its use in contrast to direct agency (mubāsharah). When contrasted with direct agency, what is meant by it is the pure condition (sharṭ maḥḍ). They used this term in liability (ḍamān), saying: "Liability falls upon the direct agent, not upon the causer (mutasabbib)." By "direct agency" they mean: the production of the efficient cause; by "causation" (tasabbub): the production of the condition. Thus they said: the digger of a well is a causer (mutasabbib), while the one who pushes [another into it] is a direct agent (mubāshir). Likewise, one who loosens the shackles of a slave until he flees is a causer; the direct agent is the slave himself — for the flight occurred by the fleeing (ibāq) upon the loosening of the shackle, not by the loosening itself. And they held that the state of being muḥṣan (i.e., having been married) in [the penalty of] stoning occupies the position of a condition. This is the closest of these usages to the lexical convention.

**The Second Mode:** Their naming of the "cause of the cause" (ʿillat al-ʿillah) as a "cause" — as in shooting an arrow, for it is said of it that it is a "cause" of death, because death does not occur by the shooting itself; thus the shooting is a cause in this respect. But since death occurs by the penetration (sarāyah) and the wound — which are produced by the shooting — the shooting is the cause of the cause. Hence it accords with the lexical convention in one of the two respects. This is the basis of the metaphor (istiʿārah), namely: that the ruling (ḥukm) is not attained through it except by the intermediary of the efficient cause, just as arrival is not attained by the road except through the intermediary of the efficient cause. Except that the traveling is not produced by the road, whereas the efficient cause here is produced by the "cause." And this genus...

chapters.arabic_text:
من السبب له حكم المباشرة من كل وجه: في إيجاب الحكم؛ فلا ينبغي أن تشتبه
المباشرة بالسبب، بهذا الإطلاق.
الوجه الثاني: تسميتهم ذات العلة -مع تخلف الصفة عنها- سببا: كتسميتهم
اليمين سببا للكفارة، وتسمية ملك النصاب سببا، دون الحنث وانقضاء الحول.
ووجه الاستعارة: أن الحكم غير حاصل بمجرده، كما لا يحصل الوصول، [والماء]
بمجرد الطريق والحبل. وهذا الجنس قد استقصيناه. وبينا أن نقصان  الصفات
التابعة، قد يفارق [نقصان] أبعاض ذات العلة في بعض الأحكام؛ كما سبق.
الوجه الرابع: تسميتهم العلة الموجبة سببا، كتسمية علل الغرامات
والعقوبات والكفارات: أسبابا. وتسمية البيع: سببا للملك إلى غير ذلك. فهذا
أبعد الوجوه في الاستعارة عن وضع اللسان؛ لأن المقصود مضاف إلى العلة، ولا
يضاف إلى السبب في الوضع. ولكن وجه الاستعارة: أن العلل الشرعية في معنى
الشروط والأمارات من [كل] وجه؛ لأنها لا توجب الأحكام بذواتها، بل يجب
الحكم عندها بإيجاب الله تعالى. فمن PageV01P592 # هذا الوجه [حسنت] الاستعارة.
فهذه مدراك مختلفة لمعنى السبب. فإذا أطلق الفقيه لفظ السبب، فإن فهم
بالقرينة مقصوده [78 - ب]-كمعارضته إياه بالمباشرة- فذاك. وإن لم يفهم:
فلابد من الاستفصال: إذا كان الغرض يختلف باختلاف الوجوه التي ذكرناها.
فإن قيل: السبب المذكور في مقابلة المباشرة، هل يناط القصاص بمثله وهو
الشرط المحض؟
قلنا: نعم: فإن القصاص عندنا يجب على شهود القصاص؛ والهلاك حصل بفعل
مختار من الولي أو القاضي؛ والصادر من الشاهد تمكين يجري مجرى الشرط.
ولكن: لما رأى الشافعي -رضي الله عنه- إيجاب القصاص على المكره، ورأى
الإكراه سببا في مقابلة مباشرة المكره- قاس الشهادة به.
وأبو حنيفة -رضي الله عنه- لا يوجب القصاص إلا بالمباشرة؛ [وتخيل: أن
المكره مباشر]، والمكره آلة.
فمنشأ النظر بيان أن الإكراه مباشرة أو تسبب.
فأبو حنيفة -رضي الله عنه- يقول: المباشرة عبارة عن إيجاد علة القتل،
[وإيجاد] علة العلة. والإكراه علة فعل المكره. ويزعم: أن PageV01P593 # فعل المكره حصل به، فإلجاؤه يحدث داعية القتل في نفسه؛ وتلك الداعية تحدث
الفعل [فكان القتل متولدا] من إكراه المكره، بواسطة داعية تولدت من
الإكراه.
والشافعي رضي الله عنه يقول: لو كان كذلك لما أثم المكره؛ فإثمه يدل على
بقاء اختياره حسا وشرعا، وفيه إخراج الإكراه عن كونه علة.
نعم: فيه مشابهة العلة من حيث أنه يثير داعية على الجملة، وإن كانت تلك
الداعية مقرونة بخيرة يتسع معها مخالفة الداعية. فكذلك في الشهادة معنى
العلة، على معنى: أنها تثير داعية في نفس القاضي من جهة الشرع؛ وتلك
الداعية تفضي إلى الهلاك بواسطة الفعل؛ فكانت في معناه؛ ولهذا كان الكلام
في طرف الرجم أظهر منه في طرف القصاص: لأن اختيار الولي ظاهر في إحالة
الهلاك عليه، وتلك الداعية لا تحدث بالشهادة. لكن يقرر ذلك بطريق آخر، وهو:
أن بطلان العصمة PageV01P594 # وحصول الإهدار [حصل] بالشهادة، وكان ذلك هلاكا حكيما، فإذا اتصل بالهلاك
الحسي: [تم، ووجب] القصاص على الشاهد: لأنه تعاطى سبب الهلاك الحكمي
المقترن بالهلاك الحسي المفضي إليه. فهذا وجه النظر في تلك المسئلة.
فإن قيل: بأي تأويل سميتم تعليق الطلاق سببا، حتى شرطتم اقتران النكاح به
للانعقاد، ومنعتم التعليق على الملك، وأبو حنيفة -رضي الله عنه- ينكر كونه
سببا؛ ويزعم: أنه يمين في الحال؛ وينقطع حكم اليمين بوجود الحنث: فلا يكون
سببا [لما يرتفع به]، فإن السبب هو الطريق إلى المقصد، فأما ما ينعدم
بالاتصال بالمقصد فلا يكون سببا؟
قلنا: تسميته سببا بمعنى العلة: التي فقدت [صفة] الإضافة إلى محل، أو
فقدت الشرط على اصطلاح الفقهاء. فإن الفراق يقع -عند وجود الصفة- بالطلاق
السابق، لا بالصفة الحادثة. وظهر أثر ذلك في PageV01P595 # الشهود: إذا رجعوا في قضية الغرم. فإذا حصل الفراق عند الدخول، كان مضافا
إلى الكلام السابق [لا] إلى الدخول: فهو العلة. فلذلك شرط اقتران شرط
الطلاق به، وهو ملك النكاح.
فإن قيل: إنما يصير كلامه علة للفراق عند الدخول؛ وقبله يمين وليس بعلة
للفراق.
قلنا: إذا وجد الدخول واللفظ، وحصل الفراق؛ فهو مضاف إلى اللفظ لا إلى
الدخول، فهذا هو المراد بكونه سببا وعلة. أما قولهم: إنه قبل الدخول ليس
بعلة، فإن عنوا به: أنه ليس بموجب للفراق في الحال، فمسلم. وذلك: لنقصان
وصف الإضافة الحاصل من الاقتران بالشرط. وأن عنوا [به]: أن ذات العلة
وركنها وما يضاف [إليه الحكم] عند حصوله غير موجود -[فهو باطل. فإن الزنا
يسمى علة وسببا على ما سبق وجهه؛ وهو غير موجب] بمجرده دون وصف الإضافة إلى
المحصن؛ ولكن عند حصول الوصف يضاف إلى الزنا، لا إلى وصف PageV01P596 # الإضافة. [فهذا -على منهاج] كلام  الفقهاء- واضح.
فإن قيل: فإن سلم كونه سببا وعلة بهذا التأويل، فلم يشترط أن يقترن به
ملك النكاح، وملك النكاح يراد لاتصال الطلاق بالمحل، وهو لا يتصل به قبل
الشرط، والمحل مهيأ للطلاق عند وجود الشرط. وليس يشترط في حال التكلم إلا
أهلية العاقد لصدور السبب منه؛ فكما لا تشترط صفات المتكلم عند وجود الصفة
والشرط، [حتى وقع] وإن كان الزوج مجنونا عند الدخول -فكذلك صفة المحل: لا
تشترط عند صدور السبب من العاقد؟
قلنا: من سلم كونه علة وسببا كما ذكرناه، لزمه أن يعترف بمذهبنا؛ إذ صفات
المحل يشترط وجودها حالة وجود السبب، وإن كان السبب في الحال لا يتصل
بالمحل ولا يتنجز حكمه. فإذا قال الرجل لأجنبية: تزوجتك على ألف، وطلقتك
على مائة؛ فقالت المرأة: زوجت نفسي، PageV01P597 # وقبلت الطلاق- لم يقع الطلاق عندهم، لأن الإيجاب تقدم [حكمه] على النكاح؛
والإيجاب لا يتصل حكمه بالمحل إلا بعد وجود القبول؛ فهي منكوحة بعيد القبول ومعه.
وكذلك قال الشافعي [79 - أ]-رحمه الله-: لو قال لعبده: كاتبتك على ألف،
وبعتك الثوب بدينار؛ فقال العبد: قبلت الكتابة، واشتريت الثوب -لم يصح شراء
الثوب. وقد كان الموجب أهلا للإيجاب حالة الإيجاب، والعبد كان أهلا للشراء
حالة القبول؛ ولكن: لما لم يقترن شرط أهلية القابل بحالة الإيجاب، لم ينعقد
سببا. فدل [على] أن مأخذهم ما سبق: من أن التعليق في الحال يمين، وليس بعلة
للفراق ولا سبب له. وقد بينا وجهه.
وأما قولهم: أن السبب ما يتقرر عند الوصول إلى المقصد، واليمين يرتفع
بوجود الصفة.
PageV01P598
قلنا: هو -من حيث كان يمينا- ليس موجبا للفراق. ومن حيث كان موجبا
للفراق، يتقرر عند الدخول، ويتنجز الفراق، [ولا يرتفع كالتطليق] الناجز؛
فإنه [سبب] يستعقب الفراق، ويكون ذلك تقررا في حقه لا ارتفاعا. وإنما سمي
يمينا: من حيث أنه بالعادة يمنع من الفعل، وهو من هذا الوجه ليس بسبب
للفراق.
وكذلك اليمين: سبب للكفارة [والمنع الشرعي]؛ ولا نقول: ارتفع بالحنث [بل
تقرر]؛ فإن اليمين الكاذبة موجبة للكفارة، وقد تحقق الوجوب واستقر. وإنما
[المرتفع] المنع الطبيعي: من حيث محاذرته لزوم الكفارة. والمنع الشرعي لا
نقول: ارتفع، بل اليمين لم تقتض المنع إلا [في] مرة واحدة، فتقرر موجبها:
أن سلم كون اليمين موجبا للمنع.
هذا ما أردنا أن نهذب به مقاصد الفقهاء من إطلاق لفظ السبب والعلة
والشرط، ووجه إضافة الأحكام إليها تحقيقا وتمثيلا [والله أعلم].
PageV01P599

- Root: س-ب-ب (s-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A rope, cord, or tether by which one reaches water (as in drawing from a well); hence, any means, path, or connection leading to an end.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological-legal usage, the "cause" (sabab) is that which is not itself productive of the effect by its essence, but rather a sign (amārah) or condition (sharṭ) upon which the Lawgiver attaches the ruling — thus it is a "way" (ṭarīq) to the divine command, not an efficient agent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, the rope (ḥabl) for drawing water; metaphorically (majāz), any means to an end. The literal sense implies direct connection; the metaphorical sense extends to indirect, conditional, or sign-like relations — the key distinction being whether the effect is attributed to the thing itself or to something else.
- Root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — for mubāsharah (direct contact/agency)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Touching skin-to-skin, direct bodily contact; hence, acting upon something immediately without intermediary.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Direct causation where the agent's act terminates upon the effect without an intervening cause; in legal theory, the one who directly performs the act (mubāshir) versus one who merely provides the means (mutasabbib).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical touch; metaphorical — direct causal efficacy. The jurists' contrast between mubāsharah and sabab hinges on this: direct agency is to the act as the rope is to the water — but the rope does not touch the water directly.
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l) — for ʿillah (cause/ratio legis)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To give a second drink to a camel; hence, a "reason" that follows upon and explains something — the underlying rationale that sustains a ruling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ʿillah is that which necessitates the ruling by its very meaning (maʿnā), whether through divine ordination or rational necessity; it is the effective cause (muʾaththir) in contrast to the mere sabab.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the second watering; metaphorical — the underlying reason that "follows" the effect and explains it. The jurists' usage blurs the line between ʿillah and sabab, but the rhetorical distinction remains: the ʿillah is that to which the ruling is properly attributed, while the sabab is merely the occasion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-ḥukm ʿalā al-sharṭ (Conditional Suspension of the Ruling) — In Arabic syntax, when a ruling is suspended upon a condition (sharṭ), the conditional particle (in/idhā) does not make the condition the agent of the ruling; rather, the ruling is attributed to the original speech act (the protasis), while the condition merely specifies the time or circumstance of its actualization. This parallels the legal distinction between the cause (which bears the ruling) and the condition (which merely activates it).
chapters.translation:
I say: The cause (sabab) has the ruling of direct agency (mubāsharah) in every respect — namely, in necessitating the legal ruling. Thus, direct agency and causation should not be conflated in this unrestricted sense.

The second sense: Their calling the essence of the cause (dhāt al-ʿillah) — even when its attribute is absent — a "cause" (sabab): as when they call the oath (yamīn) a cause for the expiation (kaffārah), and call ownership of the nisāb (minimum taxable amount) a cause, even without the occurrence of the violation (ḥanath) or the completion of the year (ḥawl). The metaphorical basis (wajh al-istiʿārah) is that the ruling is not obtained by the cause alone, just as reaching [the water] is not obtained by the mere road and rope [without the act of drawing]. This genus we have already exhausted, and we have shown that the deficiency of dependent attributes may differ from the deficiency of the parts of the cause's essence in certain rulings, as previously established.

The fourth sense: Their calling the necessitating cause (al-ʿillah al-mūjibah) a "cause" (sabab) — as when they call the causes of financial penalties (gharāmāt), punishments (ʿuqūbāt), and expiations (kaffārāt) "causes" (asbāb); and their calling the sale (bayʿ) a cause for ownership, and so forth. This is the most remote of the senses in metaphorical extension from the linguistic convention (waḍʿ al-lisān), because the intended effect is attributed to the ʿillah, not to the sabab, in the original linguistic usage. But the metaphorical basis is that the legal causes (al-ʿilal al-sharʿiyyah) are, in every respect, in the meaning of conditions (shurūṭ) and signs (amārāt) — for they do not necessitate the rulings by their own essences; rather, the ruling becomes obligatory at their occurrence by the command of God Most High. So from this perspective, the metaphorical extension is fitting.

These, then, are the various points of reference (madārik) for the meaning of "cause" (sabab). So when the jurist utters the word "cause," if his intent is understood through contextual indication (qarīnah) — such as his contrasting it with direct agency — then that suffices. But if it is not understood, then one must seek clarification (istifṣāl), for the purpose varies according to the different senses we have mentioned.

If it is said: "The cause mentioned in contrast to direct agency — is retaliation (qiṣāṣ) attached to something like it, namely, a mere condition (sharṭ maḥḍ)?"

We say: Yes. For retaliation, in our view, is obligatory upon the witnesses of retaliation (shuhūd al-qiṣāṣ); and the destruction [of the victim] occurred through a voluntary act of the guardian (walī) or the judge; and what issued from the witness is a mere enabling (tamkīn) that runs in the course of a condition. But when al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — saw the obligation of retaliation upon the one who compels (mukrih), and saw that compulsion (ikrāh) is a cause in contrast to the direct agency of the compelled person, he analogized testimony (shahādah) to it.

Abū Ḥanīfah — may God be pleased with him — does not obligate retaliation except through direct agency; and he imagined that the compeller is a direct agent, and the compelled person is merely an instrument (ālah).

So the origin of the inquiry is to clarify whether compulsion is direct agency or causation (tasabbub).

Abū Ḥanīfah — may God be pleased with him — says: "Direct agency (mubāsharah) is the expression for the bringing into existence of the cause of killing, and the bringing into existence of the cause of the cause. Compulsion is the cause of the compelled person's act." And he claims that the act of the compelled person occurred through it — for the compulsion generates in him the motive (dāʿiyah) for killing, and that motive generates the act. Thus the killing is generated (mutawallid) from the compeller's compulsion, through the intermediary of a motive that was generated from the compulsion.

Al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — says: "If it were so, the compelled person would not be sinful. For his sinfulness indicates the persistence of his choice (ikhtiyār) both sensibly and legally, and this removes compulsion from being a cause."

Indeed, there is in it a resemblance to the cause (mushābahat al-ʿillah) in that it stirs a motive in a general sense — even if that motive is coupled with a choice (khīrah) within which opposing the motive remains possible. Likewise, in testimony there is the meaning of cause, in the sense that it stirs a motive in the soul of the judge from the direction of the Law; and that motive leads to destruction through the intermediary of the act. So it is in its meaning. For this reason, the discussion on the side of stoning (rajm) is more evident than on the side of retaliation (qiṣāṣ) — because the guardian's choice is manifest in attributing the destruction to him, and that motive is not generated by the testimony. But this can be established by another path, namely: that the nullification of inviolability (buṭlān al-ʿiṣmah) and the occurrence of the forfeiture (īhādār) occurred through the testimony, and that was a "legal destruction" (halāk ḥukmī). So when it is connected to the physical destruction (al-halāk al-ḥissī), it is completed, and retaliation becomes obligatory upon the witness — because he undertook the cause of the legal destruction that is conjoined with the physical destruction that leads to it. This, then, is the aspect of inquiry in this question.

If it is said: "By what interpretation have you called the suspension of divorce (taʿlīq al-ṭalāq) a 'cause' (sabab), such that you required the conjunction of marriage (nikāḥ) with it for its validity, and you prevented suspension upon mere ownership (milk)? Yet Abū Ḥanīfah — may God be pleased with him — denies that it is a cause, and claims that it is an oath (yamīn) at the present moment, and the ruling of the oath is terminated by the occurrence of the violation (ḥanath) — so it cannot be a cause for that which terminates it. For the cause is the path to the intended end; but that which is annihilated upon connection with the intended end cannot be a cause."

We say: Its being called a "cause" is in the sense of the ʿillah that has lost the attribute of attribution (ṣifat al-iḍāfah) to a locus (maḥall), or has lost its condition, according to the convention of the jurists. For the separation (furqah) occurs — at the existence of the attribute — through the prior divorce utterance, not through the newly occurring attribute. The effect of this appeared in the case of the witnesses when they retracted in a matter of financial liability (ghurm). So when the separation occurs at the time of consummation (dukhūl), it is attributed to the prior speech, not to the consummation — so it is the ʿillah. For this reason, the conjunction of the condition of divorce with it was required, namely, ownership of the marriage bond (milk al-nikāḥ).

If it is said: "His speech only becomes a cause for separation at the time of consummation; before that it is an oath, not a cause for separation."

We say: When consummation and the utterance both exist, and separation occurs, it is attributed to the utterance, not to the consummation. This is what is meant by its being a cause (sabab) and an ʿillah. As for their saying that before consummation it is not a cause — if they mean that it does not necessitate separation at the present moment, this is conceded. That is due to the deficiency of the attribute of attribution that results from its not being conjoined with the condition. But if they mean that the essence of the cause (dhāt al-ʿillah) and its pillar (rukn), and that to which the ruling is attributed upon its occurrence, do not exist — this is false. For adultery (zinā) is called a cause and a reason (sabab) according to what we have previously explained, and it does not necessitate [the penalty] by itself without the attribute of attribution to the married state (iḥṣān); but upon the occurrence of the attribute, [the penalty] is attributed to the adultery, not to the attribute of attribution. This — upon the methodology of the jurists' discourse — is clear.

If it is said: "Granting that it is a cause and an ʿillah by this interpretation, why did you require that ownership of the marriage bond be conjoined with it? For ownership of the marriage bond is intended for the connection of the divorce to the locus (maḥall), and it does not connect to it before the condition; and the locus is prepared for divorce upon the existence of the condition. But at the moment of speaking, only the capacity (ahliyyah) of the contracting party for issuing the cause is required — just as the attributes of the speaker are not required at the existence of the attribute and condition (so that [the divorce] occurs even if the husband is insane at the time of consummation) — so likewise, the attribute of the locus: why is it not required at the time the cause issues from the contracting party?"

We say: Whoever concedes that it is an ʿillah and a cause as we have described must acknowledge our doctrine. For the attributes of the locus are required to exist at the moment of the existence of the cause, even if the cause at that moment does not connect to the locus nor does its ruling become effective. So if a man says to a foreign woman: "I have married you for a thousand, and I have divorced you for a hundred," and the woman says: "I have married myself and I accept the divorce" — the divorce does not occur in their view, because the offer (ījāb) preceded its ruling upon the marriage; and the offer's ruling does not connect to the locus except after the existence of acceptance (qabūl). So she is a wife immediately after acceptance and with it.

Likewise, al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said: If a man says to his slave: "I have made a kitābah (manumission contract) with you for a thousand, and I have sold you the garment for a dinar," and the slave says: "I accept the kitābah, and I have purchased the garment" — the purchase of the garment is not valid. For the offeror was qualified to make the offer at the moment of the offer, and the slave was qualified to purchase at the moment of acceptance. But since the condition of the acceptor's capacity was not conjoined with the moment of the offer, it did not contract as a cause. This indicates that their principle is what preceded: that the suspension (taʿlīq) at the present moment is an oath, not a cause for separation nor a reason for it. And we have already explained its basis.

As for their saying that the cause is that which is established (yataqarrar) upon reaching the intended end, while the oath is terminated by the existence of the attribute:

We say: It — insofar as it is an oath — does not necessitate separation. But insofar as it necessitates separation, it is established at the time of consummation, and the separation becomes effective, and it is not terminated — like the immediate divorce (al-ṭalāq al-nājiz). For it is a cause that brings about separation as its consequence, and that is an establishment (taqarrur) in its regard, not a termination. It is only called an "oath" insofar as it habitually prevents the act, and from this aspect it is not a cause for separation.

Likewise, the oath is a cause for the expiation and for the legal prohibition (al-manʿ al-sharʿī). And we do not say that it is terminated by the violation; rather, it is established. For the false oath necessitates the expiation, and the obligation has been realized and settled. What is terminated is only the natural prohibition (al-manʿ al-ṭabīʿī), insofar as one fears the liability of the expiation. As for the legal prohibition, we do not say it is terminated; rather, the oath did not require the prohibition except once, so its necessitation was established — granting that the oath is a necessitator of prohibition.

This is what we intended to refine regarding the jurists' purposes in their unrestricted use of the terms "cause" (sabab), "ratio" (ʿillah), and "condition" (sharṭ), and the manner of attributing rulings to them, both in verification (taḥqīq) and by way of example (tamthīl). And God knows best.

### || CHECK مسألة: لا تثبت بالقياس الشرعي القضايا العقلية واللغوية

### || AUTO القول في بيان ركن الحكم من أركان القياس وهو الركن الثالث

يجوز أن يثبت بالقياس كل حكم شرعي، لم يتعبد فيه بالعلم. ويتبين هذا
بالضبط بالنظر في المسائل:
مسئلة: لا يجوز أن يثبت بالقياس الشرعي القضايا العقلية واللغوية، لأن
القياس دليل شرعي: فلا يدل إلا على قضية شرعية.
ويخرج عليه: [أن] تسمية النبيذ خمرا بالقياس، لا وجه له: لأنه أمر لغوي،
فيعرف من وضع اللغة. وإذا لم ينقل الاسم، ولا نقل من أهل اللغة تجويز
[الإثبات] للأسامي بالقياس -لم يكن الاسم لغويا؛ والأسامي اللغوية أعلام
للمسميات: فلا وجه للتعرف فيها بالقياس.
PageV01P600
نعم: الطريق أن نسلم أنه لا يسمى خمرا؛ ولكن الخمر محرمة لعلة الإسكار،
فتحريم غير الخمر كما حرم الربا في غير البر: لمشاركته البر في معنى الطعم،
وإن لم يشاركه في الاسم. وكذلك: إثبات اسم الزنا للواط، واسم السرقة
للنباش، واسم اليمين لليمين الغموس، [بالقياس]-لا وجه له: فإن هذه أمور لغوية.
فإن سلمنا اتباع الأحكام هذه الأسامي، وجب إثبات الأسامي بالنقل؛ كما روى
أنه -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: "إذا أتى الرجل الرجل فهما زانيان"، وأمثال
ذلك. أو نزعم: أن الأحكام غير منوطة بهذه الأسامي، وإنما هي منوطة بمعان
تتضمنها. فمناط الحكم من الزنا: تضييع الماء بالجماع المشتهي المحرم؛
ومناطه من السرقة: أخذ المال المحترم من الحرز؛ إلى أمثال لذلك:
وكذلك النظر في أن الطلاق هل يحتمل العتاق [أم لا]؟ وأن قوله: أنت طالق
هل يحتمل العدد [أم لا]؟ إلى أمثال هذه المسائل.
[فأمثال هذه المسائل] إنما تتعرف من البحث عن وضع اللغة: بطريق الاستعارة
والكناية؛ فالقياس في  هذه المسائل باطل.
PageV01P601

### || CHECK مسألة: ما تعبدنا فيه بالعلم لا تثبت بالقياس

وكذلك القضايا العقلية: كالقتل مثلا، وأن المكره متسبب أو مباشر، وأن كل
واحد من الشركاء قاتل أم لا. فهذا يعرف بتعرف حد القتل، وهو أمر عقلي: لا
يعرف بالقياس الشرعي.
نعم: يجوز أن يثبت [الشرع لفعل] ليس قتلا تحقيقا، حكم القتل، فيعبر عنه:
بأنه قتل شرعا، أي هو قائم مقام القتل: في إفادة الحكم.
مسئلة: ما تعبدنا فيه بالعلم لا يثبت بالقياس؛ [لأن القياس] لا يفيد إلا
ظنا، ولا يثمر العلم.
ويخرج مخرجون على هذا الأصل: أنا إنما لم نثبت صلاة سادسة [القياس، لهذا
الأصل. وهذا فيه نظر؛ فإن تقرير الوجوب بالظن ممكن كما في الوتر؛ وإنما لم
نوجب صلاة سادسة] [لا] لأنه [لا] قياس يدل عليه، [بل: لا] نعقاد الإجماع
على الانحصار، ولأنه
PageV01P602

### || CHECK مسألة: الحكم الثابت من جهة الشرع نوعان: نصب الأسباب عللا للأحكام، وإثبات الأحكام ابتداء

لو كانت واجبة: لتواتر [نقل] فعلها، كما تواتر [في] سائر الصلوات؛ [فعدم]
التواتر -في ممحل وجوب التواتر عرفا- يفيد العلم بالانتفاء؛ فلا يستعمل
القياس على ضد المعلوم. فإن أراد هذا التصرف بما ذكره ما أشرنا إليه، فلا
نعترض عليه.
مسئلة: الحكم الثابت من جهة الشرع، نوعان:
أحدهما: نصب الأسباب [عللا] للأحكام؛ كجعل الزنا موجبا للحد، وجعل الجماع
موجبا للكفارة، وجعل السرقة موجبة للقطع. إلى غير ذلك: من الأسباب التي عقل
[من] الشرع نصبها عللا للأحكام.
والنوع الثاني: إثبات الأحكام ابتداء من غير ربط بالسبب.
وكل واحد -من النوعين- قابل للتعليل والتعدية مهما ظهرت العلة المتعدية.
فيجوز أن يقال: الجماع إنما نصب سببا لعلة كذا، فينضب [الأكل] سببا لوجود
العلة. والزنا إنما نصب سببا للرجم لكذا، فاللواط ينصب سببا لوجود تلك
العلة؛ وإن لم يكن اللواط زنا [79 - ب]
PageV01P603
